name: Aalto Sans
classification_notes: Modular humanist sans-serif with a neutral, clean construction and gently friendly curves. Corporate orientation throughout. Three subfamilies (Pro, Essential, Essential Alt) each in 8 weights with matching italics. The Pro subfamily extends to Latin Extended and adds a full OpenType feature set including small caps, stylistic alternates, case-sensitive forms and tabular figures. Alfonso García contributed digital editing and the italic designs.
summary: A modular humanist sans-serif in 49 styles across three subfamilies, built for corporate identity and branding work.
description: Aalto Sans is a neutral humanist sans-serif in 8 weights with matching italics, structured across three subfamilies: Pro, Essential and Essential Alt. The Pro version covers Latin Extended and includes small caps, stylistic alternates, case-sensitive forms, tabular figures and currency symbols. At 49 styles in total, it handles most corporate and branding applications without fuss.
foundry_blurb: A modular humanist-flavoured sans-serif designed for corporate use and brand identity. The family is neutral and clean with friendly, modern design characteristics, and performs well for mid-length text. The Pro version adds Latin Extended coverage and OpenType features including small caps and stylistic alternates.

name: Abstract
classification_notes: Contemporary serif with eclectic influences across seven weights. True italics are drawn with their own distinct character rather than a mechanical slant. Includes alternates, lining and old style figures, numerators and denominators, and Cyrillic support across all 14 styles.
summary: A seven-weight contemporary serif with purpose-drawn italics, alternates, multiple figure styles and Cyrillic support across all 14 styles.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara and Rodrigo Fuenzalida at Latinotype in 2020, Abstract spans Thin to Black, each weight paired with a true italic drawn to carry its own personality. The family includes alternates, lining and old style figures, and numerators and denominators for detailed typographic setting. Cyrillic support across all 14 styles gives it genuine range beyond Latin scripts.
foundry_blurb: Abstract is a contemporary, eclectic serif inspired by modern life, developed during 2020. A true italic with its own distinct character accompanies each weight, and the family includes alternates, multiple figure styles and Cyrillic support.

name: Abstract One
classification_notes: Contemporary serif with an eclectic character; true italics with their own personality distinct from the roman; alternates, lining and old-style figures, numerators and denominators, and Cyrillic support. No condensed or mono variants.
summary: A 14-style contemporary serif by Luciano Vergara with expressive italics, alternates, dual figure sets, and Latin–Cyrillic coverage.
description: Abstract One is a contemporary serif designed by Luciano Vergara with an eclectic sensibility suited to editorial and text work. Seven weights each carry a matching italic drawn with its own character, while alternates and both lining and old-style figures give it typographic flexibility. Cyrillic support extends its reach across Latin and Slavic scripts.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary, eclectic serif inspired by modern life and designed during the pandemic. The family offers 14 styles across seven weights, with a true italic that carries its own personality, alternates, lining and old-style figures, numerators and denominators, and Cyrillic support.

name: Acaraje
classification_notes: Contemporary grotesque with progressive stroke modulation that grows more pronounced across heavier weights; the lighter end reads as clean and neutral while the heavier weights take on a warmly expressive quality, all within a classically grounded grotesque structure.
summary: Sofia Mohr's grotesque for Latinotype uses progressive stroke modulation that builds from restrained at Light to noticeably warm at Black, giving a classically structured sans a personality that most neutral grotesques lack.
description: Released by Latinotype in 2023, Acaraje is Sofia Mohr's grotesque in which lighter settings read as clean and disciplined while heavier weights develop real character through increasingly pronounced modulation. Fourteen styles span seven weights with italics throughout, making the family workable across text and display roles. A variable version followed in 2024, extending its range further.
foundry_blurb: Acarajé is a grotesque whose versatility comes from modulation – personality grows with the weights, producing a jovial face that retains the qualities of classic grotesque construction throughout its range.

name: Acarajé Variable
classification_notes: Grotesque sans-serif with an unusual design trait: stroke modulation that becomes more pronounced at heavier weights, lending warmth uncommon in the genre. Variable weight axis spans Light to Black with a full italic companion family.
summary: A grotesque sans-serif whose stroke modulation builds with weight, giving it a warmth and character that most grotesques deliberately withhold.
description: Designed by Sofia Mohr and released through Latinotype in 2024, Acarajé Variable is a grotesque with an unusual design decision at its core: stroke modulation that intensifies as weight increases. This lifts it away from the neutral end of the grotesque spectrum, sitting somewhere between the rigour of classical grotesques and the approachability of humanist sans-serifs. The variable format covers Light to Black, with a seven-weight italic family and support for alternates and small caps.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Acarajé as a grotesque with a particular modulation that grows with weight, maintaining a jovial character while preserving the defining traits of more classical grotesques. The variable version adapts freely from legible body text at lighter weights to expressive, characterful headlines at maximum weight, with alternative glyphs available to extend the system.

name: Aestetico
classification_notes: Contemporary grotesque drawing on classic sans-serif conventions. Structured as three sister families — standard, Formal and Informal — each sharing the same weight range but diverging in letterform character: the Informal is rounder and more expressive, the Formal holds to traditional grotesque geometry, and the standard sits between them.
designer: Daniel Hernández, Luciano Vergara, Alfonso García
summary: A 54-style grotesque from Latinotype split across three stylistic variants — standard, Formal and Informal — giving a single type system distinct tonal registers from expressive to traditional.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández, Luciano Vergara and Alfonso García, Aestetico spans three sister families each carrying nine weights with matching italics. The Informal cuts lean rounder and more expressive; the Formal holds closer to conventional grotesque geometry. With 395 glyphs and support for over 200 languages, it covers broad editorial and branding territory without asking users to switch families.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Aestetico as an exploration of how subtle shifts in letter shapes and curves alter a typeface's character. Three sister families — Aestetico, Aestetico Formal and Aestetico Informal — each pay tribute to classic sans-serif traditions while steering in different directions, with the Informal designed as rounder and quirkier and the Formal adhering to traditional sans-serif structure. Together the 54 styles are pitched at editorial, branding, advertising and digital applications.

name: Alecrim
classification_notes: Contemporary grotesque referencing 20th-century classics — Helvetica, Frutiger and Franklin Gothic — without directly copying them. Low contrast, firm strokes, generous x-height, taut curves and closed terminals. Designed to perform across both small text and display sizes.
summary: A composed contemporary grotesque from Sofia Mohr, drawing on mid-century classics to produce a neutral, durable workhorse with 10 weights, full italics and a variable axis.
description: Alecrim sits in the geometric grotesque tradition, referencing Helvetica and Frutiger without mimicking them. Firm strokes, a generous x-height, taut curves and closed terminals give it a legible composure that holds across small text and large headlines alike. Ten weights, full italics and a variable font make it a practical choice for identity and editorial systems that need longevity over novelty.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype designed Alecrim to resist trend cycles. A sober grotesque rhythm built on precise construction, generous x-height and low contrast, it covers visual identity, editorial and typographic systems where clarity and durability are the brief. The family spans 10 weights from Ultra Thin to Heavy, each with an italic, plus a variable font — 21 styles in total.

name: Amarela Stencil
classification_notes: High-contrast serif with stencil apertures throughout; extreme thick-thin stroke contrast creates a graphic, textured presence. Open counters from stencil cuts reinforce the display-only character. Not suitable for text sizes.
summary: A high-contrast stencil serif by Sofia Mohr, spanning five weights plus two decorative variants and built for titles, packaging and branding.
description: Amarela Stencil pairs sharp serifs with extreme stroke contrast and open stencil apertures, giving it a bold graphic presence in display settings. The family runs from Ultra Light to Black with two additional decorative style variants, providing enough range to carry varied branding work. OpenType alternates and coverage for over 200 languages are included throughout.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary typeface built for titles, packaging and branding, with sharp serifs and extreme stroke contrast delivering a strong, distinctive character. The family spans five weights and two decorative styles, with a standard character set supporting over 200 languages and OpenType features included.

name: Amarga
classification_notes: High-contrast serif with pointed terminals and Didone-influenced contrast ratios. Built for display use but weight range extends to text-weight Thin and ExtraLight. Nine weights plus matching italics give it practical range.
summary: A high-contrast display serif by Sofia Mohr with pointed terminals and nine weights, built around the visual tension of coffee's bitter intensity.
description: Amarga is a serif typeface designed by Sofia Mohr and released through Latinotype in 2022. Its defining features are high stroke contrast and sharply pointed terminals, which give it a strong visual presence suited to editorial layouts, posters and brand identities. The family covers nine weights from Thin to Black, each with an italic, making it a useful display workhorse across a range of contexts.
foundry_blurb: Amarga takes its name and spirit from the bitter taste of coffee. The design is a serif with high contrast and pointed terminals, available in nine weights – Thin through Black – plus italics, totalling 18 fonts. Strong visual impact makes it a natural choice for editorial, branding, posters and web display work.

name: Amigável
classification_notes: Contemporary geometric sans-serif with low stroke contrast, generous x-height and open counters optimised for small-size legibility. Geometric construction with softened joints and a humanist gesture. Includes stylistic alternates for single-storey and double-storey forms of a and g.
summary: A geometric sans from Sofia Mohr that pairs strict circular construction with softened joints and a generous x-height, offered in seven weights with matching italics and a full variable font.
description: Built on geometric bones with low stroke contrast and open counters, Amigável holds up cleanly from small interface sizes to display scale. Stylistic alternates let designers switch between single-storey and double-storey forms of a and g within the same weight, giving the typeface some flexibility of tone. It suits interface design, editorial work and branding that wants structure without stiffness.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype is a Chilean type foundry founded in 2008, with over 300 families in its catalogue spanning branding, advertising and digital design. The studio works with clients including Zoom and Ogilvy and offers custom type services alongside its retail library.

name: Amostra
classification_notes: Rounded organic sans-serif where contrast increases across the weight range – thin cuts are relatively low-contrast, heavy cuts are markedly high-contrast. Distinctive droplet-shaped terminals give letterforms a semi-calligraphic quality. Falls between humanist and display sans in character; not a strict geometric or grotesque.
summary: An organic sans-serif by Sofia Mohr with distinctive droplet terminals and contrast that builds across nine weights, suited to branding and editorial work.
description: Amostra's central design idea is that contrast grows with weight – the Thin sits fairly even-stroked while the Heavy becomes markedly high-contrast, so each end of the range has a different personality. Droplet-shaped terminals lend the letterforms a calligraphic edge without tipping into script. Eighteen styles with full italic coverage, plus a generous OpenType feature set including swash, contextual alternates, ornaments and titling variants, make it a capable choice for identity, packaging and editorial applications.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Amostra as a new organic sans-serif – unique, daring and highly contrasted – built for contemporary design demands. Its droplet endings and weight-driven contrast variation create strong typographic hierarchy across branding, packaging and editorial projects.

name: Andes
classification_notes: Neo-humanist sans-serif positioned as a display typeface. Mixed terminal styles draw from both humanist and rational traditions, giving it what the foundry describes as the look of "mixed typography". Full weight range from Ultra Light to Black with matching italics makes it more versatile than a strictly decorative display face.
summary: A neo-humanist display sans in ten weights with matching italics, a condensed sibling, and alternate italic glyphs that add character in editorial settings.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández and released in 2011, Andes sits between a display face and a workhorse sans. Its mixed terminal styles draw from both humanist and rational traditions, making it usable across retail, magazine, logotype and book contexts. The italic includes alternate glyphs for a, g, y and z – adding distinctiveness where emphasis is needed.
foundry_blurb: A display typeface with neo-humanist characteristics, whose distinctive terminals give it the feel of mixed typography. The family spans ten upright weights and ten italics sharing a consistent x-height, with a condensed version available alongside a Rounded variant. The italic contains additional alternate glyphs for select letters to help emphasise key words or phrases.

name: Andes Condensed
classification_notes: Neo-humanist display sans-serif in condensed form. Varied terminal treatments across the family produce a subtle mixed-typography quality. Ten weights from UltraLight to Black, each with a matching italic, plus alternate italic glyphs for a, y, z and g. Part of the broader Andes system alongside a regular-width family and Andes Rounded.
summary: A condensed display sans-serif from Latinotype with neo-humanist character, spanning ten weights from UltraLight to Black with matching italics.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández and published by Latinotype in 2012, Andes Condensed brings a neo-humanist sensibility to condensed type. Varied terminal treatments across the family give it a slightly mixed-typography feel, while consistent x-heights across all weights keep settings coherent at any size. A practical choice for retail branding, magazine headlines and logotype work.
foundry_blurb: Andes is a display typeface with neo-humanist characteristics. Its varied terminals and other design details give it the appearance of mixed typography. The family spans ten upright weights from UltraLight to Black, each paired with an italic, and includes alternate italic glyphs for the letters a, y, z and g to help emphasise specific text.

name: Andes Italic
classification_notes: Neo-humanist sans-serif with mixed terminal treatments across the character set. A 10-weight italic-only subfamily of the broader Andes superfamily. Genuine italic alternate forms for a, g, y and z distinguish it from a slanted roman. Shares structural DNA with Hernández's earlier Merced design.
summary: A neo-humanist italic display sans by Daniel Hernández, spanning ten weights from UltraLight to Black with true italic alternates for a, g, y and z.
description: Published by Latinotype in 2012, Andes Italic is built on a neo-humanist structure with varied terminal treatments that give it an eclectic, editorial character. Ten weights from UltraLight to Black share a consistent x-height, and genuine italic alternates for a, g, y and z mean it functions as a true italic rather than a slanted roman. Related to Hernández's earlier Merced, it targets retail, magazine and logotype contexts where the italic carries real typographic weight.
foundry_blurb: Andes Italic is a display typeface with neo-humanist characteristics. Varied terminals give it a quality of mixed typography, and the family includes dedicated italic glyph variants for a, y, z and g to add emphasis and sharpen the contrast with upright settings. Ten weights run from Ultra Light to Black, all at a consistent x-height. Based on the design of Merced, it is suited to retail, magazines, logotypes and books.

name: Andes Neue
classification_notes: Contemporary geometric sans-serif with slight humanist touches. Four stylistic alternates range from clean and minimal to more expressive glyph variants. Designed for both text and display use, with an emphasis on broad Latin multilingual coverage.
summary: A geometric sans-serif by Daniel Hernández, released in 2019, offering 56 styles across four stylistic alternates with a 759-glyph character set covering 219 Latin-based languages.
description: Andes Neue is a contemporary geometric sans-serif that expands the original Andes family with a substantially enlarged character set and four distinct variants. Alt 1 strips back legacy details for a cleaner read, Alt 2 promotes alternates to defaults, and Alt 3 blends all three approaches — giving designers genuine typographic range within a single purchase. Seven weights from Thin to Black, each with italics and small caps, make it a dependable workhorse for editorial, branding and multilingual work.
foundry_blurb: Andes Neue builds on the original Andes with a greatly expanded character set, four stylistic alternates and seven weights suited to both short and mid-length text. The 759-glyph set covers 219 Latin-based languages across 212 countries, making it one of Latinotype's most broadly applicable families.

name: Andes Rounded
classification_notes: Neo-humanist sans-serif built on a Grotesk skeleton, with humanistic terminals and rounded corners throughout all weights. Related to the Andes family; shares design features with Merced. The rounded treatment gives it warmth while the Grotesk structure maintains legibility across sizes.
summary: A rounded neo-humanist sans from Latinotype spanning ten weights, pairing a Grotesk skeleton with softened humanistic terminals for a warm, characterful display face.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández in 2014, Andes Rounded takes a Grotesk structure and softens it with humanistic terminals and rounded corners throughout, giving it warmth without sacrificing legibility. The family runs from UltraLight to Black across upright, italic and condensed variants, holding consistent x-height at every weight. It suits retail, editorial and logotype work where a friendly sans needs real weight range.
foundry_blurb: A display typeface with neo-humanist characteristics whose different terminals and mixed typographic elements give it a distinctive character. Built on a Grotesk skeleton with humanistic rounded corners, it spans ten weights from UltraLight to Black in upright, italic and condensed cuts. Includes alternate italic glyphs for a, y, z and g to aid emphasis, and is suited to retail design, magazines, logotypes and books.

name: Anguita Sans
classification_notes: A condensed grotesque sans with soft rounded terminals and a generous x-height. All 16 styles span eight weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic. Proportions are tightly condensed throughout, making it a single-width display family rather than a variable-width system. Positioned for headline and short-form display use in print and digital.
summary: A condensed grotesque from Sofia Mohr for Chile's Latinotype, with rounded terminals and a large x-height across eight weights plus matching italics, built for headlines and short display text.
description: Anguita Sans is a condensed grotesque designed by Sofia Mohr and published by Latinotype in 2020. Rounded terminals and a generous x-height give the letterforms a soft, approachable quality within their tight proportions. Eight weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, provide enough range for consistent display work across both print and digital applications.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Anguita Sans as a stylish and versatile condensed sans suited to a wide range of applications, with its rounded terminals and large x-height enabling strong vertical rhythm, particularly in titles and short lines of text.

name: Animal
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif with dramatic thick-thin stroke variation, sharp terminals and angular strokes. Four widths (Condensed, Narrow, Regular, Expanded) each in three weights, giving twelve styles. Strong editorial and fashion character; not intended for continuous text.
summary: A high-contrast display serif with four widths and three weights, built for editorial headers, fashion campaigns and bold packaging work.
description: Animal is a high-contrast display serif by Juan Bruce, published through Latinotype in 2025. The family spans four widths – Condensed, Narrow, Regular and Expanded – each in three weights, totalling twelve styles. Sharp terminals and dramatic stroke contrast give it a commanding editorial presence suited to fashion campaigns, posters and branding.
foundry_blurb: A high-contrast serif combining fluid curves with dramatic stroke contrasts drawn from the strength and balance of the natural world. Unusual terminals and angular strokes create a distinctive, commanding presence suited to branding, posters, fashion campaigns and packaging.

name: Antartida
classification_notes: Monolinear geometric sans-serif with a deliberately neutral character. Even stroke weight throughout; no optical adjustments or humanist softening. Four weights from Light to Black, each with a matching italic. Alternate glyphs included for headline use. A rounded variant (Antartida Rounded) exists as a separate family.
summary: A monolinear geometric sans-serif in four weights with italics, built for clean, neutral work across body text and display.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara and released in 2012, Antartida holds a consistent monolinear stroke weight across a Light-to-Black range, giving it an undemonstrative, functional character. Each weight ships with an italic, and alternate glyphs extend its usefulness for headline setting. It occupies well-trodden geometric sans territory without staking out distinctive ground, though the craft is considered and the family is practical.
foundry_blurb: Antartida is a sans-serif typeface whose monolinear structure gives it a neutral character – functional, clean and minimal. The eight-font family spans four weights with italics and includes alternate glyphs for emphasising text or headlines.

name: Antartida Essential
classification_notes: Even-stroke monolinear construction with geometric proportions and minimal contrast. The Essential cut is a reduced subset of the broader Antartida family: 4 styles (Light, Bold + italics), 219 glyphs covering Windows 1252, no alternates. Neutral and clean without distinctive personality.
summary: A lean monolinear sans-serif offering Light and Bold weights with italics, cut from the broader Antartida family with no alternates and limited glyph coverage.
description: Antartida Essential is Luciano Vergara's stripped entry point into the Antartida family – a monolinear sans-serif with even stroke weight and restrained proportions suited to functional text work. The Essential cut ships with just four styles and no alternates, making it a budget-conscious option rather than a comprehensive type system. It reads cleanly at small sizes but its limited glyph count and lack of variants cap how far it stretches.
foundry_blurb: A minimal sans-serif whose simple monolinear structure gives it a clean, neutral quality designed to simplify the designer's workflow. From Los Andes, a Concepción-based foundry established in 2011 by Luciano Vergara and collaborators, whose typefaces draw on travel, nature and direct experience.

name: Antartida Rounded
classification_notes: Geometric-leaning sans-serif with uniformly soft, rounded terminals throughout. Proportions are clean and neutral with no strong humanist or grotesque pull. The rounding is applied consistently rather than as a superficial finish, giving the typeface a calm, approachable character. Sits comfortably in the friendly rounded sans tradition alongside VAG Rounded and Nunito.
summary: A clean, neutral rounded sans-serif by Luciano Vergara with four weights, broad Latin language coverage and a warm, approachable character suited to UI and display use.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara and released in 2012, Antartida Rounded is a sans-serif whose softly rounded terminals lend it a friendly warmth without undermining its functional, minimal proportions. Four weights from Light to Black each come with an italic, and the family covers a wide spread of Latin-based languages including Eastern European and Turkish. It works well in display settings and UI copy where a light, welcoming tone is needed.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Antartida Rounded as a sans-serif with rounded terminals whose simple, neutral character is functional, clean and minimal, with the rounded terminals lending it a friendly and warm quality. The family includes alternate glyphs for headline and emphasis use.

name: Antartida Rounded Essential
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with rounded terminals applied consistently across all strokes. Low contrast, clean construction with a neutral typographic colour. A four-style subset of the wider Antartida Rounded family, covering Light and Bold with their italics only.
summary: A geometric rounded sans-serif by Luciano Vergara with soft terminals throughout – clean, neutral and functional, available in Light and Bold with italics.
description: Antartida Rounded Essential is a four-style subset of the Antartida Rounded family, pairing Light and Bold with their italics. The rounded terminals soften the geometry without tipping into novelty, giving the typeface a warm, approachable character. It works well in branding and UI contexts where a friendly but restrained tone is wanted.
foundry_blurb: A sans-serif with rounded terminals; simple, neutral and minimal in character. The rounded stroke endings give it a clean functionality alongside a friendly warmth.

name: Antonietta
classification_notes: Calligraphic script rooted in the Copperplate tradition, inspired by rococo aesthetics and the personality of Marie Antoinette. The script variant features high x-height, condensed proportions and short ascenders and descenders modifiable via contextual alternates (878 glyphs). Designed by Mauricio Astete Brito with explicit reference to Hermann Zapf, Ricardo Rousselot and Herb Lubalin. Developed by converting hand lettering into digital form under Latinotype's guidance.
summary: A rococo-inspired Copperplate script by Mauricio Astete Brito, developed from hand lettering and referencing Zapf, Rousselot and Lubalin, with seven variants including four decorative cap cuts and an ornaments set.
description: Released in 2016, Antonietta draws on Marie Antoinette's flamboyance and the Copperplate tradition, producing a calligraphic script with high x-height, condensed proportions and contextual alternates across 878 glyphs. Four decorative cap variants – standard, illuminated, shadow and inline – plus a dedicated ornaments font extend the family into a self-contained display system. Best suited to logotypes, labels, packaging and short headlines where period-appropriate theatrics are the brief.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Antonietta as Mauricio Astete Brito's debut typeface: a rococo-spirited Copperplate script inspired by Queen Marie Antoinette's eccentricity, developed from hand lettering under Latinotype's guidance, and referencing the work of Hermann Zapf, Ricardo Rousselot and Herb Lubalin.

name: Apparel
classification_notes: Contemporary transitional-style serif drawn from the 1912 ATF MacFarland series; proportions and colour share ground with Times New Roman and Caslon; split into Basic (text) and Display (high contrast) optical variants; medium-large x-height; moderately slanted italics available as OpenType Stylistic Alternates
summary: A contemporary editorial serif in two optical variants – Basic and Display – drawn from the 1912 ATF MacFarland series, suited to headlines and brand identity work.
description: Apparel pairs a medium-large x-height with modulated stroke contrast across 20 styles, split between a text-ready Basic subfamily and a higher-contrast Display. Designed by Daniel Hernández and Alfonso García in 2020, it draws on American Type Founders heritage while sitting comfortably in a contemporary branding register. Support for 200-plus Latin languages and a basic Cyrillic set broadens its practical range.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Apparel as a contemporary, classy serif with a laid-back attitude. Inspired by the MacFarland series in the 1912 ATF catalog, it shares functional characteristics with Times New Roman and Caslon while maintaining its own personality. A medium-large x-height makes it well-suited to headlines and brand identity design.

name: Aromatica
classification_notes: Rounded humanist sans-serif with calligraphic influences. Letterforms soften at terminals in a way that references handwriting without imitating it. Accompanied by a monolinear script and a decorative patterns font — three subfamilies together forming a single branding kit.
summary: A five-weight rounded sans-serif by Sofia Mohr, released in 2017 via Latinotype, with a monolinear script companion and a herb-and-spice-inspired patterns font aimed at branding and packaging work.
description: Aromatica pairs five weights of a clean rounded sans with a monolinear script and a decorative patterns font. The letterforms borrow gently from handwriting — rounded terminals, even stroke weight — without losing typographic control. Published by Latinotype in 2017, the family covers 207 languages and is pitched squarely at packaging and branding contexts.
foundry_blurb: A rounded typeface with a simple, clean look that echoes the strokes found in handwriting while keeping readability intact. Specially designed for branding and packaging, though suited equally to headlines, publishing and advertising. The family includes a monolinear script and a companion patterns font drawn from aromatic herbs and spices.

name: Arquitecta
classification_notes: Geometric sans with humanist proportions, blending Bauhaus-influenced rational construction with early 20th-century hand lettering traditions. Features ink traps for print, small x-height with pronounced ascenders and descenders. Positioned as a text-reading alternative to Futura, Kabel and Avant Garde. Updated with corrected contours in 2023.
summary: A geometric sans-serif from Daniel Hernández that pairs Bauhaus-influenced construction with humanist proportions, designed with extended text reading in mind.
description: Arquitecta draws on early 20th-century American and European hand lettering to produce a geometric sans that performs well at text sizes, with a small x-height, pronounced ascenders and descenders, and ink traps built in for print. The family spans 16 weights from Thin to ExtraBold, each with a matching italic, and includes old-style figures and fraction support. It occupies the same territory as Futura or Kabel, but with more deliberate attention to extended reading comfort.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Arquitecta as a rational geometric typeface with humanist proportions, conceived for text layout and continuous reading. The design draws on Bauhaus experimentation and first-half-of-century hand lettering traditions, offering a practical alternative to geometric classics like Futura, Kabel and Avant Garde.

name: Arquitecta Office
classification_notes: Geometric construction with humanist proportions; ink traps aid text rendering; Office-compatible variant of the main Arquitecta family, reduced to four styles with weight names recalibrated to display in correct hierarchy within Microsoft Office font menus. Bold is notably heavier than its counterpart in the full family.
summary: A four-style Microsoft Office–ready cut of Arquitecta, Daniel Hernández's geometric humanist sans drawn from early 20th-century hand-lettering and Bauhaus influences.
description: Arquitecta Office reduces the full 16-style Arquitecta family to Regular, Italic, Bold and Bold Italic, with weight names set so they appear in correct order within Microsoft Office font menus. The design pairs rational geometric structure with humanist proportions, drawing on Bauhaus experimentation and early 20th-century American and European hand-lettering — sitting alongside Futura and Avant Garde while staying legible at text sizes. Ink traps help print performance, and old-style numerals and fractions carry over from the original family.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype adapted Arquitecta for use in Microsoft Office, naming weights so they display in clear hierarchy within Office font lists. The bold weight is notably heavier than its equivalent in the original full-family release.

name: Arquitecta Standard
classification_notes: Rational geometric construction with humanist proportions. Small x-height and pronounced ascenders/descenders favour text use. Ink traps prevent fill at smaller sizes. Draws on Bauhaus experimentation and early 20th-century American and European hand lettering. Positioned as a text-weight alternative to Futura, Kabel and Avant Garde.
summary: A geometric sans with humanist proportions built for text, spanning eight weights with italics and refined with ink traps for small-size performance.
description: Arquitecta Standard pairs geometric structure with humanist proportions to produce a text face suited to continuous reading. Its small x-height and pronounced ascenders give it a classical feel within a rational framework, and ink traps prevent fill under press conditions. Eight weights with matching italics make it a reliable choice across editorial and brand work.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by American and European hand lettering from the first half of the 20th century, Arquitecta Standard carves out space as a paragraph alternative to classics like Futura, Kabel and Avant Garde. The 16-style family includes European accent support, ink traps to prevent press impressing spots, and optimised hinting throughout.

name: Assemblage
designer: Bruno Jara, Alfonso García, Luciano Vergara, Daniel Hernández
classification_notes: Roman square capitals inform the proportions; the italic departs into Elzeverian and Dutch Baroque territory with swashes, ending forms and ornamental alternates. Purpose-built for packaging and titling rather than text setting.
summary: A six-weight display sans rooted in Roman square capitals, built for wine labels and packaging with a Baroque-influenced italic, dedicated ornaments and 212-language coverage.
description: Assemblage draws from Roman square capital proportions to produce a clean display sans across six weights from Thin to Black. The italic departs into Elzeverian and Dutch Baroque territory, adding swashes, ending forms and three sets of ornamental small caps. At 979 characters, it ships with companion dingbat and ornament sets tailored to packaging and decorative publishing.
foundry_blurb: A typeface inspired by Roman square capitals, designed for wine-bottle labelling and general packaging. Six weights run from Thin to Black; the italic draws from Elzeverian and Dutch Baroque models, bringing swashes, alternates and ornamental small caps. Companion dingbat and ornament sets extend the family into decorative publishing work.

name: Atlan
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif in the 1920s expressionist tradition, drawing explicitly from Rudolf Koch's Kabel. Eight weights with full italic counterparts; no condensed variants. Latin script with Western and Latin American language coverage.
summary: A 1920s-rooted geometric sans from Chilean foundry Latinotype, spanning eight weights with full italic coverage and a clear debt to Rudolf Koch's Kabel.
description: Designed by Jorge Cisterna and Daniel Hernández and released in 2017, Atlan takes the expressionist geometric sans tradition – most visibly Kabel – and reworks it for contemporary publishing and branding contexts. The family covers eight weights with italic counterparts, from a refined Thin suited to editorial layouts through to a Heavy cut built for logotypes and packaging. The design is functional and even-handed, sitting comfortably in corporate and editorial work without much surprise.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Atlan as a Latin spin-off of classic geometric sans typefaces from the 1920s, reinterpreting their expressive qualities without sacrificing versatility. The range runs from a Thin weight suited to publishing and corporate websites through to a Heavy variant optimised for logotypes and packaging.

name: Australis Pro
classification_notes: Designer's own term "hybrid roman" signals a deliberate blending of old-style humanist structure with more contemporary proportions. The italic carries a pronounced calligraphic quality. A separate Swash companion adds swash alternates, discretionary ligatures, and contextual alternates for display settings. Primarily suited to editorial and text use.
summary: A Gold Prize-winning hybrid roman from Chilean designer Francisco Gálvez Pizarro, refined over a decade from its 2002 Morisawa competition entry into a six-weight editorial serif with a separate swash companion.
description: Australis Pro is a hybrid roman serif designed by Francisco Gálvez Pizarro, blending old-style humanist structure with a calligraphic italic sensibility. It won the Gold Prize at the 2002 Morisawa International Type Design Competition, with the full six-weight family released publicly in 2012. A companion Swash subfamily extends the range with swash alternates, discretionary ligatures, and contextual alternates for display work.
foundry_blurb: Australis is a hybrid roman typeface that took first prize in the Morisawa International Type Design Competition in 2002. The complete family took a further decade to develop, with its release timed to coincide with the competition's reopening in Japan in 2012.

name: Australis Pro Swash
classification_notes: An all-italic calligraphic script family extending Australis Pro with exaggerated swash treatments, contextual alternates and ligatures that lean into a hand-drawn, mannered quality. Inherits the optical refinement of a Morisawa International Type Design Competition Gold Prize-winning parent design (2002). Display-only; not suited for body text.
summary: A swash italic extension of Francisco Gálvez's Morisawa Gold Prize-winning Australis Pro, adding exaggerated cursive flourishes across three italic weights for display and branding work.
description: Australis Pro Swash builds on a typeface with serious competition pedigree, overlaying the original design's calligraphic bones with pronounced swash details and decorative mannerism. Three weights – Italic, Bold Italic and Heavy Italic – are available, each carrying OpenType support for standard and discretionary ligatures plus contextual alternates. The family is built for display settings: headlines, packaging and lettering where personality outweighs neutrality.
foundry_blurb: Founded in Concepción, Chile in 2007, Latinotype set out to bring South American and Latin design traditions into contemporary type. Led by Miguel Hernández alongside Luciano Vergara and Daniel Hernández, the studio has grown into a catalogue of over 200 original typefaces drawing on Chilean visual culture, political poster art and the region's broader typographic history.

name: Autor
classification_notes: Medium-contrast sans-serif with dynamic stroke modulation and distinctly angled terminals. Sits between humanist warmth and geometric precision — closer to the sharper, more editorial end of the spectrum. Not a neutral grotesque; the stroke variation gives it presence at both text and display sizes.
summary: A medium-contrast sans-serif with angled terminals and measured stroke modulation, spanning seven weights with matching italics for editorial and branding work.
description: Autor was designed by Luis Bandovas and released by Latinotype in 2018. Its stroke variation and angled terminals give it a crisp, contemporary edge that reads well at both text and display sizes. The fourteen-style family covers 400+ glyphs across 200+ languages, making it a credible workhorse for editorial, branding and publishing contexts.
foundry_blurb: Autor brings dynamic stroke modulation to the sans-serif form, with a clean structure and angled terminals that produce a sharp, contemporary character. Its fourteen styles – seven weights each with a roman and italic – suit a wide range of applications from book and magazine body text to logotypes, headers and advertising.

name: Bach
classification_notes: Hybrid display type system combining a high-contrast serif (derived from Latinotype's Garden typeface) with a brush-pen script and two decorative ornament sets (Borders and Floral). Sixteen styles in total. The serif follows a traditional display structure with strong stroke contrast; the script is drawn with a brush pen, giving it a loose calligraphic quality. Intended for packaging, labelling and poster display rather than running text.
designer: Mendoza Vergara Studio (Cecilia Mendoza, digital editing; Luciano Vergara and Coto Mendoza, supervision)
summary: A 16-style display system pairing a high-contrast serif with a brush-pen script and decorative ornaments, aimed at packaging, labelling and poster work.
description: Bach was released by Latinotype in 2016, designed by Mendoza Vergara Studio. It combines a six-weight display serif (with italics, drawn from the same roots as the Garden typeface) with two weights of brush-pen script and two ornament sets covering decorative borders and floral motifs. The system is designed to work as a self-contained toolkit for artisanal packaging, labelling and illustrated editorial work.
foundry_blurb: A display type system built around the idea of returning to natural, handcrafted values. Bach combines a calligraphic brush script with a refined display serif and ornamental sets – borders and florals included – making it a complete solution for labelling, packaging, illustrated books and posters.

name: Basic Sans
classification_notes: Neutral low-contrast grotesque with consistent stroke width and open apertures. An Alt subfamily provides stylistic alternates (single-storey 'a', alternate 'g' and similar). Basic Sans Cnd is a separate condensed companion family mirroring the full 28-style range at a narrower width.
summary: A workmanlike neutral grotesque from Latinotype with seven weights, matching italics, a condensed companion and solid coverage of 206 languages.
description: Basic Sans is a functional, low-contrast grotesque designed by Daniel Hernández, suited equally to body copy and display settings. Seven weights from Thin to Black come with matching italics; an Alt subfamily provides stylistic alternates for key characters. A full condensed family, Basic Sans Cnd, extends the range for space-constrained layouts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Basic Sans as a grotesque with a functional, neutral and seemingly clean style – designed for publishing, branding, posters and headlines – that keeps a basic appearance while including details that give it a distinct personality.

name: Basic Sans Condensed
classification_notes: Condensed grotesque sans-serif with a deliberately neutral, functional character. Seven weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic. Ships in two subfamilies: Basic and Alt (alternate character set). Closely related to Basic Sans, sharing the same design DNA in a narrowed width.
summary: A condensed grotesque from Chilean foundry Latinotype, covering seven weights from Thin to Black with matching italics, an alternate-character subfamily and support for 206 languages.
description: Released in December 2016 by Daniel Hernández, Basic Sans Condensed takes the neutral grotesque character of Basic Sans into a tighter width. The family spans 28 styles across two subfamilies – Basic and Alt – with 416 characters and broad Latin language coverage. It suits publishing, branding, posters and headlines where a clean, functional condensed face is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Basic Sans Condensed as a grotesque with a functional, neutral and clean aesthetic – a narrower companion to the original Basic Sans. Designed for versatility across publishing, branding, posters and medium-sized text, the family offers 416 characters with support for 206 languages.

name: Basic Sans Narrow
classification_notes: Condensed neutral grotesque with clean lines and considered detailing. Part of the wider Basic Sans family, sharing its functional character and broad weight range in a compressed width.
summary: A condensed grotesque from Latinotype with a neutral, functional character, seven weights and matching italics, suited to publishing, branding and headline use.
description: Basic Sans Narrow is the compressed cut of Daniel Hernández's Basic Sans, a neutral grotesque that pairs clean geometry with enough considered detail to hold its own. Seven weights run from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, and an alternate figure set forms a second subfamily. The 416-character set covers 206 languages, making it a practical choice for multilingual Latin-script work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Basic Sans Narrow as a grotesque with a functional, neutral and clean style — one that aims to read as unassuming while retaining enough individual detail to avoid blandness. The family is intended for publishing, branding, posters and medium-sized text applications.

name: Beauchef
classification_notes: Rational geometric sans-serif with deliberately rough, textured strokes produced through optical compensation rather than clean geometry. The design departs from conventional perceptual rules while maintaining strong legibility. Commissioned for institutional use, it pairs an avant-garde stroke character with calm, precise proportions.
summary: A rational geometric sans by Juan Pablo De Gregorio, commissioned for the University of Chile's mathematical modelling centre, with deliberately rough strokes and careful optical compensation.
description: Designed for the University of Chile's Centro de Modelamiento Matemático, Beauchef applies a geometric skeleton to rough, textured strokes – an outcome of deliberate optical compensation rather than ornamentation. Five weights run from Light to Black, each paired with an italic, covering Western, Central European, Baltic and Turkish character sets. It sits between institutional rigour and a quietly unusual character that distinguishes it from standard geometric sans-serifs.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Beauchef as a typeface originally developed for the University of Chile's Centre for Mathematical Modelling. It combines an avant-garde approach to perceptual compensation with calm, humble proportions – as tough as advanced mathematics, and as legible and exact as numbers themselves.

name: Beth
classification_notes: Pop gothic serif with extreme stroke contrast drawn from engraving traditions. Formal, monument-like uppercase with humanist terminals; single-storey calligraphic lowercase influenced by Edward Johnston's Foundational Hand. Beth Alt subfamily provides alternate terminal treatments and shifted proportions within the same structural logic.
summary: A high-contrast pop gothic serif pairing a formal engraving-inflected uppercase with a calligraphic Johnston-influenced lowercase, delivered across 14 styles in two parallel character registers.
description: Beth sets a monument-like uppercase — drawn from early twentieth-century English shopfront lettering and engraving contrast — against a single-storey calligraphic lowercase informed by Edward Johnston's Foundational Hand, creating structural tension that is rare in high-contrast serifs. Ale Navarro designed it for Latinotype in 2026, spanning seven weights in two subfamilies: the standard Beth and Beth Alt, which offers distinct terminal treatments and altered proportions for a different formal register. The extreme hairline-to-heavy contrast makes it a natural fit for luxury packaging, editorial mastheads and poster work; below 11pt it is not in its element.
foundry_blurb: Beth draws from early twentieth-century English shopfront lettering and neoclassical type traditions, with the calligraphic lowercase shaped by Edward Johnston's Foundational Hand and the contrast ratios pulled from the engraving work of Gustave Doré and William Blake. Its upper- and lowercase operate in separate expressive registers — formal and monumental above, fluid and calligraphic below — and the two subfamilies, Beth and Beth Alt, extend those choices further with differing terminals and proportions. Latinotype positions it as a typeface equally suited to a luxury fragrance label and a concert poster.

name: Better Sans
classification_notes: Geometric construction softened by rounded, compact letterforms and warm humanist proportions; distinctive character treatments across 16 styles from Thin to Heavy.
designer: Luciano Vergara, Jorge Cisterna, Daniel Hernández, Felipe Sanzana
summary: A rounded geometric sans with warmth built in, spanning 16 styles from Thin to Heavy, well suited to branding and digital headlines.
description: Better Sans pairs geometric construction with round, compact letterforms that feel approachable without losing clarity. Sixteen styles cover Thin through Heavy with matching italics, giving solid range for both branding and editorial work. The distinctive character treatments make it strongest at display sizes, in headlines, apps and brand identities.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Better Sans as a dependable companion that merges geometric shapes with warmth. Round proportions and distinctive character treatments give words a clear identity, while the full weight range handles everything from traditional print to digital-first applications.

name: Biennale
classification_notes: A geometric sans-serif with a prominently large x-height and strong visual presence. Eleven weights from Hair to Heavy, each with a matching italic, totalling 22 styles. The standard character set of 417 glyphs covers over 200 Latin-based languages. Clean geometric construction with no condensed or extended variants.
summary: A geometric sans-serif by Daniel Hernández with a large x-height, spanning 11 weights from Hair to Heavy each with a matching italic.
description: Biennale is a geometric sans-serif built around a large x-height, which keeps it legible and consistent across the full weight range. The family runs from Hair to Heavy across 11 weights, each paired with a matching italic — 22 styles in total. With over 200 Latin-based languages covered, it holds up well for branding and headline work that needs broad character support.
foundry_blurb: Biennale is a geometric typeface with a strong character and a large x-height, designed for a wide range of applications including headlines and branding. Its distinctive details and consistent page colour create varied design possibilities across the weight range.

name: Biennale Arabic
classification_notes: Arabic companion to the geometric sans-serif Biennale Latin family; clean, large-x-height letterforms that follow geometric construction principles while respecting Arabic calligraphic conventions; 11 weights from Hair to Heavy, each with a matching italic
summary: A geometric Arabic sans-serif in 11 weights with matching italics, designed to sit alongside its Latin counterpart in bilingual branding and editorial work.
description: Released in March 2025, Biennale Arabic extends Daniel Hernández's geometric Latin family into Arabic script, preserving the original's large x-height and strong character across 22 styles. The design balances calligraphic Arabic conventions with contemporary geometric clarity, making it practical for bilingual layouts where visual consistency between scripts matters. Weight coverage runs from Hair to Heavy, with a matching italic at every step.
foundry_blurb: Biennale Arabic brings the geometric and contemporary character of the original Latin family into Arabic script, striking a balance between calligraphic tradition and legibility. It integrates cleanly with its Latin counterpart for bilingual work across branding, editorial and digital projects.

name: Bikini Season
subcategory: font duo – display sans + calligraphy script
classification_notes: Two-style font duo. Bikini Season Sans draws from Roman capital proportions with a clean, contemporary finish. Bikini Season Script is a loose modern calligraphy with ornamental OpenType features. Both styles are display-weight only, built for poster and branding hierarchies rather than running text.
summary: A summer-themed font duo by Luciano Vergara and Guisela Mendoza pairing a Roman-proportioned display sans with a loose calligraphy script for poster and branding use.
description: Bikini Season pairs two contrasting styles: a display sans built on Roman capital proportions with a clean, chic finish, and a casual handwritten script with OpenType ornaments. Both styles are display-weight and designed to be combined for visual hierarchy in branding, labeling and poster work. The summer/boho concept is baked into the name and aesthetic, which keeps its useful range narrow.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Bikini Season as a relaxed, spontaneous and feminine duo – a boho beach-vacation companion. The sans takes its structure from Roman capitals but adds a contemporary, chic quality; the script brings modern calligraphy with a handmade feel and a set of ornamental characters. The two styles are intended to create contrast and visual counterpoint when combined.

name: Blackberry
classification_notes: Angular-serif display face drawing from 19th-century wood type, built as a ten-part layered system with 3D extrusions, shadow, inline and outline variants. Numbered layers (One through Eight) are designed to be stacked for composite effects rather than used as conventional weight steps.
summary: A ten-layer wood type display system with angular serifs drawn from vintage packaging and showbill lettering, designed for stacked poster, label and branding work.
description: Blackberry is a layered display family by Jorge Cisterna and Bruno Jara Ahumada, comprising eight combinable layers plus flags and dingbats for building up 3D extrusions, shadows and outline effects. The design pulls from 19th-century wood type traditions – angular serifs, slightly curved strokes and sharp edges – and is aimed squarely at labels, packaging and large-scale poster work. Support for over 200 Latin-based languages gives it more reach than most vintage-revival display faces.
foundry_blurb: A typographical family drawn from vintage packaging design, old-fashioned advertising and show business marketing campaigns. Blackberry revives wood type characteristics – angular serifs, diagonal curves and sharp edges – through a dynamic layering system of 3D extrusions, shadows, inline graphics, dingbats and flags across ten fonts with support for over 200 Latin-based languages.

name: Blanc
classification_notes: Humanist sans with geometric construction; low contrast between thick and thin strokes; calligraphic details on select glyphs add personality without disrupting the neutral character. Includes a Heavy Inline variant alongside the main 8-weight family.
summary: A geometric humanist sans by Jorge Cisterna with eight weights, calligraphic stroke details on select glyphs, and an inline variant suited to headlines and corporate work.
description: Blanc pairs low-contrast geometry with calligraphic touches on specific glyphs, giving the family a quiet distinctiveness within its stated neutrality. Eighteen styles run from Thin to Black with italics throughout, plus a Heavy Inline variant. It sits well in headlines, subheadings, and corporate design where a degree of character is welcome without veering towards the idiosyncratic.
foundry_blurb: A functional humanist sans with a marked personality, Blanc is Latinotype's ode to neutrality: a geometric face characterised by low contrast between thick and thin strokes with calligraphic features that emphasise specific glyphs. The family is designed for headlines, subheadings, corporate design, advertising, and publishing.

name: Blauth
classification_notes: Contemporary sans with a notably compact x-height and softened corners. Sits between geometric precision and humanist warmth – crisply structured but not cold. Small x-height gives it classic proportions more common in transitional serifs. Equally usable for running text and display headlines.
summary: A warm sans from Latinotype designer Sofia Mohr, Blauth uses a compact x-height and softened corners to sit between geometric clarity and humanist approachability across 18 styles.
description: Designed by Sofia Mohr and published in 2018, Blauth pairs a small, classically proportioned x-height with gently rounded corners – enough structure for body text, enough warmth for editorial and brand work. Eight weights with matching italics give it solid range. Language support covers Central European, Baltic, Turkish and Pan-African Latin scripts alongside standard Western European sets.
foundry_blurb: Blauth brings contemporary versatility and classic elegance into one family. Its compact x-height echoes traditional typeface proportions while softened corners give warmth without sacrificing precision. Works across extended text passages and makes a strong impression in uppercase display setting.

name: Bock
classification_notes: Asymmetric display slab serif with compact letterforms engineered to disrupt typographic rhythm. Two weights only, no italics. The Fat cut eliminates surrounding letter spacing, pushing into extreme-weight display territory.
summary: A compact 2011 display slab with asymmetric stroke construction that deliberately unsettles typographic rhythm, built for logotypes and short editorial headlines.
description: Bock pairs a slab serif structure with asymmetric line construction, giving its letterforms a stable yet slightly off-kilter quality. The family has two weights: the regular cut and Fat, which strips away inner and outer letter spacing for maximum visual density. It suits logotypes and short display settings where a blunt, characterful headline face is needed.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Bock as a recreational face born from experimentation with the slab serif form, using asymmetric lines to produce something compact and stable that still breaks typographic rhythm. The Fat weight takes this further by removing the space around each letter, creating a font built for weight and attitude.

name: Boho
classification_notes: Gestural calligraphic script developed using a Cola pen technique. The core script spawns four variants – plain, Drop, Line and Line Drop – with teardrop terminals distinguishing the Line cuts. Complementary Sans and Serif subfamilies share the same proportional base. Dingbats and Ornaments complete the system.
summary: A gestural calligraphic script family from Guisela Mendoza, built on Cola pen technique and expanded into a 26-style system with complementary Sans, Serif and decorative companions.
description: Boho was Mendoza's first script release, launched in 2015 and rooted in experimental Cola pen calligraphy she developed while designing Macarons. The family spans four script variants – plain, Drop, Line and Line Drop, with teardrop terminals distinguishing the Line cuts – alongside matching Sans and Serif subfamilies at four weights each. Boho Dingbats and Ornaments complete the system, making it a self-contained toolkit for bohemian-aesthetic branding work.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by a free spirit who moves between city life, nature and art with equal ease, Boho is drawn from Cola pen calligraphy and designed to carry that open, unbound energy across branding, editorial and packaging applications.

name: Bosque
classification_notes: Rough-edged handmade display face with six layerable variants (Regular, Shadow, Wood, Wood Shadow, Shadow One, Dingbats). Forms have soft terminals and an organic, hand-drawn quality. Designed for stacking variants to achieve textured depth effects. Not suitable for text use.
summary: A rough-edged handmade display face with six layerable variants — Regular, Wood, Shadow, Wood Shadow, Shadow One and Dingbats — built for craft-inflected, textured headlines.
description: Released in 2012 by Chilean designers Paula Nazal Selaive and Daniel Hernández, Bosque pairs a raw hand-drawn quality with six variants designed for layering. Stack Wood over Shadow for typographic depth, or use Regular alone for a looser, hand-lettered feel. The extended character set includes ligatures and alternates, though the face is suited to short display work rather than running text.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype is a Chilean type foundry that draws on South American cultural identity to produce display and script typefaces for the contemporary design industry. Based in Concepción and Santiago, the studio mixes local influences with international craft standards.

name: Boston
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with slightly rounded edges, derived from Latinotype's 2013 Trenda. Consistent stroke weight throughout, with a pronounced uppercase personality. Includes small caps, alternates and ligatures via OpenType.
summary: Boston is a slightly rounded geometric sans-serif from Latinotype, spanning eight weights with matching italics and a strong uppercase character suited to corporate and logotype work.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández and Paula Nazal Selaive, Boston draws from Latinotype's 2013 Trenda, softening its geometry with subtly rounded edges. The family runs from Thin to Heavy across eight weights, each with a matching italic, and ships with small caps, alternates and a 634-character set covering 206 languages. The extreme weights serve display use; mid-range cuts hold up in short to mid-length text.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Boston as a versatile, functional display font with strong uppercase personality. Built for corporate projects, logotypes and publishing, the lightest and heaviest weights are intended for display, while the middle cuts handle short to mid-length texts.

name: Bowie
classification_notes: Sharp-edged, uppercase-only display sans with a strong angular character. Designed as a full type system, pairing weighted all-caps fonts with a script catchwords subfamily and decorative dingbat/flag sets. Reverse italic (backslant) cuts are included alongside standard italics across all five weights.
summary: A sharp all-caps display sans from 2016, released as a 20-style system spanning five weights with standard and reverse italics, script catchwords, and two sets each of decorative dingbats and flags.
description: Bowie is built around five weights of an angular, uppercase-only sans – Thin through Black – each cut in both regular and reverse italic, which is an unusual and useful addition for typographic contrast. The family extends into script catchwords and two sets each of dingbats and flags, making it a self-contained toolkit for branding and packaging. Its 439-character set covers 206 languages, giving it genuine range for a display face.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Bowie as a type system that carries a strong personality, an urban feel and an unprejudiced style. Its three sections – sharp uppercase weights, script catchwords, and decorative dingbat and flag sets – are suited to publishing, branding and packaging projects. The name comes from Jim Bowie, the American pioneer and knife inventor whose name also inspired David Jones to take his stage name.
designer: Luciano Vergara, Daniel Hernández, Bercz Studio, Latinotype Team

name: Branding
classification_notes: Spurless sans-serif with straight curves and convex terminals. Medium-large x-height with slightly wider horizontal proportions. Contemporary construction aimed squarely at display and identity work.
designer: Luciano Vergara, Daniel Hernández, Alfonso García
summary: A spurless geometric sans-serif with convex terminals and a full weight range, built for logotype and identity work with broad multilingual coverage.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara, Daniel Hernández and Alfonso García, Branding is a display-oriented sans-serif with straight curves, convex terminals and a medium-large x-height suited to identity and packaging work. It spans seven weights from Thin to Black, each with an italic, giving the family real range without a condensed cut. The 544-glyph set covers 128 languages and includes old-style figures and multiple alternates for compositional flexibility.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Branding as their interpretation of a contemporary typeface that pairs technical construction with approachable rounded shapes. They position it for logotypes, isotypes and short text, citing its medium-large x-height, slightly wider proportions and convex terminals as the defining details that give it a clean, distinct finish.

name: Branding SF
classification_notes: Spurless construction with medium-to-large x-height, rounded apertures and convex terminals. Not a geometric or humanist in the strict sense — sits between the two via its rounded, open forms and lack of spurs. Comparable territory to Avenir Next or Proxima Nova but with a softer, rounder personality.
summary: A spurless sans with rounded shapes and convex terminals, spanning seven weights across four widths for logotype and display work.
description: Branding SF extends Latinotype's original Branding design into a system of 56 styles covering standard, condensed, compressed and narrow widths, each with matching italics. The spurless construction, medium-large x-height and convex terminals give it a clean, friendly character that reads well at display sizes. Four alternate sets, old-style figures and support for 128 languages round out a family aimed squarely at identity and short-form typesetting.
foundry_blurb: Branding SF is a multi-style sans-serif built for versatility without losing its core character. Its spurless letterforms, rounded shapes and convex terminals span seven weights and four widths — standard, condensed, compressed and narrow — all with matching italics, 544 characters and support for 128 languages.

name: Breton
classification_notes: Geometric slab serif with a pronounced proportional contrast between rounded characters (o, c, e) and angular non-rounded ones (n, m, z). Ten weights from Hair to Black with matching italics; 20 styles total.
summary: A geometric slab with ten weights and matching italics, distinguished by deliberate proportional contrast between its wide rounded letters and narrower angular ones.
description: Breton is a geometric slab serif by Daniel Hernández and Rodrigo Fuenzalida, published by Latinotype in 2019. Its defining trait is the marked difference in width between round characters like 'o' and 'e' and their narrower counterparts like 'n' and 'z', producing an energetic visual rhythm at display sizes. With 20 styles across ten weights, matching italics and support for 200+ Latin-based languages, it handles headline and branding work capably.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Breton as inspired by Boston, with a strong personality built for headings and branding. The family's most distinctive trait is the contrast in proportions between rounded and non-rounded characters; each of the 20 styles covers more than 200 Latin-based languages across 417 glyphs.

name: Brocha
classification_notes: Humanist display sans-serif with a pronounced handmade quality. Letterforms draw on pre-Columbian visual language, giving the family an expressive, slightly irregular texture well suited to large-scale use. The Alt subfamily introduces alternate characters that increase variety within the same typographic voice.
summary: A handmade-feeling humanist display sans by Jorge Cisterna, rooted in pre-Columbian Easter Island art, spanning 32 styles across Basic and Alt subfamilies.
description: Brocha began as field sketches Cisterna made during a 2011 Easter Island visit, later refined into a polished display family released by Latinotype in 2015. The letterforms carry a warm, deliberately irregular quality that works well at headline and logotype scale. A parallel Alt subfamily doubles the palette, giving designers a wider range of expressive variants within the same typographic voice.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Brocha as a display sans with an expressive, highly humanist handmade look inspired by pre-Columbian art. Cisterna started the project with rough sketches drawn on Easter Island in 2011, refining them over years of practice while preserving their original Latin American character. The family runs across eight weights with italics in both Basic and Alt subfamilies, totalling 32 styles suited to headlines, logotypes and packaging.

name: Brutalista
classification_notes: Early twentieth-century grotesque and neo-grotesque roots. Medium x-height, low contrast, clear counterforms. Distinctive cuts in select characters add personality without breaking functional clarity. Includes Alt subfamily with alternate letterforms.
summary: A 28-style neo-grotesque by Jorge Cisterna drawing on early twentieth-century grotesque sources, with distinctive character cuts and an Alt subfamily offering alternate letterforms.
description: Brutalista is a neo-grotesque from Chilean designer Jorge Cisterna, referencing brutalist architecture's approach to raw material through a type lens. Medium x-height and low contrast give it broad range across headlines and informational settings. The Alt subfamily adds alternate letterforms, extending design flexibility without requiring a separate family.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by brutalist architecture's emphasis on raw material expression, Brutalista merges grotesque and neo-grotesque influences from the early twentieth century with a contemporary sensibility. Clear counterforms and low contrast underpin its versatility; peculiar cuts in select characters give it personality beyond the genre standard.

name: Cagliari
classification_notes: High-contrast modern serif blending Didone proportions with neo-Grotesk restraint. Derived from the Queulat design with amplified stroke contrast and abrupt thick-thin transitions. Pronounced teardrop terminals and minimalist letterform geometry place it firmly in the fashion-editorial Didone tradition.
summary: A high-contrast Didone display serif by Jorge Cisterna that tempers classical thick-thin drama with neo-Grotesk restraint, suited to fashion editorial and luxury brand identities.
description: Cagliari builds on the Queulat design, pushing stroke contrast further and sharpening the terminal details to produce a distinctly fashion-forward character. The neo-Grotesk influence keeps the letterforms clean without softening the drama of the thick-thin transitions. At 14 styles across seven weights, it covers display headlines, editorial headers and logotype work with consistent personality.
foundry_blurb: An elegant, easy-to-use typeface that marries the traditional flavour of Didone faces with the simplicity of Modern and neo-Grotesk design. Built on the Queulat foundation with higher stroke contrast and abrupt weight variations, Cagliari suits fashion magazines, literary publications and prestigious brand identities.

name: Camila
classification_notes: High-contrast Didone serif notable for its deliberate omission of teardrop terminals, a hallmark of the Bodoni–Didot tradition. In their place, thin serifs with soft finishes produce a cleaner, more contemporary silhouette. Contrast between thick stems and hairline strokes remains pronounced. Seven weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic.
summary: A delicate Didone serif from Chilean studio Latinotype, defined by its omission of teardrop terminals and available in seven weights with matching italics.
description: Designed by Paula Nazal Selaive and published in 2016, Camila departs from classical Didone convention by removing the teardrop terminals, leaving thin serifs with soft finishes that read as cleaner and more contemporary. Seven weights from Thin to Black, each paired with a true italic, give it genuine range from display headings to body copy. It suits editorial, fashion and brand identity work where a feminine high-contrast serif is called for.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Camila as a delicate and smooth Didone drawn from concepts of elegance, simplicity and femininity, with Coco Chanel as its primary point of reference. The family covers 426 characters and supports 206 languages.

name: Campeche
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque rooted in late 19th-century grotesque forms, inflected with a Latin American sensibility. Two optical variants (text and display) across three widths. Expressive character shapes that bend convention while remaining functional across both display and body-text contexts.
summary: A 54-style grotesque by Sofia Mohr that fuses late 19th-century forms with a Latin American character, spanning three widths and text and display variants.
description: Designed by Sofia Mohr and released in 2023, Campeche grows from grotesque type traditions of the late 1800s while bending their conventions with a distinctly Latin American playfulness. The family runs from condensed to expanded across nine weights, in both text and display versions, totalling 54 static fonts plus a variable. It suits packaging, editorial and branding work and its width range makes it well-suited for complex typographic systems that need hierarchy without losing visual coherence.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Campeche as a comprehensive typographic system built for contemporary design demands. The family draws on late 19th-century grotesque letterforms, giving them a Latin American freshness. It grew from an earlier typeface called Seriguela before evolving into a distinct identity, with multiple widths and the normal/display split enabling complex hierarchical systems within a single coherent voice.

name: Campeche Variable
classification_notes: 19th-century grotesque revival with Latin American character. Three-axis variable font (weight, width, display) available as a single variable file or 54 static variants across three widths (condensed, normal, extended) and two optical styles (text and display), each in nine weights.
summary: A three-axis variable grotesque by Sofia Mohr that fuses late 19th-century type forms with Latin American graphic sensibility across weight, width and display axes.
description: Campeche Variable draws on grotesque typefaces from the 1800s, filtered through the playful visual character of Latin American design. The system spans three axes – weight, width and display – encompassing 54 static combinations in the accompanying non-variable family, giving designers fine control over hierarchy within a single coherent system. It works well across packaging, editorial and branding applications where expressive type with structural discipline is needed.
foundry_blurb: Campeche is an expressive, functional family that departs from classic typographic convention where the design calls for it. Rooted in late 19th-century grotesques and shaped by a Latin American sense of personality, the design evolved from an earlier typeface called Seriguela into its own distinct system. Three variable axes – weight, width and display – allow designers to build graphic systems at different levels of hierarchy while keeping the family visually unified.

name: Canturiana
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif with Art Deco inflection, derived from Morris Fuller Benton's Canterbury (ATF, 1920s). Upright-only, five-weight family with an ornamental glyph set exceeding 1,000 characters including swashes, contextual alternates and ligatures. Intended for titles and short display text rather than extended body setting.
summary: A high-contrast Art Deco display serif drawn from Morris Fuller Benton's 1920s Canterbury, offering five weights and over a thousand glyphs including extensive swashes, alternates and ligatures.
description: Canturiana takes Morris Fuller Benton's 1920s Canterbury as its reference and translates it into a contemporary Art Deco idiom with sinuous curves, heightened contrast and a rich ornamental vocabulary. Designed by Daniel Hernández, Luciano Vergara and César Araya and released by Latinotype in 2022, the five-weight family covers over a thousand glyphs – swashes, alternates and ligatures included. It is built for titles, packaging and short-form display work rather than extended text setting.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Canturiana as carrying a romantic and musical air through sinuous construction and an Art Deco sensibility. The name comes from "canturía" – the Spanish term for the exercise of singing – framing the typeface as a typographic choir of contrasting qualities: classic and cool, disruptive and romantic, literary and musical.
designer: Daniel Hernández, Luciano Vergara, César Araya

name: Catrina
classification_notes: Display slab serif with expressive letterforms balancing geometric construction and organic curves; ships with a companion Handmade variant, catchwords and dingbats across 14 styles total.
summary: A slab-display family from Chilean foundry Latinotype, spanning six weights with a rougher handmade companion set, catchwords and dingbats for packaging, branding and title work.
description: Designed by Eli Hernández and released in 2017, Catrina pairs clean slab serif letterforms against a rougher handmade variant across six weights from Thin to Black. The 14-style family adds catchwords and dingbats, making it a self-contained toolkit for expressive branding and advertising. Its balance of geometric precision and organic warmth gives it a distinctive character in display contexts.
