foundry_blurb: An expressive typeface whose curves and straight lines meet in harmonious synchrony, suited to packaging, branding, titles and advertising.

name: Chakai
classification_notes: A contemporary glyphic serif with softened, barely bracketed serifs and controlled stroke contrast, sitting in the territory between traditional serif and sans-serif. The defined horizontal strokes recall optical faces like Optima but with a more editorial, high-contrast sensibility. Two subfamilies (Chakai and Chakai Alt) offer alternate letterforms within the same design language.
summary: A contemporary glyphic serif with softened serifs, controlled contrast and seven weights across two subfamilies, designed for editorial and branding work.
description: Chakai sits between serif and sans-serif, with reduced stroke contrast, soft serifs and defined horizontal strokes that keep it readable in long text and distinctive at display sizes. The Alt subfamily provides alternate letterforms for additional typographic variety. Seven weights, each with a matching italic, cover complex layouts from packaging headlines through to extended editorial copy.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Chakai as "a well seasoned typeface with a touch of spice" built on a balance of brightness, subtlety and functionality. Its soft serifs and defined horizontal strokes provide visual stability across weights, and the range of styles makes it suitable for logos, packaging and editorial design alike.

name: Cinema
classification_notes: Condensed serif display face with strong vertical stress and precise serif construction. Drawn from vintage Chilean magazine typography of 1941 and theatrical marquee lettering traditions. The condensed proportion is the primary design — not a variant — with nine weights from Thin to Black.
summary: A condensed serif display face with nine weights, drawing on vintage Chilean editorial design from 1941 and theatrical marquee lettering.
description: Cinema is a condensed serif built for headlines, posters and editorial layouts, with a strong vertical presence and precisely drawn serifs. Its concept references the bold type of Chilean magazines from 1941 and the lettering of stage and cinema marquees, giving it a specific cultural grounding. Nine weights from Thin to Black provide good range for display hierarchies.
foundry_blurb: Cinema is a condensed serif with the flair of the stage and the charisma of vintage marquee lettering, drawing inspiration from the bold editorial design of Chilean magazines from 1941. It is engineered for contemporary media — headlines, branding, posters, covers and audiovisual projects — blending nostalgic theatrical aesthetics with modern typographic discipline.

name: Clasica Sans
classification_notes: Contemporary humanist sans-serif built on classical Roman letter proportions. Balanced stroke contrast across the weight range makes it equally at home in body text and display settings. Seven weights from Thin to Ultra Black, each with a matching italic.
summary: A fourteen-style humanist sans-serif by Enrique Hernández, grounded in classical proportions and designed for publishing work across both text and display sizes.
description: Clasica Sans draws on classical Roman letter proportions to produce a contemporary sans-serif with balanced contrast throughout the weight range. Seven weights from Thin to Ultra Black, each with a matching italic, give it enough range for editorial systems that need consistency from body copy to headline. Solid and competent rather than distinctive, it holds up well in print contexts at any scale.
foundry_blurb: Clasica Sans is a fresh, contemporary typeface built on classical proportions. The family spans 7 weights with italics – 14 styles in total – covering everything from body text to display headlines. Balanced contrast and consistent construction make it a reliable choice for publishing and print design, performing well at small and large sizes alike.

name: Clasica Slab
classification_notes: Humanist slab serif drawing structural proportions from Optima — notably thin vertical strokes — with the addition of even, symmetrical serifs. Low contrast overall, with a geometric quality to the serif treatment that distinguishes it from bracketed oldstyle slabs. Alternate glyphs for a, e, f, g, r and y introduce mild typographic variety.
summary: A nine-weight humanist slab serif by Enrique Hernández, taking Optima's thin vertical strokes as its starting point and adding symmetrical serifs to produce a grounded, editorial-ready family.
description: Designed by Enrique Hernández and published by Latinotype in 2014, Clasica Slab borrows the proportions and fine vertical strokes of Optima and applies even, symmetrical serifs that push the tone towards something more structured and print-friendly. Nine weights from Thin to UltraBlack, each with a matching italic, give it a practical range across headline and text settings. Alternate glyphs for a, e, f, g, r and y allow quiet typographic variation within a single family.
foundry_blurb: Clasica Slab is defined by the contrast between its thin vertical strokes and its symmetrical, even serifs — an approach that takes Optima as its reference point while carving out a distinct slab identity. The family spans nine weights with italics, covering light display use through to heavy editorial titling. Alternate character forms for several common letters add a further layer of flexibility for detailed typographic work.

name: Comalle
classification_notes: Organic display face with handwritten script influence. Deliberately heavy strokes prioritise counter space craft over letterform construction – the whites are where the design precision lives. Single-weight release; no italic, condensed or extended variants.
summary: A single-weight organic display face built around counter space: Juan Pablo De Gregorio designed its heavy letterforms as vessels for precisely crafted whites rather than ends in themselves.
description: Comalle draws on handwritten script traditions without following any calligraphic ruleset, giving it an expressive brush quality suited strictly to display use. The stroke weight is deliberately heavy, intended to fill the page fast, with the real craft invested in the counter spaces. As a single-weight release, its application is narrow – headlines and logotypes at large sizes where the tension between dense black forms and deliberate white space can register.
foundry_blurb: Comalle is an organic typeface that rescues elements of handwritten script without adhering to a strict calligraphic structure. Its strokes are heavier than its counter forms, designed to fill the page and create immediate visual impact. The precision of the design lives in the white space rather than the letterforms themselves, aiming to enchant through delicate counter space while making an impact through heavy outlines.

name: Consuelo
classification_notes: Casual brush script with four textural variants (Regular, Rough, Shadow, Shadow Two), each paired with an italic, plus an ornaments set. Designed for display use at headline and logotype scale.
summary: A brush-stroke script in nine variants – Regular, Rough and two Shadow treatments, each with an italic, plus ornaments – suited to logotypes, headlines and short advertising copy.
description: Consuelo is a casual brush script by Eli Hernández, released through Latinotype in 2014. The family earns its keep through range: four distinct textural treatments (Regular, Rough, Shadow, Shadow Two) each paired with an italic give designers options within a single cohesive hand. An ornaments set extends it further for editorial and branding use.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by brush strokes, Consuelo is built for decorative titles, short phrases, magazines, logotypes and advertising. The family comprises four variants – each with a companion italic – and a set of ornaments.

name: Cookery
classification_notes: Hand-drawn brush pen script with an irregular baseline. Single weight. Extensive OpenType alternate set including automatic connected/disconnected letterform switching, swashes, initial and terminal forms, and old style figures.
summary: A single-weight hand-drawn brush pen script by Sofia Mohr, with an irregular baseline and a generous OpenType alternate set suited to food packaging, menus and display logotypes.
description: Cookery is a brush pen script with 613 characters and a thorough OpenType feature set, including letters that automatically switch between connected and disconnected forms, swashes, and initial and terminal variants. The irregular baseline gives it a convincingly hand-lettered quality. Its application is squarely in display contexts – packaging, restaurant menus, invitation cards, book covers – where the alternates can be drawn on to vary rhythm and avoid repetition.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary, friendly and authentic hand-drawn brush pen typeface with an irregular baseline. Suited to book covers, logotypes, packaging, restaurant menus, invitation cards and advertising, with an extensive alternate character set for a natural, playful and individual look.

name: Cordillera
classification_notes: Geometric/neo-grotesque hybrid with classic proportions. Pairs clean rational structure with subtle humanist warmth. Ships as two complementary subfamilies: the standard Cordillera for neutral text applications and Cordillera Alt with alternative characters for more expressive display use. Thirty-six styles total across both families.
summary: A clean corporate sans-serif from Chilean foundry Latinotype, blending geometric and neo-grotesque forms across 36 styles in two complementary subfamilies.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara in 2023, Cordillera pairs classic proportions with geometric and neo-grotesque character forms, positioned for branding, editorial and digital work. The Alt subfamily provides alternative glyphs that shift the tone between expressive headline and neutral body text within a single system. At 36 styles from Thin to Black with italics throughout, the family offers solid coverage for corporate and interface applications.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Cordillera as clear, simple and multipurpose – a sans-serif that combines classic proportions with geometric and neo-grotesque characters. The Alt subfamily's alternative characters let designers move between expressive headlines and neutral body text while keeping the system visually coherent.

name: Corporative
designer: Javier Quintana, César Araya, Bruno Jara, Luciano Vergara, Daniel Hernández
classification_notes: Semi-serif construction bridges sans and serif traditions: letterforms carry subtle stroke terminations and modest contrast that add warmth without adopting bracketed or wedge serifs. Proportions are naturally condensed across all subfamilies, making the family feel compact even in its standard width. Closer to a humanist sans with calligraphic finishing details than to a true serif family.
summary: A 64-style semi-serif family with standard, alternate and condensed subfamilies, designed by the Latinotype team for corporate branding and display work across 128 languages.
description: Corporative was the first typeface released by the Latinotype team, built to combine personality with practical breadth across print, branding and web applications. Its semi-serif construction gives letterforms a warm, slightly calligraphic presence without committing to full serifs, and the naturally condensed proportions keep it useful in tighter layouts. Four subfamilies – Corporative, Alt, Condensed and Alt Condensed – each span eight weights with italics, bringing the total to 64 fonts and 350-plus characters covering 128 languages.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Corporative as their first team release – a semi-serif with marked personality suited to large display sizes, whose condensed proportions also make it workable at smaller settings. The family spans four subfamilies across eight weights each, with a 350-character set covering 128 languages and supporting both desktop and webfont use.

name: Corporative Sans
classification_notes: Condensed sans-serif with four subfamilies: standard, Alt (alternative letterforms), Condensed and Condensed Alt. Eight weights from Hair to Black, all with matching italics, totalling 64 styles. Personality sits between display and workhorse text use. Developed under supervision of Vergara and Hernández by Javier Quintana, Rodrigo Fuenzalida and César Araya.
summary: A 64-style condensed sans-serif from Latinotype with four subfamilies including Alt variants, eight weights with matching italics throughout, and 128-language support.
description: Designed in 2015 by Luciano Vergara and Daniel Hernández with the Latinotype team, Corporative Sans is the sans companion to the foundry's flagship Corporative family. Its four subfamilies – standard, Alt, Condensed and Condensed Alt – share eight weights from Hair to Black, each with italics, giving 64 styles to deploy across headline and body contexts. The Alt cuts introduce alternative letterforms that add a degree of differentiation within the same structural system.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Corporative Sans as having marked personality and distinctive traits suited to display use at large sizes, with condensed proportions that keep it practical at smaller settings. The family ships with 350 characters covering 128 languages, and its four subfamilies are designed to be mixed, letting designers combine widths and alternate letterform sets within a single visual system.

name: Corporative Sans Rounded
designer: Luciano Vergara, Daniel Hernández, Elizabeth Hernández, Rodrigo Fuenzalida
classification_notes: Rounded variant of Corporative Sans with consistently curved terminals throughout. Shares the same structural DNA as its parent family — neutral, corporate skeleton — but the rounded treatment softens it into friendlier territory. Available in 32 styles (8 weights plus italics in a standard and an alternate subfamily). A separate Condensed family also exists. Suited to both display and running text sizes.
summary: A rounded-terminal companion to Corporative Sans, offered in 32 styles with 350 characters covering 128 languages, aimed squarely at branding and packaging.
description: Corporative Sans Rounded takes the neutral corporate structure of Corporative Sans and applies curved terminals throughout, softening the personality without sacrificing the weight range – Hair to Black – needed for serious brand use. The family ships in 32 styles across a standard and an alternate subfamily, both with full italic coverage. The 350-character set supporting 128 languages makes it a practical choice for international brand identity work.
foundry_blurb: Corporative Sans Rounded adds curved terminals to the Corporative Sans structure, giving the face a friendly character while keeping it functional at both display and text sizes. The family includes 350 characters covering 128 languages, and is well suited to logotypes, posters, signage, branding and packaging.

name: Corporative Sans Rounded Condensed
classification_notes: Condensed variant of Corporative Sans Rounded. Softened terminals and rounded stroke endings throughout. Narrow proportions with a relatively low x-height by display-grotesque standards. Consistent stroke contrast typical of a geometric-influenced design. Alt subfamily provides alternate letterforms for the same weights.
summary: A 32-style condensed rounded sans from Latinotype, built for tight-spaced layouts where warmth from softened terminals is still wanted.
description: Corporative Sans Rounded Condensed is the narrow variant of Corporative Sans Rounded, designed for logotypes, packaging and signage where horizontal space is at a premium. Eight weights run from Hair to Black, each with a matching italic, and an Alt subfamily provides alternate letterforms across the same range. A 350-character set gives coverage across 128 languages, making it a practical choice for multilingual Latin-script projects.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes this as the narrowed version of Corporative Sans Rounded, offering high performance in text setting. The condensed proportions make it suited to logotypes, posters, signs, branding and packaging, performing well at both display and small sizes.

name: Corporative Slab
classification_notes: Slab serif companion to the Corporative sans-serif family. Thick rectangular terminals applied to the same rounded stroke structure as the parent design, keeping visual coherence between the two. Consistent stroke weight across the range. Designed primarily for display but readable at small sizes.
summary: A slab serif companion to Corporative, spanning eight weights from Hair to Black with matching italics and thick terminals that hold up at both headline scale and small sizes.
description: Designed by César Araya and released by Latinotype in 2020, Corporative Slab takes the rounded strokes and proportions of the Corporative sans-serif family and adds thick slab terminals for a more assertive character. The 16-style family pairs each of its eight weights with a matching italic, covering logos, posters, packaging and editorial applications without stretching too thin. A 350-character set supports over 200 Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Corporative Slab as the slab serif counterpart to their Corporative family, preserving the original main strokes and rounded edges to maintain coherence between the two. The thick terminals give it a strong, distinctive voice, while the breadth of the weight range makes it appropriate for large-scale display work as well as smaller-size use.

name: Corporative Soft
designer: Javier Quintana, Eli Hernández, Rodrigo Fuenzalida
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with uniformly softened, rounded terminals throughout. Structurally derived from Corporative but distinctly warmer in character. Consistent stroke modulation, clean axes, and a large x-height make it well-suited to display and branding contexts. Four subfamilies (standard, alternate, condensed, condensed alternate) share the same rounded construction.
summary: A rounded geometric sans-serif – the softer sibling of Corporative – spanning 64 styles across standard, alternate and condensed subfamilies with broad multilingual coverage.
description: Corporative Soft takes the structural geometry of Corporative and rounds its terminals, giving the design a warmer, more approachable quality without losing its corporate clarity. The family spans four subfamilies – standard, alternate, condensed and condensed alternate – each in eight weights with matching italics, totalling 64 styles. With 350 characters covering 128 languages, it's built for branding, packaging and display work at scale.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Corporative Soft as the rounded companion to Corporative, with the smooth transition from straight to curved lines lending a friendlier feel while preserving the face's marked personality and suitability for large sizes. The foundry positions it for logos, posters, signs, branding and packaging.

name: Courtney
classification_notes: Unicase display with thick, irregular strokes and a grunge-western aesthetic. Four styles across two variants: a clean version and a rougher textured version, each with italic. Ligature-heavy with dedicated connector characters for editorial composition.
summary: A unicase display face with thick, irregular strokes and a grunge-western character, built for logos, posters and short editorial use.
description: Courtney comes in two variants – a clean cut and a rougher textured version – each with an italic, giving four styles in total. It carries an extensive ligature set alongside dedicated connector characters such as "and", "the" and "by" to help build tight typographic lockups. The unicase structure and roughened aesthetic make it best suited to headline and logo work at large sizes.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Courtney as a unicase display font with thick and irregular strokes, supported by a varied set of ligatures and a collection of connector characters. They position it as ideal for short texts, magazine layouts and logos.

name: Couturier
classification_notes: High-contrast Didone with vertical stress and hairline serifs drawn from 18th-century models. True italics with humanist characteristics distinguish it from strictly mechanical Didone designs.
summary: A high-contrast Didone serif by Diego Maldonado, grounded in 18th-century models with true humanist italics, swashes and ornamental ligatures for editorial and luxury work.
description: Couturier draws on 18th-century Didone letterforms, redrawn with a contemporary sensibility to suit fashion editorial, high-end branding and publishing. The family spans four weights with true humanist italics, backed by swashes, ornamental ligatures and alternative glyphs. Language coverage reaches more than 200 languages across 1,200+ characters.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype pitch Couturier as a haute couture solution for premium type work, built on precisely drawn curves and well-balanced counterforms. The design's ornamental ligatures, alternative glyphs and decorative swashes are positioned as ready-to-use tools for editorial, publishing and luxury branding projects.

name: Couturier Poster
classification_notes: High-contrast Didone with 18th-century proportions; elevated thick-thin stroke contrast relative to the text-weight companion Couturier; optimised for display, headline and poster settings with a 1,248-character set including swashes, ligatures, small caps and alternates
summary: High-contrast Didone designed for large-scale use: six weights with matching italics, swashes, ligatures and small caps across 200-plus Latin languages.
description: Couturier Poster is the display companion to Latinotype's Couturier, built with greater stroke contrast for headline and poster settings. Designed by Diego Maldonado and released in 2019, it spans six weights from Thin to Black, each with matching italics, plus swashes, ligatures, small caps and alternates. Coverage extends to more than 200 Latin-derived languages.
foundry_blurb: Couturier Poster takes the original Couturier and pushes the contrast higher, expanding the family from eight to twelve styles optimised for large sizes. It pairs naturally with Couturier for body text and can sit anywhere between restrained and characterful depending on how it is used, with more than 200 languages covered.

name: Cover Sans
classification_notes: Humanist geometric sans-serif with an orthogonal structure and condensed proportions. Low x-height and open apertures distinguish it from purer geometric designs. Alternative characters add personality without departing from the geometric framework.
summary: A humanist geometric sans with condensed proportions and low x-height, available in seven weights with matching italics for editorial and identity use.
description: Cover Sans pairs geometric construction with humanist sensibilities, built around an orthogonal structure that provides compositional stability while open apertures keep text readable at smaller sizes. The low x-height lends it a refined quality suited to magazine headlines and annual report settings. Seven weights from Thin to Heavy each ship with a matching italic, making it a practical choice for extended editorial systems.
foundry_blurb: Cover Sans is a humanist geometric typeface with an orthogonal structure that provides stability in text composition. Its open shapes and low x-height give it balance and an air-breathing quality. Latinotype designed it with magazines, publishing, annual reports and business logotypes in mind, with alternative characters giving it a modern, elegant personality.

name: Cringe Gothic
designer: Luciano Vergara, Jorge Cisterna, Daniel Hernández, Ale Navarro
classification_notes: Post-cringe grotesque with deliberately awkward terminals, wide apertures and exaggerated letterforms; compact proportions give it functional range beyond display use despite its expressive character
summary: A post-cringe grotesque with deliberately awkward terminals, wide apertures and eight weights designed for expressive branding with an internet-native sensibility.
description: Cringe Gothic leans into intentional imperfection, with exaggerated letterforms and terminals that deliberately break typographic convention. Eight weights – Thin to Heavy, each with a matching italic – give it genuine functional range despite its display-first DNA. Aimed at brands that prefer the off-kilter to the polished, it draws on contemporary internet culture without tipping into self-parody.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype pitches Cringe Gothic as a grotesk with a wink – wide apertures, quirky terminals and exaggerated forms that embody a post-cringe aesthetic. Made for brands that would rather appear vulnerable than flawless, it treats deliberate imperfection as a kind of honesty rather than a shortcoming.

name: Culinary
subcategory: Themed decorative display system with script
classification_notes: A multi-subfamily thematic display system comprising a four-weight decorative serif, a matching four-weight calligraphic script, a hairline/outline (Line) variant across both, a sans in Line only and an ornamental borders/dingbat component. OpenType features include ligatures, swashes, oldstyle figures, and initial/terminal alternates. Unified by a food and cooking aesthetic throughout.
summary: A ten-style typographic system by Sofia Mohr built around a culinary theme, pairing a decorative serif, a calligraphic script and a sans across matched weights with an ornamental borders component.
description: Culinary is a 2016 thematic display system from Latinotype, grouping a four-weight decorative serif, a matching four-weight script, a sans line variant and an ornamental borders component under a single food-and-cooking identity. Sofia Mohr loaded the system with OpenType swashes, ligatures, oldstyle figures and initial/terminal alternates to give it expressive range. The brief is narrow – restaurant and café branding, menus, packaging, recipe books – and the design rarely steps outside it.
foundry_blurb: A typographic system inspired by the art of cooking, shipping as two core subfamilies – a four-weight display serif with a line variant and a borders set, alongside a matching four-weight script with its own line style. Built for packaging, restaurant and café branding, bakeries, logos, magazines, menus, recipe books and invitations.

name: D Sari
classification_notes: Neo-humanist sans-serif with rounded forms and apexed characters. Less pointed than classic neo-humanist models, which gives it a warmer, more approachable feel while retaining structural rigour. Moderate contrast. Eleven-weight range with matching italics for 22 styles total.
summary: A neo-humanist sans-serif with eleven weights and matching italics, built around rounded forms and apexed characters that temper the genre's usual austerity.
description: Designed by Diego Aravena Silo in 2014, D Sari takes the structural logic of neo-humanist sans-serifs and softens it with rounded shapes and less pointed apexes, producing a family that reads as approachable without losing precision. The 22 styles, spanning Thin to UltraBlack each with a paired italic, give it enough range for both headline and body use. It performs well in advertising, editorial and motion graphics contexts where a contemporary sans with some warmth is needed.
foundry_blurb: A dynamic sans-serif family rooted in neo-humanist traditions, combining rounded shapes, apexed characters and restrained contrast. Less pointed than most neo-humanist typefaces, it suits prominent lettering, magazines, motion graphics, advertising, logotypes and signage.

name: D Sert
classification_notes: Geometric display sans rooted in Chilean constructivism. The standard version has expressive diagonal strokes and bowls that project above cap height, giving it a calligraphic quality. The Alt version systematises the diagonals and aligns bowls to cap height for a cleaner read. Both share the same 11-weight range with italics. Based on designer Diego Aravena's earlier Pirata face.
summary: A 47-style display super family drawn from 1970s Chilean constructivist poster art, with capitals whose bowls break above the cap line for an unusual calligraphic tension.
description: D Sert takes its design language from the political propaganda posters of Chile's La Unidad Popular movement, translating that constructivist graphic energy into a geometric sans with an expressive edge. The family ships in two main versions: the standard cut, where diagonal strokes are freely expressive and capital bowls project above cap height; and the Alt, where both are reined in for a more systematic, composed result. Three Extra variants round out a 47-style system spanning Thin to UltraBlack with italics, giving the face more range than its display classification might suggest.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions D Sert as a meeting point between Chilean graphic art revival and contemporary type thinking – drawing directly from 1970s constructivist design and the political poster work of La Unidad Popular, then pairing that historical reference with the handmade movement and super font family conventions. Two distinct versions handle diagonals and capital proportions differently, offering a choice between expressive and systematic interpretations of the same concept.

name: D.I.Y. Time
classification_notes: A multi-style hand-drawn type system of 11 fonts spanning organic brush and ink letterforms through to a constructed sans informed by Gill's classical proportions and a matching slab. All styles share a handmade aesthetic as their unifying thread. The family extends into catchwords, ornaments and dingbats, making it a self-contained craft display system.
summary: A hand-lettered type system of 11 styles spanning organic brush and ink letterforms to Gill-proportioned sans and slab variants, unified by a handmade craft philosophy.
description: D.I.Y. Time pairs expressive brush and ink styles with a constructed sans shaped by Gill's classical proportions and a matching slab, all sharing the same hand-drawn origins. Designed by Luciano Vergara and Guisela Mendoza for Latinotype in 2014, the family extends to catchwords, ornaments and dingbats for decorative typesetting. The concept is deliberately narrow – craft and artisan work – which limits its range but keeps it coherent within that lane.
foundry_blurb: D.I.Y. Time is a hand-drawn type system born from the global DIY counterculture, built for those who value handwork and attention to materials and process. Drawn with various brushes and pens on paper, the family mixes organic expressive styles with references to the classical proportions of Gill, spanning ink, brush, sans and slab variants alongside catchwords, ornaments and dingbats.

name: Dans Le Cuisine
classification_notes: Single-weight ornamental dingbat set containing 67 kitchen-themed pictograms assigned across the character set. Not a text typeface in any conventional sense. Visual style draws on mid-century Chilean print ephemera. Part of a series of themed dingbat sets by Guisela Mendoza, including Dans le Toilette, Dans le Jardin and Dans le Noël.
summary: A single-weight dingbat set by Guisela Mendoza containing 67 kitchen-themed pictograms drawn from the aesthetic of 1960s Chilean cooking magazines.
description: Dans Le Cuisine is a pictogram font rather than a text face, mapping 67 illustrated kitchen objects across the character set. The drawings take their cues from mid-century Chilean print ephemera, giving the set a warm, hand-crafted quality that reads as decorative. It belongs to a series of themed dingbat sets by Mendoza alongside Dans le Toilette, Dans le Jardin and Dans le Noël.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by the wild curves, flavours and experimentation of 1960s Chilean cooking magazines, the set gathers 67 kitchen-themed pictograms into a single decorative font.

name: Dans Le Jardin
classification_notes: Single-weight ornamental dingbat; all glyphs are decorative floral and curvilinear symbols rather than letterforms. Companion piece to Dans Le Cuisine from the same designer.
summary: A single-weight ornamental dingbat of floral and curvilinear symbols with a vintage character, released as a companion to the Dans Le Cuisine set.
description: Dans Le Jardin is a dingbat font by Guisela Mendoza, published by Latinotype in 2012 as a companion to Dans Le Cuisine. The glyphs are entirely decorative — floral and organic forms with expressive, vintage-inflected curves rather than text characters. Its one weight is suited to pattern-making, poster illustration and decorative composition work.
foundry_blurb: A continuation of the Dans Le Cuisine dingbat, offering wild, expressive curves with a distinctive vintage character. The symbols are designed for building patterns and compositions in posters, websites and print.

name: Dans Le Noël
classification_notes: A pictographic dingbat in which all glyphs are Christmas-themed ornamental symbols rather than letterforms. Display is the closest available schema category. Part of the Dans series alongside Dans Le Cuisine and Dans Le Jardin.
summary: A single-weight Christmas dingbat by Guisela Mendoza, swapping letterforms for festive ornamental pictograms drawn from vintage illustration.
description: Dans Le Noël replaces standard glyphs with Christmas-themed pictograms drawn from vintage illustration traditions, designed for seasonal cards, patterns and decorative layouts. Released by Latinotype in 2012, it is part of the Dans series alongside Dans Le Cuisine and Dans Le Jardin, with the three fonts intended to mix and match. With a single weight and no letterforms, its application is narrow by design.
foundry_blurb: A Christmas dingbat built to bring character to seasonal work. The pictographic glyphs draw on vintage illustration and sit alongside the other Dans series fonts for coordinated use across cards, patterns, posters and digital compositions.

name: Dans Le Toilette
classification_notes: Symbol/dingbat font composed entirely of vintage-style illustrations; single weight; no alphabetic characters; part of a thematic domestic dingbat series.
summary: A single-weight dingbat font of vintage bathroom-themed illustrations, part of Latinotype's domestic dingbat series.
description: Dans Le Toilette is a novelty dingbat font by Guisela Mendoza, filled with vintage-style illustrations drawn from the morning bathroom routine. It belongs to a thematic series alongside Dans le cuisine, Dans le jardin and Dans le Noël, each covering a different domestic setting. Suited to posters, patterns and decorative branding where retro illustrative character is the point rather than legible text.
foundry_blurb: A fun dingbat inspired by things that happen fast in the bathroom every morning, designed for use on posters, covers, patterns, brands and anything calling for a vintage touch.

name: Darwin
classification_notes: Eclectic sans-serif that combines grotesque, geometric and humanist influences with DIN-adjacent character. Comes in two subfamilies: Normal (conventional) and Alt (stylistic alternates for added visual variety). Primarily a display face for headlines and short copy rather than running text.
summary: Darwin blends grotesque, geometric and humanist influences across 20 styles, with an Alt subfamily designed to add character to headline and poster work.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara and released in 2014, Darwin pairs a conventional Normal subfamily with an Alt that offers stylistic alternates for compositions needing more personality. The family runs from Extra Light to Black with italics throughout, covering headline, poster and logo work. It draws on vintage grotesque and DIN-adjacent references without committing fully to either tradition.
foundry_blurb: Darwin is an eclectic assembly of grotesque, geometric and humanistic styles, built for headlines, short text, posters and logos. The Alt subfamily adds a layer of visual interest to compositions.

name: Darwin Office
classification_notes: A streamlined Office-compatibility adaptation of Darwin, which itself blends grotesque, geometric and humanist influences. Darwin Office uses weight names specifically chosen to display correctly in Microsoft Office font menus. The bold is deliberately heavier than its counterpart in the standard Darwin family to ensure legible hierarchy in the font picker. Ships as two four-style subfamilies: Darwin Office and Darwin Alt Office.
summary: Darwin Office is a stripped-down, Office-ready adaptation of the Darwin grotesque-humanist sans, with weight names engineered for clean hierarchy in Microsoft Word and PowerPoint font menus.
description: Developed by Los Andes Type and published through Latinotype, Darwin Office reduces the broader Darwin family to eight styles across two subfamilies, each weight named to sit legibly within Office's font picker. The bold is noticeably heavier than its counterpart in the full Darwin range, ensuring clear typographic hierarchy where the software's UI imposes its own constraints. For anything outside Office workflows, the parent Darwin family offers considerably more range and character.
foundry_blurb: Darwin Office is an adapted version of the Darwin font for use in Microsoft Office, with font weights named to display clearly in Office program font lists for good hierarchy. The bold variant is heavier than in the original Darwin. The family ships as two subfamilies, Darwin Office and Darwin Alt Office, each in four styles.

name: Darwin Pro
classification_notes: Hybrid sans that blends grotesque, geometric and humanist traditions. Open apertures, sturdy stroke contrast and optically grounded proportions. The Pro version was completely redrawn from the original Darwin, with new figures and an expanded character set while preserving the eclectic multi-influence construction.
summary: A fully redrawn sequel to Darwin, merging grotesque, geometric and humanist influences across seven weights with italic companions, oldstyle figures and extended language coverage.
description: Darwin Pro is a sans-serif published in 2017 through Latinotype by Chilean studio Los Andes Type. The family spans seven weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, and includes OpenType alternates, oldstyle figures, numerators and denominators. It suits editorial, branding and advertising work where a confident, multi-reference contemporary sans is needed.
foundry_blurb: Darwin Pro is the sequel to Darwin, completely redrawn with extended language support and a new figure set. Building on the original's mix of grotesque, geometric and humanist references, it offers fourteen styles across seven weights with OpenType alternates and oldstyle numerals.

name: Darwin Rounded
classification_notes: Geometric construction with condensed proportions and softened, rounded terminals. Features an abrupt transition from curve to straight line alongside subtle calligraphic and humanist influences carried over from the original Darwin. Three subfamilies – Pro, Essential and Essential Alt – share the same seven-weight range with italics throughout.
summary: A rounded geometric sans by Luciano Vergara that builds on his original Darwin, offering 42 styles across three subfamilies with condensed proportions and softened terminals.
description: Darwin Rounded follows on from the original Darwin with rounded terminals, condensed proportions and a subtle calligraphic undercurrent inherited from its predecessor. Three subfamilies – Pro, Essential and Essential Alt – each run from Thin to Black with matching italics, giving the family genuine range. OpenType features include oldstyle figures and alternate characters, suiting it to editorial, branding and display work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Darwin Rounded as the resequel to their original Darwin family, bringing updated language support, reworked figure sets and a softer terminal treatment across all 42 styles.

name: Decour
classification_notes: Low-contrast slab serif with Art Deco-derived proportions. Exaggerated cap-to-x-height ratio gives it strong display presence. Seven weights in standard and condensed widths, all with italics. OpenType features include small caps, alternates and ligatures; 364 glyphs per style.
summary: A low-contrast Art Deco slab serif with a strongly pronounced cap-to-x-height ratio, spanning seven weights in both standard and condensed widths with matching italics.
description: Decour takes its proportions from Art Deco type traditions – geometric slab serifs with minimal stroke contrast and a pronounced height difference between uppercase and lowercase letters. That case contrast drives its display character, making it well-suited to headings and subheadings. Twenty-eight styles across standard and condensed widths give it useful range for publishing and retail applications.
foundry_blurb: Decour is a slab serif whose proportions draw from Art Deco design, featuring low contrast between thick and thin strokes. The pronounced height difference between uppercase and lowercase letters makes it expressive at display sizes, particularly in headings and subheadings, with applications that extend to publishing and retail.

name: Decour Soft
classification_notes: Rounded-terminal slab serif with humanist proportions and low overall contrast. Art Deco influence appears in the pronounced height differential between upper and lowercase letters. Soft variant of the original Decour family, trading sharp slab terminals for rounded ones to produce a warmer, more approachable character.
summary: A rounded-terminal slab from Jorge Cisterna that softens Decour's Art Deco structure with humanist proportions and warm curves across seven weights.
description: Decour Soft takes the slab serif bones of the original Decour and rounds every terminal, producing a friendlier face without abandoning the low contrast and humanist proportions underneath. An Art Deco-inflected size difference between capitals and lowercase gives it some visual tension that stops it reading as purely casual. Seven weights with matching italics make it usable across logotypes, packaging and editorial subheadings.
foundry_blurb: Decour Soft is the rounded-edge version of Decour – a humanist slab serif with low contrast and strong curves that give it a warm, approachable character. It retains Decour's Art Deco-influenced proportions, including the pronounced difference in scale between upper and lowercase letters. Latinotype positions it for logotypes, packaging and book or magazine titles.

name: Diploma Script
classification_notes: Copperplate-influenced calligraphic script with brush pen construction applied to the letterforms. Single weight issued in two feature tiers (Basic and Pro); the Pro adds contextual alternates for initial, medial and terminal positions. Accompanied by a dedicated Ornaments companion font.
summary: A Copperplate-influenced calligraphic script by Marcelo Quiroz that fuses formal pen letterforms with brush pen technique, suited to invitations, certificates and logotypes.
description: Diploma Script takes Copperplate as its structural starting point and applies brush pen construction to arrive at letterforms that are formal without being rigid. The Pro cut adds contextual alternates at initial, medial and terminal positions, giving fine control over the rhythm of connected text. The family ships with a companion Ornaments set and covers 900+ characters across more than 200 languages – unusually broad coverage for a calligraphic script.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Diploma Script as born from merging classic calligraphy with contemporary tools, using Copperplate style as the structural foundation and blending in brush pen drawing techniques to balance elegance with readability.

name: Domi
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif drawing on 20th-century typographic rationalism. Closed apertures, straight cut terminals, restrained stroke modulation, and strong weight contrast from Thin to Black. Structural clarity in both uppercase and the geometrically constructed lowercase. No condensed or extended subfamily.
summary: A well-resolved geometric sans-serif by Daniel Hernández, built on rationalist principles with closed apertures, straight terminals, and a nine-weight range that earns its keep across branding, editorial and signage work.
description: Domi is a geometric sans-serif rooted in 20th-century typographic rationalism, with closed forms, straight-cut terminals and restrained stroke modulation that give it a confident, architectural tone. Its nine weights span Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, making it versatile across hierarchies without feeling generic. The geometrically constructed lowercase and firm capitals translate well across industrial, fashion, cultural and identity applications.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Domi as a straightforward sans-serif defined by the contrast between its extreme weights and its emphasis on counterform rhythm. The closed apertures and straight terminals produce a confident character suited to typographic hierarchies and dense text alike, while its rationalist geometry adapts to identity, signage and editorial contexts.

name: Dulce
classification_notes: Single-weight swash display face with monoline thin strokes that swell and thicken at terminal points. Extensive OpenType ligature support (standard and discretionary) and an ornamental glyph set. Bridges the aesthetic gap between a classic swash face and a decorative script without adopting a slanted axis.
summary: A single-weight swash display face by Paula Nazal Selaive, built around strokes that swell at their terminals, an extensive ligature set and ornamental glyphs for headline and logotype use.
description: Dulce's thin strokes thicken wherever two terminals meet, lending the letterforms a quality that sits between a classic swash face and a decorative script. Its OpenType feature set centres on ligatures – both standard and discretionary – alongside ornamental glyphs including hearts, flowers, banners and frames. Best suited to short display settings where a romantic, feminine register is needed: editorial headlines, logotypes, packaging.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Dulce as a swash typeface with an elegant and romantic touch, noting that its thin strokes thicken where terminals meet and swell at their endpoints. They recommend it for magazines, logotypes and advertising, pointing to its extensive ligature collection – activated through standard and discretionary ligature settings – as the feature that makes it adaptable across different headline contexts.

name: Dulce Pro
classification_notes: Monoline display face with swash capitals and elongated teardrop terminals. Script-adjacent character forms — flourished but upright, not connected. Companion ornaments set extends decorative range.
summary: A thin, monoline display face with swash capitals and script-adjacent flourishes, designed by Paula Nazal Selaive for Latinotype in 2013.
description: Dulce Pro builds on an earlier release of the same name, refining its monoline letterforms and elongated teardrop terminals into something more considered. Initial capitals carry ornamental swashes; lowercase characters end in decorative flourishes — romantic in register, upright in construction. A companion Ornaments set adds hearts, banners and frames for use alongside the main family.
foundry_blurb: Dulce Pro is a romantic, thin typeface that borrows from script conventions without fully committing to them. Its capitals open with swashes and its lowercase closes with delicate finals, while the separate Ornaments style adds hearts, flowers, banners and decorative frames for mixing.

name: Elemental Sans Pro
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif with calligraphic influence in stroke construction. Letterforms carry subtle weight variation and pen-derived logic without veering into script territory. Sits in the tradition of optically warm, readable humanist sans designs.
summary: A Chilean humanist sans-serif with calligraphic roots, developed by Francisco Gálvez and overhauled in 2010 with four weights, matching italics and small caps throughout.
description: Elemental Sans Pro began as a 1997 design by Francisco Gálvez, launched commercially in 2001, then received a full OpenType overhaul in 2010 to coincide with Chile's bicentenary. Its defining quality is a calligraphic undercurrent in the stroke construction – humanist in form but with a pen-derived logic that keeps it warm at text sizes. Four weights from light to extrabold each come with an italic and small caps, giving the family reasonable range for editorial and body work.
foundry_blurb: Elemental is a humanist sans-serif whose principal characteristic is a hybrid of calligraphic outline forms. Created in 1997 and launched in 2001, it was redesigned in 2010 as a full OpenType release with an improved italic, produced by Chilean foundry Latinotype.

name: Emperator
classification_notes: High-contrast calligraphic serif conceived from calligraphic study, offered in three distinct textural variants: Classic (clean, formal), Hand (organic, drawn) and Rough (coarse, textured). All three share the same underlying design system and weight range. No true italics; stylistic differentiation is achieved through the variant structure rather than slant. Clearly a display family — recommended primarily for titles, labels, packaging and short text.
summary: A calligraphic display serif by Marcelo Quiroz spanning three textural variants – Classic, Hand and Rough – across 18 styles with 750+ glyphs and support for 200+ Latin-based languages.
description: Emperator is built on calligraphic foundations, shaped by Marcelo Quiroz's study under master calligraphers. The family offers three distinct aesthetic treatments within one design system: a clean Classical style, an organic Hand-drawn version and a coarse Rough cut, each running through Light, Regular, Bold and Black. Small caps, ligatures, fractions and stylistic alternates are included throughout, making it a capable choice for titles, labels, packaging and short editorial text.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Emperator as a fresh take on classic typefaces, grounded in Quiroz's calligraphic training. The three subfamilies – Classic, Hand and Rough – are designed to balance elegance, legibility and expressiveness across different applications. The full character set runs to 750+ glyphs with small caps, ligatures, fractions and stylistic alternates, covering more than 200 Latin-based languages across Pro and Essential licensing tiers.

name: Emperatriz
classification_notes: High-contrast display serif rooted in classical Roman proportions with a contemporary editorial finish. The family ships as two coordinated variants – a high-contrast serif and a slab – each in four weights from UltraLight to Bold. No italics. Generous counter forms, alternate capitals (Q, R, P, O), and a rich OpenType feature set including oldstyle numerals, ligatures and manicules. Positioned squarely at headline and short-text display use.
summary: A high-contrast display serif by Chilean designer Sandra García, pairing a classical serif and a slab variant across four weights with broad Latin script coverage and a well-stocked OpenType feature set.
description: Emperatriz draws on classical Roman proportions and delivers them with a clean, contemporary editorial character suited to headlines, magazine titles, book covers and brand identity. The family comprises two coordinated variants – a high-contrast serif and a slab – each running UltraLight through Bold, with alternate capitals, ligatures, oldstyle numerals and manicules throughout. Language support extends to more than 200 Latin script languages, making it a practical choice for multilingual publishing.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Emperatriz as firmly rooted in Roman tradition yet squarely in the present – monumental in form, clean and modern in execution. Designed by Sandra García, they position it for editorial work across magazines, catalogues, book covers, corporate identities, packaging and labels, with every style sharing generous counter forms and a full set of typographic details.

name: Emy Slab
classification_notes: Egyptian-proportioned slab serif with soft, rounded terminals rather than the genre's typical blunt cuts; the Alt subfamily introduces asymmetric letterforms for display applications, shifting the family's character from text-optimised to graphic.
summary: An Egyptian slab built on classical proportions but softened with rounded terminals, split across two subfamilies – one text-weight, one display-oriented – in seven weights with italics throughout.
description: Emy Slab takes the solid structure of Egyptian-style slabs and relaxes them with soft terminals, moving the genre's characteristic rigidity towards something warmer and more readable at text sizes. The family divides cleanly into two purpose-built subfamilies: Emy Slab Basic targets editorial, book and corporate work, while Emy Slab Alt introduces asymmetric letterforms and a more graphic presence for logotypes, packaging and screen use. Seven weights with matching italics across both subfamilies produce 28 styles covering 440 characters and 208 languages.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Emy Slab as a slab serif rooted in the classical proportions of Egyptian typefaces, distinguished by soft terminals that give it a more modern and approachable character. The Basic subfamily is designed for editorial and publication work – books, magazines, corporate design – while the Alt subfamily, with its asymmetric shapes and contemporary feel, is aimed at logotypes, branding, packaging and television applications.

name: Equity Sans
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif constructed on circular forms throughout, but departs from pure-geometry coldness by rounding every terminal and opening up the apertures generously. Sits between strict geometric and humanist sans in mood. The Alt subfamily offers alternate glyph variants for additional character expression within the same structural framework.
designer: Luciano Vergara, Jorge Cisterna, Daniel Hernández, Alexis Navarro
summary: A geometric sans-serif from Latinotype that softens circular-form construction with rounded terminals and open apertures, landing in useful territory between cold precision and humanist warmth.
description: Equity Sans is built on pure circular geometry but counters the clinical quality that often comes with it by rounding every terminal and keeping the apertures open and generous. Designed by four collaborators at Latinotype, it covers 32 styles across two subfamilies – Equity Sans and Equity Sans Alt – each running eight weights with matching italics. The brief is clearly beauty, wellness and lifestyle branding, and it performs well for that, though the rounded-geometric-sans territory is crowded.
foundry_blurb: Equity Sans is described by Latinotype as soft geometry with sharp presence – a typeface built on circular forms that combines the crispness of modern geometric design with a warmth achieved through rounded terminals, generous curves and an open rhythm. Intended for brands that need presence without aggression and character without rigidity, it is pitched at beauty, lifestyle packaging, logos, landing pages and editorial campaigns where warmth and care are part of the message.

name: Estampa Script
classification_notes: Formal calligraphic script with high stroke contrast and teardrop terminals drawn from the Didone tradition. Unusually, the family spans five weights (Extra Light to Bold), giving it more range than most script typefaces. Released 2017, designed by Sofia Mohr for Latinotype.
summary: A high-contrast calligraphic script by Sofia Mohr, drawing on Didone typographic conventions with teardrop terminals and an unusually broad five-weight range.
description: Designed by Sofia Mohr and released in 2017, Estampa Script applies the high stroke contrast and teardrop terminals of Didone typefaces to a formal calligraphic structure. The five-weight range from Extra Light to Bold is rare for a script and gives it genuine flexibility across branding, packaging and fashion-adjacent contexts. It reads as polished and considered rather than novelty-driven.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Estampa Script as a five-weight script face with high contrast between thick and thin strokes and teardrop terminals reminiscent of Didone typefaces – a combination that gives it a strong, distinctive character suited to clothing, interior design, branding, packaging, advertising and publishing.

name: Estandar
classification_notes: Wayfinding-inspired geometric sans-serif with a mid-century signage aesthetic. Open, evenly spaced letterforms drawn from historical park and public transport lettering. Relatively conventional construction; the retro character comes from proportion and spacing rather than unusual structure.
summary: A retro wayfinding sans by Luciano Vergara, drawing on mid-century park and transport signage across six weights with matching italics and a dingbats companion.
description: Estandar takes its cues from the lettering traditions of mid-century public signage, translating clean geometric letterforms into a practical 13-style family. Six weights run from ExtraLight to Black, each with a companion italic; a dingbats set rounds out the wayfinding brief. The aesthetic sits between vintage and functional, making it serviceable for editorial, branding and period-appropriate signage work without tipping into pastiche.
foundry_blurb: A retro and vintage wayfinding sans-serif drawn from old signage in Central Park and across Europe.

name: Estandar Rounded
classification_notes: Condensed rounded grotesque with tall x-height and soft terminal rounding throughout. Draws explicitly on mid-century wayfinding and park signage lettering. An extension of the original Estandar family rather than a standalone design. The rounding is restrained — more softened edges than a full geometric rounded treatment.
summary: A condensed rounded sans drawing on vintage park and transit signage, with six weights, full italics and a dingbat set.
description: Estandar Rounded extends Luciano Vergara's original Estandar family by softening its condensed grotesque forms with rounded terminals — a nod to mid-century wayfinding lettering from Central Park and European transit systems. Six weights run from Extra Light to Black, each paired with an italic, giving it reasonable range for headline and display use. Tall x-height keeps it legible even when set small, and a dingbat font is included alongside the text styles.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype present it as a retro and vintage wayfinding sans serif inspired by old signals in Central Park and Europe — a condensed design with a tall x-height suited to signage, titles, packaging and advertising.

name: Facundo
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif that borrows its uppercase construction from Latinotype's Trend family, then softens the result into something more neutral and friendly. Clean circular geometry with enough warmth to avoid the cold rigidity of stricter geometric faces.
summary: A geometric sans from Latinotype with seven weights and matching italics, drawing on the letterforms of Trend and covering over 200 languages across Latin and Cyrillic scripts.
description: Facundo pairs simple geometric construction with details borrowed from Latinotype's Trend, arriving at something friendlier and more versatile than either a strict geometric or a humanist sans. It spans 715 characters and supports over 200 languages across Latin and Cyrillic scripts, giving it real breadth for international branding and web work. The weight range is well-considered, from Thin through Black with italics throughout, though the overall personality is pleasant rather than distinctive.
foundry_blurb: Facundo is built on simple geometric shapes and the uppercase glyphs of Latinotype's Trend family, with subtle nuances intended to set it apart. The design aims for a fresh, friendly character suited to corporate identity, branding and web design. It ships in seven weights with matching italics, totalling 14 styles, and supports over 200 languages via Latin and Cyrillic scripts.

name: Faraon
designer: Rodrigo López Fuentes, Sergio Leiva Whittle
classification_notes: Unbracketed slab serif in the Egyptian tradition, citing Rockwell and Memphis as direct references. Three widths (Condensed, Regular, Expanded) each span seven weights with matching italics, totalling 42 styles. Includes small caps, ligatures and swashes, giving it editorial as well as display range.
summary: A 42-style Egyptian slab offered in Condensed, Regular and Expanded widths, filtering the geometry of Rockwell and Memphis through a cleaner, more contemporary lens.
description: Faraon is an Egyptian slab serif released in 2024, spanning seven weights and three widths with matching italics across all 42 styles. It takes the structural weight of industrial precedents like Rockwell and Memphis and gives them a lighter, fresher character – equally at home in tight headlines and running text. Small caps, ligatures and swashes extend its usefulness in editorial and branding contexts.
foundry_blurb: Faraon takes its cues from the industrial slab tradition – fonts like Rockwell and Memphis – and reinterprets them with an Egyptian aesthetic and a softer contemporary touch. Three widths and seven weights give it the flexibility to drive dynamic layouts across print and web, while the full suite of OpenType features makes it a practical tool for editorial and display work alike.

name: Fibra
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with experimental structural details – tight contrast between rounded letterforms (a, d) and straight-sided ones (n, h), triple terminals on the W, a projection off the A stem, and an exaggerated R terminal. Two sub-families: Basic tones the quirks down for formal settings; Alt plays them up for display work.
summary: A geometric sans-serif with genuine structural personality, split into a restrained Basic family and an expressive Alt family built for headlines and logotypes.
description: Fibra is a 28-style geometric sans-serif by Jorge Cisterna, built around deliberate tension between rounded and straight-sided forms. Idiosyncratic details – triple terminals on the W, a projection off the A stem, an exaggerated R terminal – give it real character without tipping into gimmick. The Alt sub-family amplifies those qualities for editorial and branding work; the Basic sub-family pulls them back for subheadings and more formal settings.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Fibra as a geometric sans-serif with experimental spirit rooted in the modernist tradition. The design plays on the contrast between strictly geometric forms and more expressive structural choices, giving the family what the foundry calls a typeface that "gives you the chills." Fibra Basic handles the formal applications; Fibra Alt is the display-ready counterpart suited to posters, magazines and logotypes.

name: Fibra One
classification_notes: Soft geometric sans with Avant Garde DNA. Rounded terminals on certain glyphs while retaining hard corners on others — creating deliberate contrast rather than a uniformly rounded system. Display details include a three-terminal W, a projecting A stem and an exaggerated R terminal. Two subfamilies (Basic and Alt) differ in stylistic intensity.
summary: A soft geometric display sans by Jorge Cisterna that tempers Avant Garde structure with selectively rounded terminals and deliberate contrast between curved and straight strokes.
description: Fibra One is a 2018 reinterpretation of Cisterna's Fibra, adding soft corners and smoother curve-to-straight transitions to give the underlying geometric structure a more approachable character. The family splits into two subfamilies: Basic, which dials back the stylistic flourishes for subheadings and corporate text, and Alt, which leans into display details like the exaggerated R terminal and three-arm W. Thirty-two styles across eight weights with italics give it reasonable range for headline-focused type systems.
foundry_blurb: Fibra One keeps the structural bones of its predecessor while rounding the corners for a more dynamic, playful personality — designed primarily for magazine headlines, posters and logotypes, with a generous x-height that extends its usefulness into corporate text settings.

name: Fidel
classification_notes: Single-weight (Black) condensed sans-serif display face. Heavily weighted with a large x-height. Draws directly from Russian Constructivist lettering and vintage Cuban communist poster typography. Available in three variants: upright, italic and stencil — all at the one Black weight. Basic Latin character set only.
summary: A single-weight condensed black display face drawn from Russian Constructivism and vintage Cuban poster lettering, suited to high-impact headline and poster work.
description: Fidel is a heavily weighted, condensed sans-serif built entirely around one personality: propagandist, loud and poster-ready. Luciano Vergara took his cues from Russian Constructivist lettering and old Cuban communist posters, resulting in a face with a commanding x-height and tight proportions. Three variants ship — Black, Black Italic and Black Stencil — but there is no weight range to speak of, which limits its versatility considerably.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Fidel Black Essential as a heavily weighted, condensed sans-serif with a large x-height, its design rooted in Russian Constructivism and vintage Cuban communist poster lettering. They position it for headlines, subheadings, posters and logotypes.

name: Fondue
classification_notes: Art Deco–inspired display sans with cursive ductus, wide horizontal proportions and a large x-height. Drawn from the hand-lettered work of Mexican cartoonist Ernesto "El Chango" Cabral in Revista de Revistas. Eclectic in character but structured enough for medium-sized text as well as headline use.
summary: A six-weight Art Deco display family derived from Ernesto "El Chango" Cabral's cartoonist lettering, with wide proportions, cursive ductus and 207-language coverage.
description: Fondue takes its cue from the hand-lettered headings Ernesto "El Chango" Cabral drew for Revista de Revistas, translated by Jorge Alberto Martínez into a six-weight family spanning Thin to Heavy. Wide horizontal proportions, a large x-height and a cursive ductus give each weight a consistent friendly rhythm that holds up at headline scale and in medium-sized text. Standard and discretionary ligatures, plus stylistic alternates, extend its range beyond a single decorative register.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Fondue as a family of eclectic shapes adapted from the Art Deco lettering Ernesto "El Chango" Cabral used throughout Revista de Revistas. Its cursive ductus, wide horizontal proportions and large x-height produce a friendly, consistent rhythm suited to headlines, branding and medium-sized text, with 496 characters covering 207 languages across six weights.

name: Fontanella
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif drawn from calligraphy and the skeleton of Roman capital letters. Slightly enlarged x-height. Includes small caps, oldstyle figures and width alternates. Warm and classic in spirit despite being a clean sans.
summary: A calligraphically rooted humanist sans in nine weights with matching italics, small caps and oldstyle figures — well suited to editorial, fashion and branding work.
description: Fontanella draws from calligraphy and the skeleton of Roman capital letters, giving it a warmth that most contemporary sans serifs lack. Its enlarged x-height holds well at display sizes, and the 18-style family is properly equipped with small caps, oldstyle numerals and width alternates. A dependable choice for fashion editorial and brand identity work that wants a classical reference without going serif.
foundry_blurb: Fontanella emerged from calligraphy and manual drawing, exploring the skeleton and classic proportions of Roman capital letters. The family's slightly enlarged x-height suits editorial, fashion, branding, magazine, television and window display applications. A classic spirit reinterpreted in a contemporary language.

name: Four Seasons
classification_notes: Handwritten display script with a naturalistic, botanical theme. Three-subfamily structure: Pro and Essential carry standard text styles (Regular, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic) while Extras delivers dingbats, ornaments, and illustrated word marks drawn from branches, leaves, and seasonal flora. Extensive OpenType feature set including swashes, ligatures, titlings, initials and alternates. Designed over a three-year period (2010–2013), giving it more considered craft than most single-season novelty scripts, but the thematic scope is narrow.
summary: A nature-themed handwritten display family from Latinotype with three subfamilies spanning text styles, botanical ornaments and illustrated word marks.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara and Guisela Mendoza over three years (2010–2013), Four Seasons is a handwritten display family structured around three cuts: Pro and Essential cover standard weights with italic, while Extras delivers dingbats, ornaments and seasonal word illustrations drawn from branches, leaves and flowers. The Pro cut includes a full OpenType feature set – swashes, ligatures, titlings, initials and alternates – making it usable beyond pure decoration. Its thematic scope is tight, best suited to packaging, editorial, and photography composition where botanical aesthetics are the brief.
foundry_blurb: Four Seasons is a display handwritten typeface inspired by nature and the changing seasons. Drawn with real handmade strokes for authentic lettering, it suits photography and illustration composition. The full family includes an extensive character set with titlings, endings, initials, swashes, ligatures and alternates, plus a set of ornaments, dingbats and botanical word illustrations drawn from branches, leaves and flowers.

name: Galadali
classification_notes: High-contrast tall condensed serif, upright-only, designed explicitly for headline and display settings. Six weights from Light to Black. Features swashes and stylistic alternates that give it a decorative, editorial character.
summary: A tall condensed serif in six weights with swashes, small caps and old-style figures, built for editorial headlines and brand display work.
description: Galadali is a high-contrast condensed serif designed by Diego Maldonado and released through Latinotype in 2021. The six-weight range runs from Light to Black and the family ships with small caps, old-style and lining figures, fractions, stylistic alternates and swashes. It leans toward elegance over brute impact, making it a reasonable choice for editorial mastheads and display-heavy brand settings.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Galadali as a tall condensed typeface made for beautiful titles — elegant in character, with strong visual impact and refined detailing. The family includes small caps, old-style and lining figures, fractions, superior and inferior letters, and a range of alternates and swashes designed to expand typographic combinations.

name: Galeana
classification_notes: Flat-sided sans serif with closed aperture and strong vertical stress. Four-width superfamily system — Compressed through Extended — each carrying six weights with matching italics. Draws editorial references from Latin American typography as seen in European publications such as Plastique and Zembla.
summary: A flat-sided editorial sans by Jorge Martínez, spanning 48 styles across four widths from Compressed to Extended, suited to headlines and brand work across 200+ Latin-based languages.
description: Galeana is a flat-sided sans serif with a closed aperture, released by Latinotype in 2020 and designed by Jorge Martínez. The family runs 48 styles across four widths — Compressed, Condensed, Standard and Extended — with six weights and matching italics in each. Conceived as a reinterpretation of Latin American editorial typography seen in publications like Plastique and Zembla, it covers 417 glyphs across more than 200 Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: Galeana takes its name and proportional logic from the African tulip tree: the narrowest, heaviest styles reference the tree's slender trunk, while the wider variants echo its broad crown. Designed as a reinterpretation of Latin American-inflected typefaces found in European editorial publications, it suits headlines, brand identity, advertising and screen use across 200+ Latin-based languages.

name: Garden
classification_notes: Display serif with a handmade, calligraphic character inspired by Brazilian textile printing and floral design. The family includes ornamental supplements – brush-calligraphy catchwords, botanical ornaments and floral dingbats – alongside four alphabetic styles in regular, swash and alternate cuts. Not a workhorse text face; intended for poster, label and headline use.
summary: A handmade display serif from Latinotype drawn from Brazilian textile and floral traditions, spanning ten styles that include swash cuts, brush-calligraphy catchwords, botanical ornaments and dingbats.
description: Garden is a display serif designed by Luciano Vergara and Guisela Mendoza, released in 2014 after a trip to Brazil that left the designers struck by its warm character and wild flora. The family has a playful, spontaneous quality suited to posters, labels and packaging. Four alphabetic styles in regular and swash cuts, each with alternates, are joined by a set of brush-calligraphy catchwords, botanical ornaments and floral dingbats.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Garden as capturing the cheerful, spontaneous spirit of Brazil – its people and wild nature feeding a serif with a warm, handmade feel. The family is positioned for text composition, posters, headlines and label design, built around original catchwords drawn from brush calligraphy and rounded out with floral dingbats and botanical ornaments.

name: Garrison
classification_notes: Contemporary humanist sans with a geometric backbone. Draws on the English humanist sans tradition — warm, organic letterform structure — while introducing controlled geometric rigidity. The dual italic system is the distinguishing feature: a mechanically slanted oblique alongside a genuinely flowing true italic, giving each weight two distinct modes of emphasis. Suitable for both continuous text and display settings.
summary: A well-made humanist sans from Juan Bruce at Latinotype, offering seven weights and a dual italic system — true italic and oblique — across 21 styles suited to editorial, branding and wayfinding work.
description: Garrison takes the English humanist sans as its starting point, pairing warm, organic letterform construction with a subtly geometric structure. Its defining feature is the duo-italic approach: each weight ships with both a mechanically slanted oblique and a genuine flowing italic, giving typographers real choice in how emphasis is handled. The seven-weight range covers light editorial text through to heavy display use without feeling stretched.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Garrison as a contemporary sans that offers a straightforward interpretation of the English humanist sans, gently blending rigid tones over a warm structure. They describe it as a powerful workhorse suited to paragraphs, branding, signage and editorial design. The duo-italic set — a slanted oblique alongside a smooth, flowing italic — is highlighted as a key differentiator within the family.

name: Gaspo Slab
classification_notes: Humanist slab serif with ink traps, strong bracketed serifs and ample counters. Proportions sit closer to humanist text tradition than geometric or Egyptian slab. Ink traps suggest optical refinement for smaller sizes. Seven weights from Thin to Black with matching italics.
summary: A humanist slab serif with ink traps and seven weights, offering solid legibility across editorial, advertising and corporate contexts in 128 languages.
description: Gaspo Slab is a 2016 slab serif by Daniel Peralta, released through Latinotype. Strong serifs, humanist proportions and ample counters give it reliable legibility at small sizes, and the ink traps point to considered optical craft. The 14-style family carries a 434-character set with tabular figures, alternates and fractions, covering 128 languages.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary slab serif with aesthetically pleasing curves, strong serifs, ample counters, humanist proportions and ink traps. The result is a functional font with a contemporary feel that reads well at small sizes, suited to headlines, editorial text, advertising, corporate use and product design across 128 languages.

name: Glyphic Sans
classification_notes: Geometric skeleton with deliberate humanist inflections; distinctive extended strokes in K, Q, y and k add character without breaking the structured rhythm. Eight weights from Thin to Extrabold, each with a corresponding italic, totalling 16 styles.
designer: Luciano Vergara, Jorge Cisterna, Daniel Hernández, Felipe Sanzana
summary: A geometric sans with humanist inflections across eight weights, pitched at technology and finance brands that want precision without coldness.
description: Glyphic Sans pairs a geometric framework with subtle humanist details – extended strokes in K, Q, y and k give it character without disrupting its clean structural rhythm. All eight weights ship with italics, making it a practical choice for digital interfaces, editorial layouts and corporate identity. Latinotype aimed it squarely at fintech and banking, where authority and approachability need to coexist.
foundry_blurb: Glyphic Sans sits at the intersection of the technical and the human – geometric proportions refined with humanist inflections, built to project trust, sophistication and a sense of innovation without tipping into coldness or excess flair.

name: GoGipsy
classification_notes: Modern calligraphic script drawn from hand-lettering, with a dynamic baseline that creates strong rhythm and movement. Swash caps, OpenType ligatures, stylistic alternates and initial letterforms are included. A companion ornaments subfamily is modelled on Mexican textile and embroidery patterns. Five styles across two subfamilies (script and drop-cap variants).
summary: A fluid calligraphic display script by Guisela Mendoza, with swashes, alternates and a textile-inspired ornament set rooted in Mexican Caribbean culture.
description: GoGipsy pairs energetic calligraphic strokes with a deliberately dynamic baseline to give the letterforms a sense of movement and spontaneity. The family runs to five styles across three subfamilies: the core script, drop-cap variants, and an ornament set drawn from Mexican textile and embroidery patterns. OpenType features include swashes, ligatures and a range of initial alternates, which makes it most useful for display-weight branding, packaging or editorial work with a Latin or artisanal flavour.
foundry_blurb: GoGipsy grew from the modern calligraphy of Guisela (Coto) Mendoza, developed with technical support from Luciano Vergara at Latinotype.
