The design takes its cues from a journey through the Mexican Caribbean, with stroke energy intended to evoke freedom, spontaneity and expressiveness. The ornaments subfamily borrows its motifs from traditional Mexican textile art and hand-embroidery.

name: Goldplay
classification_notes: Rounded geometric sans with soft terminals and a large x-height. The Alt subfamily introduces semi-serif details on select letterforms, shifting the feel toward display and branding. Both variants share the same seven-weight range with matching italics.
summary: A rounded geometric sans in 28 styles across a clean standard cut and a semi-serif Alt variant, with broad Latin coverage designed for editorial, branding and screen work.
description: Goldplay pairs soft, rounded terminals with a generous x-height across seven weights, each with a matching italic. A second subfamily, Goldplay Alt, introduces semi-serif details for a more expressive display character suited to logotypes, packaging and TV. The 540-character set covers more than 200 Latin-based languages, making the family genuinely practical for international work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Goldplay as a modern typeface built on rounded letterforms and classical proportions, grown from the same design DNA as Isidora Sans. The standard version is clean and contemporary, aimed at headlines, books, magazines and corporate identity; the Alt semi-serif cut is pitched at branding, packaging, web and motion. Both share a large x-height and a 540-character Latin Extended set covering more than 200 languages.

name: Grobek
classification_notes: Old-style serif with diagonal stress and soft teardrop terminals. Draws on Garamond and 15th-century models while borrowing warmth from American Typewriter. Two subfamilies: Grobek (classic) and Grobek Alt (stronger personality, more expressive).
summary: A Garamond-inflected old-style serif from Enrique Hernández with teardrop terminals and diagonal stress, offered in eight weights across two subfamilies – one classic, one more expressive – and covering over 200 Latin-based languages.
description: Grobek draws on 15th-century type models and Garamond's structure, softened by the warm teardrop terminals associated with American Typewriter. The result is a readable serif that sits comfortably in editorial and branding work without leaning too far in either direction. The Alt subfamily amplifies its character for more expressive applications, while 32 styles in total give it solid practical range.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Grobek as a serif that balances classic aesthetics with a contemporary sensibility, inspired by Garamond and 15th-century typefaces. Its defining features are diagonal stress and soft curved teardrop terminals. The Grobek Alt subfamily is designed to offer a stronger personality and greater design freedom than the base family.

name: Grota
classification_notes: A grotesque sans-serif with a unicase construction, meaning uppercase and lowercase letterforms share a unified optical height. Its gestural, hand-lettering-derived strokes give it a warmth and expressiveness uncommon in conventional grotesques. Positioned at the display end of the sans-serif spectrum despite spanning a full weight range.
summary: A unicase grotesque with gestural, hand-lettering-influenced forms, running Thin to Black with italics, suited to expressive headlines and brand work.
description: Grota is a unicase grotesque sans-serif designed by Daniel and Eli Hernández for Latinotype, published in 2013. Its gestural character draws on hand-lettering traditions, giving it warmth and personality without tipping into script territory. The family has since expanded into Grota Sans and Grota Sans Rounded, broadening its range considerably.
foundry_blurb: A very expressive grotesque with a gestural character inspired by hand lettering. Unicase in construction, it is designed for logos, brands, magazines, headlines and books.

name: Grota Rounded
classification_notes: Grotesque sans-serif with fully rounded terminals and a unicase design. Letterforms carry a gestural quality drawn from hand lettering, giving the face more warmth than a strict geometric or neo-grotesque. The unicase approach mixes uppercase and lowercase proportions for an unconventional rhythm at display sizes.
summary: A rounded grotesque with unicase proportions and gestural warmth, built for confident display work in branding and editorial.
description: Grota Rounded pairs grotesque geometry with fully rounded terminals and letterform proportions drawn from hand lettering. Its unicase design gives headlines a relaxed, unconventional rhythm that works well in logos and magazine settings. Six weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, give it enough range for varied branding and print use.
foundry_blurb: Grota Rounded is a very expressive font with a gestural character inspired by hand lettering. Grotesque, unicase, and designed for logos, brands, magazines, headlines and books.

name: Grota Sans
classification_notes: Humanist grotesque with semi-condensed proportions and a Latin design sensibility. Elevated x-height and varying contrast across weights give it range from body copy to display. The Alt subfamily substitutes more humanistic character forms, adding warmth beyond a strict neo-grotesque structure.
summary: A humanist grotesque with semi-condensed proportions and ten weights, offering a standard and Alt subfamily for editorial, branding and body text work.
description: Grota Sans covers 40 styles across two subfamilies — the core family and an Alt variant with more humanistic character alternatives — each in ten weights with true italics. Semi-condensed proportions and a high x-height make it adaptable from running text columns to strong display headlines. OpenType support includes ligatures, diacritics and alternates across 34 European languages.
foundry_blurb: A grotesque shaped by Latin design sensibility, built by Daniel and Ely Hernández at Latinotype. Suited to logos, editorial layouts, packaging and web, with coverage from Thin to Black and a full italic complement alongside an alternate character set with more humanistic forms.

name: Grota Sans Rounded
classification_notes: Grotesque sans-serif with rounded terminals throughout; part of the broader Grota type system alongside the straight-edged Grota Sans and Grota Unicase; includes an alternate character subfamily (Grota Sans Alt Rounded) with variant letterforms.
summary: A 40-style rounded grotesque spanning 10 weights with matching italics and an alternate character subfamily, part of Latinotype's broader Grota type system.
description: Grota Sans Rounded softens the skeleton of its parent grotesque family with rounded terminals, covering Thin through Black with matching italics across two subfamilies: the standard cut and an alternate set with variant letterforms. The 40-style family is well-suited to branding, logotype and editorial work where a friendlier grotesque is needed. It sits within the Grota system alongside straight-edged Grota Sans and Grota Unicase, giving designers a coherent multi-subfamily toolkit.
foundry_blurb: A grotesque typeface with Latin character, designed to work in tandem with Grota Sans and Grota Unicase. The rounded version applies softened terminals across the full weight range, making it practical for logos, brands, books and headlines.

name: Grotesco
classification_notes: South American grotesque drawing from the American grotesk tradition. Ten weights with matching italics; two alternate character sets for display and identity applications; extended Latin and Cyrillic coverage. Alfonso García contributed digital editing, italic development and Cyrillic/currency expansion.
summary: A South American grotesque from Luciano Vergara, spanning 10 weights with full italics, Cyrillic support and two alternate character sets for branding and advertising work.
description: Grotesco draws from American grotesk conventions, reinterpreted with a Latin American sensibility by Chilean designer Luciano Vergara. The family runs from Thin to Heavy across 10 weights, each paired with an italic, and includes two alternate character sets suited to logo and identity work. Cyrillic coverage and extended currency symbols were developed in collaboration with Alfonso García.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Grotesco as a South American take on the American grotesque, combining grotesk structure with what the foundry calls Latino rhythm and flair. Two alternate character sets give designers flexibility across logos, brands and advertising layouts. Alfonso García contributed the italic development, Cyrillic expansion and currency symbol support.

name: Guadalupe
classification_notes: High-contrast Didone serif in the Didot tradition, with pronounced thick-thin stroke contrast and hairline serifs. Offered in two distinct terminal cuts: Regular (classical roman) and Gota (more expressive, suited to display setting). Extensive alternates and swashes throughout. Available in Pro and Essential tiers.
summary: A Chilean Didone with dual terminal variants and generous alternates, built for fashion editorial and luxury branding.
description: Guadalupe is a high-contrast Didone serif by Chilean designer Daniel Hernández, drawing squarely from the Didot tradition. It comes in two terminal cuts – Regular, the classical roman, and Gota, a more expressive variant suited to display setting – with a generous set of alternates and swashes across both. The result is a versatile luxury serif aimed at fashion magazines, logotypes and upscale branding.
foundry_blurb: Guadalupe belongs to the classical Didot family. It is a high-performance font with a great set of alternates and swashes, carefully refined in its details. Available in two terminal versions – Regular, a classic roman, and Gota, more expressive for word-setting – it is positioned for fashion magazines, logotypes and luxury contexts.

name: Handy Cut
classification_notes: Irregular display face built around letterforms cut from paper with bare hands. Deliberately rough, uneven strokes with unicase-adjacent character shapes. Ships with a companion Dingbats style. No body-text utility whatsoever — purely expressive at headline or logo scale.
summary: An experimental display face drawn from the rough, torn quality of paper cut with bare fingers, shipping in two styles: an irregular roman and a companion dingbats set.
description: Handy Cut is a novelty display typeface by Patricia Vergara, built from the aesthetic of paper cut with bare hands on a farm in southern Chile. The family ships in two styles: a main roman of deliberately irregular, rough-edged letterforms, and a Dingbats companion for decorative use. It suits craft-adjacent logos, short expressive headlines or any context where a lo-fi, handmade quality is the entire point of the brief.
foundry_blurb: An experimental project inspired by cutting paper with only your fingers, created by Paty Bean from a farm in southern Chile. It includes dingbats and alternate characters for use in expressive, irregular short texts.

name: Hawking
classification_notes: Modern slab serif with minimal stroke contrast and slightly squarish letterforms. Generous counter spaces and a relatively large x-height with lowercase ascenders extending above cap-height for legibility. Serifs combine curved and straight lines. Designed explicitly for text-setting in scientific and technical contexts.
summary: A purposeful rational slab serif designed for scientific and technical publishing, with minimal stroke contrast, open counters and a generous x-height.
description: Hawking is a clean, modern slab with squarish letterforms and minimal modulation, built for continuous reading in scientific, journalistic and literary texts. Lowercase ascenders extend above the cap-height, improving legibility at text sizes. The bolder weights hold up well as display faces for headlines and section markers.
foundry_blurb: A slab typeface with slightly squarish shapes and a rational, modern look, designed with scientific publications in mind. Minimal modulation and generous counter spaces aid legibility across long texts, while a large x-height and ascenders above the cap-height give it presence on the page. The family also suits journalistic, technical and literary use, with the heavier weights adapted for headline setting.

name: Hernandez Bros
classification_notes: Latinotype's own product page describes Hernandez Bros as a "modern sans serif," but multiple independent resellers (Creative Market title copy, Fonts.com, fonthaus) classify it as a serif, and the MyFonts editorial profile states it "must be accompanied by neutral fonts, hopefully sans serif" – placing it as the expressive, non-sans element of any pairing. Classified here as serif (display) based on the weight of reseller evidence, the design context, and the ATF Bulfinch inspiration (a high-contrast display type). Display-only; not suited to body text.
summary: A high-contrast display typeface by Chilean siblings Ely and Daniel Hernández, developed from drawings traded against the 1912 ATF Bulfinch, with eight weights from Extralight to Black suited to headlines, branding and editorial work.
description: Hernandez Bros grew from a drawing exercise the Hernández siblings ran during the 2021 lockdowns, exchanging sketches derived from the Bulfinch in the 1912 ATF catalogue. The process produced a modern display typeface with pronounced stroke contrast, eight upright weights and alternative characters that mix classical construction with geometric touches. It is a strict headline face, best used at display sizes alongside a neutral sans for body copy.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Hernandez Bros as a modern type family born from a collaborative family effort during the pandemic, with the Hernández siblings trading drawings against the 1912 ATF Bulfinch in a back-and-forth creative process. Spanning eight weights from Extralight to Black, it is characterised by elegant stroke contrasts and harmonious proportions, with Latinotype recommending it for titles, branding, editorial design and magazines.

name: Hernández Niu
classification_notes: Display slab serif with thickened serifs and functional ink-traps. Six weights from ExtraLight to Heavy, each with a matching true italic. Based on the earlier single-weight Hernández Bold, expanded and refined for broader typographic use. Detailed forms and counterforms intended for large-size setting.
summary: A display slab serif of six weights with matching true italics, built around thickened serifs and expressive ink-traps for confident use at large sizes.
description: Hernández Niu extends Latinotype's earlier Hernández Bold into a full six-weight family, adapting the heaviest weight for improved small-text legibility while keeping the design's defining ink-traps intact. True italics run across all weights, and a 397-character set covers 212 languages, making it a practical choice for editorial, branding and magazine work. The name uses 'niu' — a Spanish-phonology rendering of 'new' — to signal that this is a reworked evolution rather than a wholly original design.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Hernández Niu as a display slab built on the foundation of the original Hernández Bold, expanded into six weights with matching true italics. Thickened serifs and functional ink-traps give the family expressive character at large sizes, while the heaviest weight has been adapted to hold up in smaller text settings. The 397-character set covers 212 languages, suiting publishing, magazine work, headlines and branding.

name: Hogar
classification_notes: Monolinear sans-serif with consistent, unmodulated stroke width throughout. Designed as a dual system: the sans carries subtle script inflections in its terminals, while the companion script subfamily borrows the upright construction of a sans. Both subfamilies run through the same five weights with shared proportions and interpolation. Accompanied by a dingbat set of furniture silhouettes. No optical sizes or condensed cuts.
summary: A monolinear sans-serif by Sofia Mohr that pairs an upright sans and companion script on shared proportions across five weights, completed by a set of architecture-inspired furniture dingbats.
description: Hogar – Spanish for "home" – was designed by Sofia Mohr in 2016, drawing on her background in architecture and interior design. The family runs a monolinear sans alongside a script subfamily, both sharing identical proportions, stroke width and weight interpolation across five cuts, plus a dingbat set of furniture silhouettes by celebrated architects. OpenType features include lining and oldstyle figures and standard ligatures, with coverage across more than 200 Latin-derived languages.
foundry_blurb: Hogar brings together a sans, a script and a set of stylish interior design dingbats in one family. Designer Sofia Mohr drew on her architecture background to create a system that reflects her love for home – a sans with script gestures and a script with sans shapes, built on monolinear strokes with consistent proportions and weight interpolation throughout.

name: Hogar Slab
classification_notes: Monolinear construction throughout. The family bridges a slab serif and a matching script variant, with the italic sitting as a deliberate transitional style between the two. Both subfamilies share proportions and weight interpolations across five weights. A decorative Patterns set completes the system.
summary: A 16-style monolinear system that merges a slab serif and a script into one family, with the italic as a considered transition between the two styles.
description: Hogar Slab is a unified type system by Sofia Mohr in which a slab serif and a script share identical proportions and weight interpolations across five weights. The italic functions as a deliberate bridge between the upright slab and script subfamilies, making cross-style mixing unusually coherent. A Patterns set drawn from architect-designed furniture rounds out the family for display applications.
foundry_blurb: Hogar Slab combines a slab serif and a script slab serif into a single type system with a monolinear construction. Both subfamilies share proportions, weight interpolations and details, with the italic representing a transition between the two main styles. An additional Patterns set draws on furniture designs by well-known architects.

name: Igna Sans
classification_notes: Humanist functional sans-serif with angled strokes and rounded terminals. Sits between geometric warmth and conventional legibility — broad enough to work in extended text and display settings without tipping too far into either.
summary: A workmanlike humanist sans by Daniel Peralta, with seven weights and matching italics, covering 206 languages across a 430-character set.
description: Released by Latinotype in 2018, Igna Sans combines angled strokes with rounded forms to produce a type family that reads cleanly in body text and holds its presence at display sizes. Seven weights from Extra Light to Black, each with a matching italic, give it a solid typographic range for corporate, branding and advertising work. The 430-character set covers 206 languages, making it a practical option for multilingual projects.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Igna Sans as a humanist, functional typeface with a contemporary feel built for advertising, corporate and retail design. The angled strokes and rounded forms give it a smooth, expressive character that performs in both body copy and display headings.

name: In a Jar
classification_notes: Hand-lettering-inspired display typeface with a vintage kitchen aesthetic. Includes dedicated Ornaments and Dingbats companion fonts alongside two-weight text cuts with italics. Built for short text at large sizes.
summary: A hand-lettered display family by Guisela Mendoza built around a nostalgic kitchen aesthetic, with alternates, ligatures and companion Ornaments and Dingbats fonts rounding out the set.
description: In a Jar draws on vintage kitchen imagery – handwritten labels, recipe cards, pantry jars – to produce a display typeface that sits squarely in food branding, packaging and greetings. Two weights with italic cuts are paired with standalone Ornaments and Dingbats fonts, giving the family more decorative range than a typical novelty release. It is built for short text at large sizes and not intended for extended body copy.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes In a Jar as a hand-lettering-based display family inspired by the grandmother's kitchen – its colours, forms and smells – and the desire to revive vintage design sensibilities. They position it for brand design, headlines, labels and greetings cards in food-related contexts.

name: Indigena
classification_notes: Symbol/dingbat font – no letterforms. All glyphs are pictorial icons derived from pre-Columbian Mapuche iconography. Closest schema category is display as there is no dingbat option.
summary: A single-style dingbat font translating pre-Columbian Mapuche iconography – drawn from Chilean textiles and ceramics – into a usable pictorial glyph set.
description: Designed by Guisela Mendoza and released in 2016, Indigena draws on "Dibujos Indígenas de Chile" (1929) by Abel Gutiérrez – a catalogue of indigenous Chilean visual art – to build a set of symbols rooted in Mapuche craft tradition. The glyphs reflect the hand-drawn quality of Mapuche weaving and pottery, including imagery tied to We Tripantu, the Mapuche winter solstice celebration. As a dingbat with a single Regular style and no letterforms, its practical range is narrow, but the cultural research underpinning it is genuine.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Indigena as a dingbat that revives the artistic expression of the Mapuche people of Chile, recovering the handmade quality of their textile and ceramic work in contemporary form. The glyphs derive from pre-Columbian iconographic drawings documented in Abel Gutiérrez's 1929 publication "Dibujos Indígenas de Chile", with a number of symbols connected to We Tripantu, the Mapuche New Year observed at the southern winter solstice.

name: Infamy
classification_notes: Layered chromatic display face built on the bubble-letter graffiti tradition. The four-style system (Outline, Highlight, Shadow, Fill) is designed to stack for full-colour typographic effects. OpenType ligatures add variation. No italic or condensed axis.
summary: A layered bubble-letter display typeface by Santiago Sancha, rooted in early American graffiti culture, with four stackable styles for building chromatic text effects.
description: Infamy draws from the bubble-letter tradition of subway and suburban graffiti, preserving the horizontal alignment and tight tracking characteristic of the form. Its four-layer system (Outline, Highlight, Shadow, Fill) lets designers stack styles to build up chromatic, shaded lettering effects, while OpenType ligatures add compositional variety. It's a committed novelty face, deliberately loose and expressive rather than a workhorse text type.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Infamy as a display typeface inspired by graffiti and street art, drawing on the bubble-letter style that dominated early American subway culture. The font recovers graffiti's horizontal alignment, tight tracking and colourful lettering, with multiple layers enabling bright, shaded effects. A pictorial rendering of character faces replaces small caps, capturing what the foundry calls the childish and irresponsible spirit of experimental graffiti.

name: Informative
classification_notes: Clean, neutral geometric sans optimised for infographic and data-visualisation contexts. Bundled with seven thematic pictogram families – alimentation, city, energy, people, politics, sport and work – each supplied in outline and solid variants. Text weights span Thin to Black with matching italics.
designer: Sergio Ramirez, César Araya, Latinotype Team
summary: A functional geometric sans bundled with seven thematic pictogram sets, built for infographics, maps and data-driven digital work.
description: The text family spans Thin to Black across seven weights, each with a matching italic. Seven icon sets – covering alimentation, city, energy, people, politics, sport and work – ship in both outline and solid variants, adding 88 glyphs per set. With 423 text glyphs supporting 207 languages, the family covers the multilingual range most infographic briefs require.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Informative as a clean, simple and versatile family designed for infographics, maps and digital applications, pairing a complete sans-serif text family with thematic pictogram sets to keep visual and textual communication within a single type system.

name: Inter Sans
classification_notes: Geometric construction with soft curves and generous counterforms; began as a Rockwell reinterpretation before establishing its own identity. Early 20th-century influences with a contemporary, screen-friendly feel. Friendly and approachable rather than cold or mechanical.
summary: A geometric sans-serif from Alfonso García for Latinotype that grew out of a Rockwell reinterpretation into a friendly, open-counter family spanning nine weights with full italic coverage.
description: Inter Sans applies early 20th-century geometric conventions softened by rounded curves and generous counterforms, giving it a legible, approachable quality without the coldness of stricter geometric designs. Nine weights from ExtraLight to Heavy, each paired with an italic, cover most practical needs in digital interfaces, corporate communications and short-form publishing. The 439-glyph character set supports more than 200 Latin-script languages.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Inter Sans as a geometric sans with an early 20th-century feel, born from a Rockwell reinterpretation that developed its own character as the design progressed. Soft curves and open counterforms give it a friendly, sincere quality well suited to web, apps, corporate use and short text. The family contains 439 glyphs and covers more than 200 Latin-script languages.

name: Internacional
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque sans-serif in the Swiss/International Style tradition, distinguished by wide proportions, a large x-height with minimal cap-height differential, rounded letterforms and angled terminal cuts on characters such as 'c' and 'a'. The Alt variant offers an alternate proportional treatment across the same weight range.
summary: A 2017 neo-grotesque from Luciano Vergara built on International Style principles, spanning 28 styles across standard and alternate widths with Cyrillic coverage.
description: Internacional takes Swiss typography as its starting point, but Vergara adds rounded forms and angled terminal cuts – visible on 'c' and 'a' – that give the face a slightly warmer register than its forebears. A large x-height and wide proportions make it effective at display sizes and in short-to-mid-length text. Seven weights with italics are offered in both a standard and an alternate variant, with Latin Extended, Central European and Cyrillic support included.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Internacional as a high-impact typeface designed for corporate identity, branding, publishing and advertising. Wide proportions, rounded letterforms and angled terminal endings on characters such as 'c' and 'a' balance visual strength with legibility for short and mid-length paragraphs.

name: Isidora
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif built on early 20th-century models, softened by rounded terminals and diagonal terminal cuts. Two distinct subfamilies — Regular (classical lean) and Alternate (display/branding lean) — each in seven weights with matching italics; condensed cuts span the full weight range, totalling 42 styles.
summary: A geometric sans by Enrique Hernández V. drawing on early 20th-century models, with rounded terminals and a dual-subfamily system across seven weights, italics and condensed cuts.
description: Isidora pairs a rational geometric skeleton with rounded terminals and softened diagonal cuts, lending warmth without sacrificing structural clarity. It ships in two subfamilies — Regular and Alternate — each running Thin to Black with matching italics and condensed variants across all weights, totalling 42 styles. A 438-character set covering over 200 languages makes it a practical choice for multilingual headline and branding work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Isidora as a modern geometric typeface rooted in early 20th-century design and given a contemporary, functional refinement. Its rounded terminals and diagonal cuts create a friendly, expressive quality within a strong, rational structure. The 42-style family spans two subfamilies across seven weights with matching italics and condensed cuts, covering 207 languages via a 438-character set — positioned for headlines, logotypes, branding, packaging, publishing and web use.

name: Isidora Sans
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif derived from the earlier Isidora by removing terminals, giving a cleaner, more contemporary character that sits closer to early 20th-century grotesque proportions than to strict geometric construction. Two subfamilies split the range: the standard cut targets text and editorial work; the Alt cut offers a more display-friendly character suited to logotypes and branding.
summary: A clean geometric sans-serif in 28 styles across two subfamilies, built on early 20th-century grotesque proportions with terminals removed for a crisper, more contemporary feel.
description: Isidora Sans strips the terminals from its predecessor to produce a sharper, more geometric character suited to editorial work, publishing and corporate design. Its Alt subfamily widens the range towards logotypes, branding and display applications without requiring a separate purchase. With 416 glyphs covering 207 languages, it handles broad multilingual Latin requirements comfortably across all seven weights.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Isidora Sans as preserving the essence and structure of classic early 20th-century sans fonts while achieving a fresh, clean, contemporary appearance through the removal of terminals. The standard subfamily is pitched at publishing, books, magazines and corporate design; the Alt variant is recommended for logotypes, branding, packaging, web and TV.

name: Isidora Soft
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with soft, rounded terminals throughout. Small x-height with classic proportions. The Alt subfamily introduces more expressive glyph alternates. 28 styles total: 7 weights × 2 subfamilies (Standard and Alt), each with matching italics.
summary: A rounded-terminal geometric sans in seven weights with matching italics, built for branding and display work where the original Isidora's structure needed a warmer, more approachable edge.
description: Isidora Soft is Latinotype's 2019 reworking of their 2016 bestselling Isidora, differentiated by softened rounded terminals that give the family a friendlier character while retaining the original's small x-height and classic proportions. It ships in 28 styles split across two subfamilies – the standard cut and the more playful Alt variant – with 452 characters covering over 200 Latin-based languages. The family suits headlines, logotypes, branding and editorial work across print and screen.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Isidora Soft as a new version of a 2016 MyFonts bestseller, with rounded, soft terminals that give it a friendly and expressive look. The contemporary style, small x-height and classic proportions make it a strong candidate for headlines, logotypes, branding, books, magazines, motion graphics and web or TV applications. The Alt variant is pitched as the more expressive and playful of the two subfamilies.

name: Javiera
classification_notes: Geometric construction with humanist terminals; small x-height creates elongated ascenders and descenders; rounded, smooth stroke endings. Sits between the rigidity of pure geometric sans and the warmth of humanist sans.
summary: A geometric humanist sans with a deliberately small x-height, giving it a tall, elegant stretch that works well in branding and editorial settings.
description: Designed by Enrique Hernández and released in 2017, Javiera pairs geometric construction with rounded, humanist terminals to produce a typeface that reads as both clean and approachable. Its small x-height is the defining characteristic, lending an elongated quality that performs particularly well at display sizes. The 12-style family, spanning Thin to Black with matching italics and over 400 characters across 200-plus languages, covers most branding and publishing needs.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Javiera as a geometric sans-serif with humanist attributes, built around a small x-height that makes ascenders and descenders appear notably longer than the norm. Rounded terminals give it a smooth, friendly character well suited to branding, magazine work and publishing projects. The family includes six weights with matching italics, stylistic alternates, and broad multilingual coverage across more than 200 languages.

name: Jazmin
classification_notes: Contemporary serif that takes Globe Gothic's geometric proportions as a structural starting point and layers in serifs, adjusted curves and variable stroke contrast. The result sits between a text and display serif – controlled enough for short editorial copy, characterful enough for logotypes and packaging. The Alt subfamily introduces alternate letterforms for a more expressive register while sharing the same weight structure.
summary: A contemporary serif from Latinotype that reinterprets Globe Gothic's proportions with added serifs and variable stroke contrast, in eight weights with a more playful Alt variant.
description: Designed by Eli Hernández in 2019, Jazmin takes the geometric confidence of Globe Gothic as its structural departure point and builds in serifs, adjusted curves and stroke contrast to produce something more characterful and contemporary. The family runs Thin to Black with matching italics, while the Jazmin Alt subfamily offers more expressive alternate characters across the same weight range. With 566 glyphs and coverage for over 200 Latin-based languages, it has the range for editorial, branding and packaging work.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by Globe Gothic, Jazmin brings different proportions, curves, serif shapes and contrast to create something classy, playful and contemporary. The family is available in two variants – Jazmin and Jazmin Alt – each in eight weights with matching italics, recommended for magazines, short text, logos, branding, packaging and advertising.

name: Juana
classification_notes: High-contrast serif with extreme thick-to-thin stroke variation; structure blends geometric and organic shapes; positioned firmly in the display register; grew out of Latinotype's earlier Jazmín typeface, refined into a more developed and considered design.
summary: A high-contrast display serif from Chilean foundry Latinotype, offering eight weights with matching italics and a separate Alt subfamily across 200+ Latin-based languages.
description: Juana combines geometric structure with organic detail to produce extreme thick-to-thin stroke contrast that reads with authority at display and editorial scale. Designed by Ely Hernández, the Basic subfamily runs from Thin to Black with full italic coverage; the Alt subfamily adds eight further upright weights with alternate letterforms. Its broad language support and sharp elegance make it a strong choice for fashion, magazine and brand applications.
foundry_blurb: A typeface with a contemporary aesthetic built from a mix of geometric and organic shapes, each letter carrying a considered and unexpected character. The extreme contrast between thick and thin strokes gives the family a sharp, elegant look. It grew from the earlier Jazmín typeface, refined into a more fully developed design that keeps the spirit of the original while pushing its visual range further.

name: Juana Sans
classification_notes: A modulated sans-serif with pronounced stroke contrast — closer in optical weight to a high-contrast serif than to a neutral grotesque or geometric. The Display variant pushes that contrast for headline use; the Text variant pulls it back for body setting while preserving the family's editorial character.
summary: A 24-style high-contrast sans-serif system with separate display and text subfamilies, designed for editorial and branding work across over 200 Latin-based languages.
description: Juana Sans is split across two subfamilies: Juana Sans (16 styles, Thin to Black with italics) for headlines and display use, where extreme stroke contrast and precise curves carry the load, and Juana Text (8 styles), which softens that contrast for comfortable long-form reading while keeping the family's distinctive editorial register. The system covers over 200 Latin-based languages, making it a practical choice for multilingual publishing. It sits comfortably in magazine layouts, brand identity and digital editorial work where type needs to hold its character at every size.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Juana Sans as a typographic system built to explore "the full editorial spectrum" — the Display variant leads with high contrast and precise curves suited to titles and visual impact, while the Text variant softens those characteristics to give smooth, comfortable reading in long paragraphs without losing the family's stylised, editorial personality.

name: Julieta
classification_notes: Unicase condensed display face that merges uppercase and lowercase letterforms into a single visual register. Extensive swash alternates, ligatures and ornamental connectors give it a romantic, calligraphic quality without being a true script.
summary: A condensed unicase display face by Paula Nazal Selaive that layers swashes, alternates and ornamental connectors into a romantic lettering system with strong compositional depth.
description: Julieta blends uppercase and lowercase letterforms into a single visual register, using its unicase structure to generate warmth and compositional range. The Pro version contains 810 glyphs – alternates, ligatures, swashes, endings and ornamental connectors – while the Essential cut provides a more contained 247-character option. It suits headlines, logotypes and editorial layouts where a decorative, romantic display voice is the primary requirement.
foundry_blurb: A condensed unicase family inspired by romanticism, designed to be charming and versatile. Mixing uppercase and lowercase forms with alternates, ligatures, swashes and endings opens up a wide range of compositional possibilities. Ornaments, connectors and catchwords complete the display system.

name: Just Pixo
classification_notes: Drawn from pixação, the monumental Brazilian street-lettering tradition. Decorative serif capitals combined with sans-serif lowercase; strongly vertical axis designed for large-scale composition. Available as variable font spanning seven weights.
summary: A Brazilian street-art display face drawn from the pixação graffiti tradition, spanning seven weights and a variable font.
description: Just Pixo takes its DNA from pixação, the monumental lettering style stencilled across Brazilian cities. Designed by Monica Rizzolli and Tony De Marco, it pairs decorative serif capitals with sans-serif lowercase, both pulled hard toward the vertical axis. Seven weights and a variable format give it more flexibility than its street-art concept might suggest, though its home is firmly in headline and urban identity work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Just Pixo within what they call the king-size, monumental category: capitals systematically aligned and justified, their extreme verticality giving the face an architectural dimension rooted in the inscriptional traditions of Brazilian urban art.

name: Kahlo
classification_notes: High-contrast Latin display serif with strong horizontal hairlines and expressive swash alternates, drawing on 19th-century Mexican decorative typography. Structured around three subfamilies — Essential, Pro and Swash — each in four weights with matching italics. Positioned squarely for headline and branding use rather than text setting.
summary: A formal Latin display serif in three subfamilies and four weights, with swash alternates and initial capitals rooted in Mexican decorative typography.
description: Drawn by Luciano Vergara and released in 2012, Kahlo pulls from 19th-century Mexican decorative illustration to produce a high-contrast serif with refined letterforms and ornamental detail. The family spans three subfamilies — Essential, Pro and Swash — each in four weights with matching italics, totalling 24 styles. Swash alternates and initial capitals extend its range across magazine headlines, cosmetics packaging and logo work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Kahlo as a formal and elegant option for designers, drawing on Mexican decorative illustration as its visual reference. The family includes ornaments, initial capitals and alternate characters, with a dedicated Swash subfamily, suited to headlines, posters, logos and cosmetics packaging.

name: Kahlo Rounded
classification_notes: Latin-style display with rounded stroke terminals throughout; built on a humanist skeleton with ornamental detailing inspired by Mexican decorative illustration; the rounding is applied consistently rather than selectively, giving it a uniform softness distinct from the sharper original Kahlo.
summary: Kahlo Rounded softens the terminals of Luciano Vergara's Latin decorative display family to produce a warmer cut suited to editorial headlines, cosmetics packaging and logotype work.
description: Kahlo Rounded is the rounded companion to the Kahlo family, designed by Luciano Vergara and released by Latinotype in 2013. Soft terminal endings replace the sharper strokes of the original, giving the design a friendlier tone while preserving its Latin decorative structure. Twenty-five styles span four weights with matching italics, split across Essential, Pro, Swash and Decorative cuts, with initial capitals and alternate characters in the higher tiers.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Kahlo Rounded as the approachable sibling of Kahlo, with rounded stroke endings that soften the design while preserving its formal Latin elegance. The family includes initial capitals, alternate characters and a set of ornaments and patterns, with language support across Western European, Central European, Baltic, Turkish, Romanian and Pan Africa Latin.

name: Kenac
classification_notes: Roman skeleton with calligraphic stroke modulation and Victorian contrast ratios; high thick-to-thin differential places it closer to a Didone-influenced display serif than a straightforward transitional; works across display and editorial text settings.
summary: A high-contrast serif by Jorge Cisterna that draws on Roman, calligraphic and Victorian traditions across ten styles, built for editorial headers and brand identity work.
description: Kenac is a 10-style serif released in 2020, designed by Jorge Cisterna at Latinotype. It fuses Roman type structure with calligraphic stroke modulation and Victorian contrast ratios, producing a sharp thick-to-thin differential that reads well at display sizes. Five weights from Regular to Black, each with a matching italic, give it enough range to carry both headlines and extended editorial copy.
foundry_blurb: Kenac combines the traditions of Roman type with calligraphic influence and Victorian style, producing unusual shapes that remain functional. Its singular modulation and contrast between thick and thin strokes make it a natural fit for titles – book covers, magazine headers and brand identity work among them – while its italic variants extend its usefulness into continuous text.

name: Latina
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif rooted in calligraphy, deliberately neutralised for extended reading. Lowercase counterforms follow Edward Johnston's Foundational style; uppercase references classical Roman inscriptions; italics draw from the Cancellaresca (Canciller) tradition. Calligraphic origins are present but restrained throughout.
summary: A humanist sans-serif for continuous text, drawing from Edward Johnston's Foundational calligraphy and classical Roman letterforms across 11 weights with full italics and small caps.
description: A humanist sans-serif for continuous text, drawing from Edward Johnston's Foundational calligraphy and classical Roman letterforms across 11 weights with full italics and small caps.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Latina as calligraphy-based but deliberately neutralised so the letterforms don't pull the reader's attention away from the text. The lowercase takes its large, rounded counterforms from Edward Johnston's Foundational style; the uppercase echoes classical Roman inscriptions; the italic follows the Canciller tradition. Small caps and multiple numeral sets are included across all 11 weights.
designer: Luciano Vergara, Daniel Hernández, Rodrigo Fuenzalida

name: Latina Essential
classification_notes: Humanist text serif rooted in Edward Johnston's Foundational pen tradition. The uppercase follows classical Roman proportions with clear stroke modulation; the lowercase is open and rounded with generous counterforms. The italic draws from the Cancellaresca (Canciller) tradition. Latina Essential is a four-weight practical subset of the full 11-weight, 22-style Latina family, omitting small caps and the extended weight range.
designer: Luciano Vergara, Daniel Hernández, Rodrigo Fuenzalida
summary: A four-weight subset of Latinotype's Latina family, offering a humanist calligraphic serif for everyday editorial and branding work.
description: Latina Essential draws from the same calligraphic source as the full Latina family, grounded in Edward Johnston's Foundational style with a Cancellaresca italic tradition. The uppercase follows classical Roman proportions with controlled stroke modulation; the lowercase is open and rounded for sustained reading comfort. With four weights and their italics it covers the practical core of the range, though without the small caps, extended weight spectrum or full language breadth of the parent family.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Latina as a humanist text family rooted in calligraphy and Johnston's Foundational style, its calligraphic qualities deliberately moderated to sustain reader focus in long text while remaining expressive at display sizes. The italic is drawn from the Canciller tradition. The full family spans 22 styles across 11 weights, includes small caps in both roman and italic, supports 219 languages and offers multiple figure sets; Essential is a focused four-weight subset designed for everyday use.

name: Latino Gothic
classification_notes: A gothic sans-serif superfamily in the neo-grotesque tradition, organised around a systematic grid of five widths and nine weights with full italic coverage. No specific historical model is cited; the design is oriented towards contemporary visual communication rather than revival or historical reference.
summary: A disciplined gothic sans-serif superfamily from Latinotype, built across five widths and nine weights with full italic coverage, totalling 90 styles.
description: Designed by Alfonso García and the Latinotype team over two years and released in 2022, Latino Gothic takes a systematic approach to gothic sans-serif type: five widths from Compressed to Wide paired with nine weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic. The breadth makes it genuinely useful across contexts, from tight headline compression to expanded editorial settings, though the design itself is competent rather than distinctive.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Latino Gothic as a contemporary rethinking of the classic gothic design, built to meet the demands of 21st-century visual communication. With five widths and nine weights, they describe it as one of the most complete gothic families on the market.

name: Latino Gothic Variable
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque / Gothic sans superfamily packaged as a variable font. Continuous weight axis (Thin to Black, 100–900) and width axis (Compressed to Wide), covering the full range of the 90-style static Latino Gothic family. Variable axes make it highly versatile for both display and body use.
summary: A variable font condensing the entire Latino Gothic superfamily into a single file, giving continuous control over nine weights and five widths from Compressed to Wide.
description: Latino Gothic Variable packages 90 discrete styles — nine weights from Thin to Black, five widths from Compressed to Wide, with italics — into a single variable font file. Designed under the artistic direction of Alfonso García, it suits everything from tight display headlines to extended body text without managing a sprawling folder of separate files. The gothic grotesque structure keeps it neutral enough for editorial, branding and wayfinding, though it breaks no new ground in the category.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Latino Gothic Variable as the product of two years of work by their design team, describing it as a new interpretation of the original Gothic design focused on the demands of contemporary visual communication.

name: Letteria Pro
classification_notes: A five-weight calligraphic display family with broad nib pen and brush influences, paired with two caps-only mechanical variants (Slab and Sans) referencing De Stijl geometry. The trio structure is designed as a unified branding system rather than a text typeface.
summary: A seven-style calligraphic display family built on broad nib pen forms, paired with caps-only Slab and Sans variants drawn from De Stijl geometry.
description: Letteria Pro pairs a pen-influenced main family running from Thin to Black with Letteria Pro Caps in Slab and Sans cuts, the latter nodding to De Stijl mechanical forms. Ligatures and swashes extend its branding range, while coverage of more than 200 Latin-script languages makes it genuinely useful for international packaging work. The trio structure is coherent: contrast between the calligraphic body and the geometric caps is the design's core tension.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Letteria Pro as a typographic trio with the soul of a broad nib pen and the grace of a brush, built for branding and packaging. The Caps variants in Sans and Slab take their cue from De Stijl design, offering mechanical capital-only counterparts to the main calligraphic family. Together, the seven styles cover more than 200 languages within the Latin alphabet.

name: Los Lana Niu
classification_notes: Display typeface derived from the 2007 Los Lana. Curves are deliberately removed in favour of angular, irregular forms that read as handmade. Small caps and contextual ligatures distinguish it from simpler novelty display faces, giving it broader utility in editorial and branding work.
summary: A rustic display face with deliberate angularity and an irregular, hand-crafted rhythm, available in 24 styles across Pro, SmallCaps, Essential and Alt Essential subfamilies.
description: Los Lana Niu is a 2016 redesign of the 2007 Los Lana, by Bruno Jara and Luciano Vergara. The original's roughness is refined by removing curves, producing angular letterforms with an intentional irregularity suited to headlines, posters and branding. The full Pro version reaches 820 glyphs, with contextual ligatures and alternates available across all six weights.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Los Lana Niu as the matured evolution of the original Los Lana, preserving its rustic character while trading curves for a sharper, more angular texture. The family covers 24 styles across Pro, SmallCaps, Essential and Alt Essential variants, with stylistic ligatures and contextual alternates built in throughout.

name: Los Lana Pro
classification_notes: Single-weight handmade display typeface with individually constructed characters rather than a modular system. Irregular angled strokes create a curved impression without using curves. Strong Andean folk character. Includes ligatures, two sets of alternate characters and titling capitals.
summary: A single-style handmade display face from Luciano Vergara, its individually drawn characters built on angled straight lines that read as curved without using curves, lending it a distinctive Andean folk texture.
description: Los Lana Pro avoids modular construction in favour of individually designed characters, each carrying the variation and slight imperfection of genuine hand-lettering. Ligatures, two sets of alternates and titling capitals give designers enough to work with across branding, packaging and editorial contexts at headline scale. Language coverage is solid, spanning Western European scripts through to Central European, Baltic, Turkish and Pan Africa Latin ranges.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe it as a handmade display typeface built from straight lines meeting at angles of varying sizes, producing a curveless face that nonetheless feels curved. Each character is individually designed, with irregular shapes and broken lines evoking a handcrafted Andean hippie aesthetic. Optimised for larger sizes and recommended for branding, editorial, packaging and invitations.

name: Los Niches
classification_notes: Stylised monoline sans-serif with manuscript-inspired strokes and calligraphic loops. Decorative in intent despite its sans construction; positioned squarely as a display face.
summary: A stylised monoline sans with manuscript-derived loops that reads youthful in colour and quietly refined in black.
description: Los Niches pairs even-weight letterforms with calligraphic strokes and loops, sitting between a clean contemporary sans and a decorative display face. Designed by Juan Pablo de Gregorio and published in 2012, it comes in just two styles, which keeps its purpose narrow. It suits short-form display work – catalog headlines, magazine pull-quotes, product packaging – where the stylised personality can carry a layout without needing much weight range.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Los Niches as a stylised sans serif that blends modern monoline characters with strokes and loops drawn from manuscript lettering. They note it takes on a youthful quality in bright colours and an elegant, contemporary register in black, and position it for catalogs, magazines and product packaging.

name: Lota Grotesque
classification_notes: Geometric grotesque sans-serif with circular letterforms and restrained contrast. The four Alt subfamilies share identical weights and character counts but differ in default character selections, allowing typographic tone to shift without a font change. Sits in the tradition of Futura-adjacent geometrics but with a warmer, more functional disposition suited to extended reading and identity work.
summary: A seven-weight geometric grotesque with matching italics across four parallel Alt subfamilies, each sharing the same 760-character set but offering different default character selections for precise typographic control.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández and Rodrigo Fuenzalida at Latinotype and released in 2017, Lota Grotesque is a clean, circular grotesque built for versatility across identity, editorial and display work. Its defining feature is a system of four subfamilies that share identical weights and character counts but differ in their programmed defaults, letting designers shift typographic character without switching between unrelated typefaces. With 219-language support, small caps, discretionary ligatures and multiple figure styles across 56 total styles, it is a genuinely thorough geometric sans-serif.
foundry_blurb: The family spans four subfamilies that share exactly the same number of characters and styles, differing only in programming and default character choices. Seven weights from Thin to Black each include a matching italic, producing 56 styles in total. The 760-character set covers 219 languages and includes alternative characters, discretionary ligatures, small caps and a range of figure and fraction options.

name: Lota Grotesque One
classification_notes: Geometric grotesque sans-serif with seven weights from Thin to Black and a matching italic for each. The 'One' suffix suggests a first release in a planned extended system. Comprehensive OpenType feature set: small caps, alternative characters, discretionary ligatures, multiple figure styles and fractions. 760 characters covering 219 Latin-script languages.
summary: A well-specified grotesque from Latinotype with seven weights, full italics, small caps and 219-language Latin Extended coverage.
description: Lota Grotesque One is Daniel Hernández's 2024 grotesque for Latinotype, with seven weights from Thin to Black and a matching italic for each. The 760-character set includes small caps, alternative characters, discretionary ligatures and fraction support. Language coverage runs to 219, making it a practical choice for multilingual Latin-script work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Lota Grotesque One as a family offering high versatility and a wide range of typographic tools to meet different design needs. Designed by Daniel Hernández with Rodrigo Fuenzalida and the Latinotype team, it spans seven weights with matching italics and is equipped with small caps, alternative characters, discretionary ligatures, and figures and fractions for editorial, branding and interface work.

name: Love Story
classification_notes: Single-weight hairline display with soft, curved letterforms and geometric underpinning. Includes a companion Dingbats set of ornaments and decorative patterns. Romantic in character; designed for large sizes and short passages. Very limited in application scope beyond occasion-specific work.
summary: A thin hairline display typeface with soft curved letterforms and a companion ornament set, designed for large-scale use in short, romantically toned passages.
description: Love Story pairs a single-weight hairline display with a companion Dingbats set of ornaments and decorative patterns. It emerged from a collaboration between Luciano Vergara and Guisela Mendoza, blending geometric construction with ornamental warmth. Released in 2013, its reach is narrow – Valentine's Day and wedding-adjacent applications, with little utility beyond those contexts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Love Story as a display hairline intended for big sizes and short texts, with soft curves and a sweet style that give it what they call a lovely personality.

name: Ltt Recoleta
classification_notes: Display serif in the 1970s soft-serif tradition, drawing on Cooper and Windsor. Rounded, fluid letterforms with gentle angled strokes and stylistic alternates in upper and lowercase. Three widths (Standard, Condensed, Compressed) each running eight weights.
summary: A width-expanded update to Latinotype's flagship Recoleta, adding Compressed and Condensed variants to the 1970s-influenced display serif across 24 styles with Cyrillic support.
description: Ltt Recoleta expands the original Recoleta with two new width variants – Condensed and Compressed – each offering eight weights from Thin to Black. The family carries forward Recoleta's soft, 1970s-influenced letterforms and stylistic alternates, with Cyrillic added for broader editorial reach. Twenty-four styles across three widths give it genuine range for headline and branding work.
foundry_blurb: An expansion of the classic Recoleta, adding two condensed variants alongside the standard width – one very condensed and svelte, the other sitting at the midpoint between standard and condensed. Each of the three widths runs eight weights from Thin to Black, with stylistic alternates throughout upper and lowercase and support for the Cyrillic alphabet.

name: Lumiere
classification_notes: Display typeface drawn from Herb Lubalin's Serif Gothic, structured as a 14-style layered system. Styles split between multi-layer fonts with pre-built inline and shadow combinations, and single-layer bases for custom stacking. Retro-influenced with geometric underpinnings; not a text face.
summary: A 14-style layered serif gothic built for stacked headline effects, drawing directly from Herb Lubalin's Serif Gothic.
description: Lumiere takes Herb Lubalin's Serif Gothic as its reference and extends it into a layered font system of 14 numbered styles. The family divides into multi-layer fonts with pre-built inline and shadow combinations, and single-layer variants for designers building their own stacks. Designed by Jorge Cisterna and Bruno Jara in 2018, it suits album artwork, film posters and book covers rather than sustained text.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Lumiere as a display typeface with a strong personality yet neutral enough for a range of applications – balancing retro influence with a modern, simplified aesthetic suited to album covers, movie posters and book cover designs.

name: Macarons
classification_notes: Hand-drawn monoline display with calligraphic, ruling-pen roots. Character construction is gestural and non-modular. Supplementary subfamilies provide catchwords and ornaments alongside the main weight range.
summary: A hand-drawn monoline display face with a ruling-pen gestural quality, packaged with catchwords and ornaments for food packaging, menus and artisanal branding.
description: Macarons takes Garamond proportions as a loose reference and reworks them through hand-drawn letterforms rather than modular construction, giving the typeface a spontaneous, crafted feel. The family ships with a Sketch variant alongside dedicated Catchwords and Ornaments subfamilies, making it a self-contained toolkit for food, hospitality and printed ephemera. Its aesthetic is firmly tied to the artisanal food movement of the 2010s, which leaves it feeling dated outside that genre.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Macarons as a fresh, spontaneous display face drawing from the slow food movement, its hand-drawn characters delivering a handcrafted quality suited to cookbooks, menus, liquor labels, wedding stationery and specialty food packaging.

name: Magallanes
classification_notes: Contemporary neo-humanist sans-serif. Strokes and terminals are informed by humanist calligraphic traditions, softening the geometry typical of geometric or grotesque sans-serifs. Positioned primarily as a display and titling face.
summary: A neo-humanist sans-serif from Latinotype with calligraphic stroke character, spanning eight weights with true italics throughout.
description: Magallanes takes its cues from humanist calligraphy, with strokes and terminals that ease the rigidity common to geometric and grotesque sans-serifs. Designed by Daniel Hernández in 2012, the family covers UltraLight to Black across 16 styles with a true italic at each weight. It sits comfortably in editorial titling, magazine headers and logotype work where a warmer sans-serif is needed.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Magallanes as a contemporary neo-humanist sans-serif whose strokes and terminals reference humanist calligraphic construction. They describe it as a titling face suited to complementing text typefaces in magazine design, logotypes and editorial contexts, with alternative glyphs available for more dynamic typographic applications.

name: Magallanes Condensed
classification_notes: Contemporary neo-humanist condensed sans; stroke terminals carry calligraphic influence from the humanist tradition; 8 weights with true (not slanted) italics; designed for display and titling use; alternative glyphs across all weights.
summary: A 16-style condensed neo-humanist sans by Daniel Hernández, with calligraphic stroke terminals and true italics across eight weights, built for editorial titling and logotypes.
description: Released in 2013, Magallanes Condensed draws on humanist tradition through its calligraphic stroke endings, giving it more warmth than a typical geometric condensed sans. Eight weights run from UltraLight to Black, each paired with a genuine italic rather than a slanted roman. Alternative glyphs across all weights add typographic range, making it a dependable choice for magazine headlines, logotypes and editorial display work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Magallanes Condensed as a contemporary neo-humanist sans in a condensed width, with strokes and terminals drawn from calligraphic humanist tradition. The family covers eight weights from Ultra Light to Black, each accompanied by true italics and alternative glyphs. Positioned as a titling complement to text faces in magazines, logotypes and editorial contexts, with language support spanning Latin, Central European, Baltic, Turkish, Romanian and Pan African Latin.

name: Magallanes Essential
classification_notes: Contemporary neo-humanist sans serif with strokes and terminals that reference calligraphic humanist letterforms. Designed primarily for titling and editorial display use rather than continuous text.
summary: A neo-humanist sans serif with calligraphic terminal detail across four weights, built for headline and editorial titling work.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández and released in 2012, Magallanes Essential draws its character from humanist calligraphic traditions while maintaining clean, contemporary proportions. The family spans Light to Black with true italics throughout, and each weight includes alternative glyphs for added typographic flexibility. It sits most comfortably at display sizes: magazine headlines, logotypes and editorial composition.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary neo-humanist sans serif whose strokes and terminals echo the calligraphic conventions of humanist type. Intended as a titling companion to text faces in magazine layouts, logotypes and editorial design.

name: Magazine Grotesque
classification_notes: A display-oriented grotesque sans-serif with deliberate structural quirks: outstroke extensions on 'a' and 'e' that reach beyond the body, and a closed aperture on 'c'. These features produce an offbeat rhythm atypical of the grotesque genre, positioning it firmly in display rather than text use.
summary: A display grotesque by Daniel Hernández with eight weights, distinguished by outstroke extensions on 'a' and 'e' and tight apertures on 'c' that give headlines an offbeat rhythm without tipping into novelty.
description: Magazine Grotesque is a sans-serif from Latinotype designed by Daniel Hernández and released in 2020 for headline and title work. It spans eight weights from Thin to Heavy and earns its character through specific structural decisions – outstroke extensions on 'a' and 'e', and a closed aperture on 'c' – that distinguish it from standard grotesque templates. With 487 characters and support for over 200 Latin-based languages, it handles a broad range of editorial and branding contexts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Magazine Grotesque as a headline and title face built around unconventional design choices: outstrokes that extend beyond the letter body on 'a' and 'e', and a closed aperture on 'c', producing an unusual rhythm suited to logos, titles and short display text.

name: Majora Pro
classification_notes: Humanist slab serif with moderate contrast between thick and thin strokes. Includes a stencil companion subfamily for display and signage use. Small caps and alternate figure styles included.
summary: A humanist slab serif in 16 styles with a matching stencil subfamily, covering editorial, packaging and signage use across 200 Latin-based languages.
description: Majora Pro is a humanist slab serif drawn by Luis Bandovas and released by Latinotype in 2019. The main family runs Thin through Black with matching italics; a stencil companion covers the same weight range for headlines, titles and signage. At 750 characters with small caps and alternate figures, it handles both sustained reading and display setting with equal ease.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Majora Pro as a slab serif with humanistic features and moderate contrast between thick and thin strokes, suited to packaging, editorial, screen and signage work. The name derives from a Portuguese historical toy manufacturer. The stencil variant was designed specifically for titles, headings and packaging applications.

name: Mandioca
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with grotesque inflections. Wide proportions, closed terminals with straight cuts, large x-height and abbreviated ascenders/descenders. Selective stroke modulation in certain areas distinguishes it from more neutral geometric grotesques.
summary: A geometric grotesque by Sofia Mohr with wide proportions, straight-cut closed terminals and selective stroke modulation, spanning nine weights with full italic coverage.
description: Mandioca is a geometric sans-serif designed by Sofia Mohr and released by Latinotype in 2026, built on wide proportions and a large x-height that give it presence at both text and display sizes. Straight-cut closed terminals and abbreviated ascenders and descenders keep the design compact, while selective modulation in certain strokes adds character without departing from the geometric framework. The full span of nine weights with matching italics makes it a practical choice across branding and editorial contexts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Mandioca as a geometric family that pairs grotesque personality with wide proportions and a large x-height. Closed ends with straight cuts and short ascenders and descenders keep the design controlled, while notable modulation in selected areas gives it a timeless and distinct identity. They position it as a versatile tool for designers needing broad weight range and strong legibility.

name: Mandioca Variable
classification_notes: Geometric grotesque with grotesque warmth, characterised by wide proportions, straight terminal cuts, a high x-height and compact ascenders and descenders. Variable weight axis. The design sits between pure geometric construction and humanist grotesque, closer to the geometric pole.
summary: A geometric grotesque variable font from Latinotype, built around wide proportions, a high x-height and straight terminal cuts, with a variable weight axis for flexible typographic control.
description: Designed by Sofia Mohr and the Latinotype team, Mandioca Variable pairs a geometric structure with grotesque sensibility, giving the face a warmer, more characterful tone than a purely grid-derived sans. The high x-height and compact ascenders suit text across a range of sizes, while the variable weight axis allows fine-grained control over typographic colour. Wide proportions and straight terminal cuts maintain legibility and consistency at display sizes.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Mandioca as a geometric typeface that blends grotesque features with a distinctive personality. Wide proportions, straight-cut terminals, a high x-height and compact ascenders and descenders together give the face what they call an authentic, timeless identity. The variable format opens up flexible weight and style adjustments to suit a wide range of typographic applications.

name: Mangueira
classification_notes: Geometric construction with vertical terminals that lean toward the humanist tradition; distinctive g and k letterforms; OpenType swash alternates; Alt subfamily strips back expressive details for text and neutral titling use.
summary: A geometric sans-serif with humanist vertical terminals and OpenType swash alternates, spanning nine weights across a display-focused family and a more restrained Alt variant for text and neutral titling.
description: Mangueira is broadly geometric in construction, but vertical terminals and distinctive g and k letterforms pull it toward warmer humanist territory. The Alt subfamily removes the expressive details, offering a calmer option for body copy and neutral headlines. Eighteen styles across the two variants give it useful range across editorial, branding and broadcast contexts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Mangueira as a versatile release suited to editorial design, branding, packaging, web and broadcast, with swash alternates accessible via the OpenType menu, 502 characters and support for over 200 Latin-based languages.

name: Marcante
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque construction paired with geometric precision; designed exclusively for display and headline use; wide curves contrast with straight strokes; single weight axis via variable font; no italic, condensed or mono variants.
summary: A neo-grotesque display face from Latinotype that pairs geometric structure with a full weight range – Regular to Black – built for headlines that need to hold their ground at scale.
description: Marcante merges the upright solidity of a neo-grotesque with geometric construction, producing a display typeface focused on weight-driven presence rather than expressive detail. Six static weights and a variable font cover the range from measured to forceful, each step compressing the counters and thickening the strokes for denser impact. There are no italics or condensed cuts – the family is single-minded about vertical punch at headline scale.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Marcante as a typeface built to stand out from the first glance, its name kept in Portuguese to convey the intent: impactful, striking and memorable. The design holds the solidity of a neo-grotesque against the precision of a geometric, suited to compositions where type takes centre stage – extreme scales, overlaps, repetitions and typographic cuts where each heavier weight pushes the character toward demanding immediate attention.

name: Marsella
classification_notes: French humanist serif tradition of the 1960s, reinterpreted with modern proportions. Generous x-height, delicate serifs and balanced construction throughout. Includes a dedicated Poster variant for compact display use and 575 glyphs with alternates for visual flow.
summary: A 2025 humanist serif from Alexis Navarro drawing on 1960s French typographic tradition, with a generous x-height, delicate serifs and nine upright weights plus a compact Poster cut.
description: Marsella takes its cues from French humanist serifs of the 1960s, updating them with careful proportions and a refined, delicate construction across nine upright weights. The Poster variant offers a more compact, display-ready cut suited to large-scale settings. Alternative glyphs extend the full repertoire to 575 characters, giving the family reasonable flexibility across editorial and branding work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Marsella as a reinterpretation of the spirit of French humanist typefaces from the 1960s, brought forward with a modern, artisanal sensibility. Its generous x-height, delicate serifs and balanced proportions aim for a refined, timeless quality. Weights run from Thin to Black, with a Poster variant designed for compact, dynamic compositions, and alternative glyphs across a 575-glyph set to ensure harmonious visual flow.

name: Marylebone
classification_notes: Three-part display family: a handmade brush script with 519 characters including ligatures, initials and terminals; a geometric unicase sans-serif with alternates and ligatures; and a hand-drawn floral dingbat set. All three styles share a decorative, craft-lettering sensibility aimed at short-text display applications.
summary: A three-part display family pairing a handmade brush script with a geometric unicase sans and a floral ornaments set, all named after the central London neighbourhood.
description: Designed by Guisela Mendoza and Luciano Vergara, Marylebone pairs a loosely brushed, irregular script with a compact geometric unicase sans and a set of hand-drawn floral dingbats. The script carries 519 characters including ligatures, initials and terminals; the sans adds alternates and monogram-friendly characters. Built for short-text display work: packaging, branding, advertising and window displays.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Marylebone as a font trio inspired by the central London neighbourhood of the same name, created for short-text display applications such as advertisements, blackboards and shop windows. The collection pairs a hand-drawn brush script with a clean geometric unicase sans – complete with alternates and ligatures – alongside a hand-drawn floral dingbat set for decorative finishing.

name: Matcha
classification_notes: A paired family of two distinct styles: a sturdy reverse-contrast-capable slab serif and a calligraphic script. Neither style is intended for body text. The slab anchors the family; the script provides the expressive counterpart. Designed for display use in packaging and editorial contexts.
summary: A paired display family from 2016 combining a sturdy slab serif with a flowing calligraphic script, built for natural product packaging, cookbooks and wellness-adjacent branding.
description: Matcha pairs a stable, warm slab serif with a spontaneous handwritten script, the two styles designed to work in tandem across packaging, editorial layouts and brand identities. Swashes, ligatures, ornaments and reverse-contrast alternative characters give the family enough expressive range for varied display use. Guisela Mendoza and Luciano Vergara drew it with the contemporary wellness and natural food market in mind, and that context shows clearly in the aesthetic.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Matcha as a typeface that balances the energy of sport culture with the organic character of natural products. The slab brings stability and friendliness; the script evokes a handmade spontaneity with variable, free-flowing character forms. Together they suit natural food labelling, fitness brands, beauty publications and cookbooks.

name: Meeting
classification_notes: Wide-cap display sans with Copperplate Gothic influence. Solid strokes, defined cuts and generous spacing give it an upright, authoritative register. Three weights only; no italics, no condensed cuts.
summary: A three-weight display sans from Latinotype that channels the spare geometry of Copperplate Gothic into wide, confident capitals with a contemporary edge.
description: Meeting pairs broad capitals with clean, precisely cut strokes and generous spacing, giving it a composed authority suited to packaging, festival posters and editorial headlines. The Light-to-Bold range is deliberately tight – no italics, no extended cuts – so it works best where a single upright voice carries the moment. The Copperplate Gothic influence is legible but restrained, landing closer to modern display than historical revival.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Meeting as a sans serif of wide capitals and firm proportions, carrying contained elegance inspired by the sobriety of Copperplate Gothic but updated for contemporary use. They position it as a serious typeface with the balance and freshness of a well-made cocktail, equally suited to coffee and spirits labels, festival posters, menus and handcrafted product design.

name: Merced
classification_notes: Light-only sans serif with curvy, expressive letterforms and a broad alternate glyph set. The design leans on character variation rather than weight range, making it a display proposition. The "curly" descriptor suggests calligraphic influence in the terminals and strokes.
summary: A light-only display sans by Daniel Hernández with curvy, relaxed letterforms and an extensive alternate glyph system for typographic variation.
