description: Merced ships in just two styles – Light and Light Italic – with its appeal built around a wide set of alternate characters rather than a weight range. The letterforms carry a curvy, casual character suited to editorial headlines and display settings. Language support covers Central and Western European scripts as well as Pan Africa Latin.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Merced as a fresh, curly and delicious sans serif, built around a wide variety of alternate types that they say offer endless possibilities for setting words, texts and paragraphs.

name: Mixta
classification_notes: Contemporary serif built around blending three terminal approaches (didone, transitional and sharp/modern) within a single family. Five subfamilies each explore a distinct terminal treatment. High glyph count with Cyrillic support. Designed by Rodrigo Fuenzalida, released 2020.
summary: A contemporary serif spanning 54 styles across five subfamilies, each exploring a distinct terminal approach – didone, transitional or sharp – within a shared typographic structure.
description: Rodrigo Fuenzalida's Mixta takes a genuinely unusual premise – combining didone, transitional and modern terminal types within a single family – and executes it across five subfamilies: Mixta Pro, Didone, Didone Alt, Sharp and Sharp Alt. Each subfamily explores a different terminal treatment while sharing the same underlying skeleton, making it coherent as a system rather than a collection of loosely related cuts. With 54 styles, Cyrillic support, small caps and over 1,200 characters across 200+ Latin-based languages, it carries real weight for editorial and branding work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Mixta as a contemporary serif with strong, defined features that grew from the idea of combining different terminal types within individual letterforms. Merging didone, transitional and modern aesthetics into one unified system, it spans five subfamilies and 54 styles, suited to editorial design, brand identity, advertising, television and social media.

name: Mixta Essential
classification_notes: Contemporary sans-serif that mixes Didone-influenced and sharp-cut terminal treatments across its letterforms. Three subfamilies — Didone, Sharp, Sharp Italic — distinguish the terminal handling. The Essential version is a stripped-down sibling to the full Mixta Pro, dropping Cyrillic, alternates and OpenType features in favour of a leaner offering.
summary: A leaner sibling to Mixta Pro that mixes Didone and sharp terminal treatments across three subfamilies, aimed at branding, advertising and social media work.
description: Mixta Essential is a contemporary sans-serif built around the idea of mixing terminal styles — Didone-influenced ball terminals alongside sharp-cut ones — to give its letterforms a singular character. Twelve styles span Light to Black across three subfamilies: Didone, Sharp, and Sharp Italic. The Essential version sacrifices the full Mixta Pro's Cyrillic support, alternate glyphs and OpenType features for a more accessible, stripped-back offering suited to branding and advertising contexts.
foundry_blurb: Mixta Essential is a contemporary sans-serif with characteristic and defined features, achieved by mixing different types of terminals to create a singular appearance. Drawn from Didone and classical letterforms alongside current design trends, it was designed specifically for branding, advertising, TV and social media. This Essential version offers basic Latin language support optimised for macOS and Windows, and does not include Cyrillic, alternate styles or OpenType features.

name: Moderna
classification_notes: Modernist geometric sans with neutral, upright construction across four weights; a full Unicase subfamily mirrors the main family, and alternate characters, arrows and labels extend its branding utility.
summary: A clean modernist geometric sans in four weights with matching italics and a full unicase variant, built for headlines, logos and short branding texts.
description: Moderna draws on the simplicity of Modernism to deliver neutral, upright letterforms across Light, Medium, Bold and Black. Each weight has a matching italic; the family is mirrored in a complete Unicase subfamily that offers a useful alternate character set for display and identity work. Alternate characters, arrows and labels add practical versatility for branding applications.
foundry_blurb: A sans serif family inspired by the simplicity of Modernism, with neutral, clean construction suited to short texts, headlines, logos and branding. Sixteen styles span both a standard and a unicase version, with alternate characters, arrows and labels included.

name: Moderna Condensed
classification_notes: A neutral, modern condensed sans-serif with geometric leanings. Four weights with italics, plus a unicase subfamily. Alternate characters, arrows and labels included. Designed for headline and display use.
summary: A clean, neutral condensed sans-serif spanning four weights with italics and a unicase variant, suited to headlines, logos and branding.
description: Moderna Condensed is a straightforward condensed sans-serif built for display and headline use. It runs from Light to Black, each with an italic, and a parallel Unicase subfamily adds a lower-contrast, mixed-case flavour useful for logo and poster work. Alternate characters, arrows and labels extend its range for branding applications.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Moderna Condensed as a modern condensed sans-serif — simple and neutral — aimed at short texts, headlines, sub-headlines, logos, posters and branding. The family ships with alternate characters, arrows and labels.

name: Moderna Grotesque
classification_notes: Contemporary grotesque rooted in early-to-mid 20th-century models. Geometric traits with precise terminals and clean curves. Includes alternate character sets for both geometric and straight variants, giving the family two distinct optical flavours within a single release.
summary: A clean 12-style grotesque from Luciano Vergara, drawing on early-to-mid 20th-century models with geometric and straight alternate sets for added flexibility.
description: Moderna Grotesque is a well-proportioned sans serif rooted in the geometric grotesque tradition, with precise terminals and balanced curves that hold up at both text and display sizes. Six weights span ExtraLight to Black, each paired with an italic, giving it a practical range for editorial layouts, branding and advertising. Alternate character sets offer geometric and straight variants, letting designers shift the family's character without changing typeface.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Moderna Grotesque as a grotesque sans serif with geometric traits, precise terminals and clean curves, drawing from early-to-mid 20th-century design heritage while being built for contemporary use. Alternate sets extend its expressive range with two distinct flavours – geometric and straight variants – within the same family.

name: Moderna Sans
classification_notes: American Gothic grotesque, drawing directly on Alternate Gothic as a reference. Three widths (Condensed, Standard, Extended) with five weights and matching italics across all — 30 styles total. No OpenType features mentioned beyond standard Latin character set.
summary: A three-width American Gothic grotesque with five weights and full italic coverage, built for editorial headlines and corporate branding across 200+ Latin-based languages.
description: Moderna Sans takes the American Gothic grotesque tradition — Alternate Gothic specifically — and delivers a clean, contemporary update. Designed by Luciano Vergara and Alfonso García and released in 2019, the family spans three widths (Condensed, Standard and Extended) with five weights and matching italics in each, totalling 30 styles. The range makes it genuinely useful for publication headline work and brand systems that need to stretch across sizes and contexts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Moderna Sans as a modern sans-serif inspired by American culture — a clean contemporary take on classic American Gothic typefaces like Alternate Gothic. They position it as a versatile three-width workhorse suited to newspaper and magazine headlines, subheadings, branding and corporate design, supporting over 200 Latin-based languages.

name: Mohr
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif with clean vertical stress and a nine-weight range from Thin to Heavy. The Alt variant introduces initial and terminal swashes on most uppercase and lowercase glyphs, giving the family a mild decorative register. Designed by Sofia Mohr, 2018.
summary: A humanist sans from Sofia Mohr spanning nine weights across two variants, with the Alt version adding swash terminals to most glyphs for a mild decorative edge in branding and display work.
description: Released in 2018, Mohr covers Thin through Heavy in both a standard Basic variant and a swash-inflected Alt, the latter applying initial and terminal swashes to most uppercase and lowercase glyphs. The design reads cleanly at body text sizes while the Alt styles work well at display scale for packaging and branding applications. With 27 styles in total and a full italic series on the Basic variant, it offers enough range to be genuinely useful without needing a second typeface.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Mohr as a neutral and contemporary typeface rooted in humanist sans-serif conventions, designed to function across everything from display to small text. It comes in three design versions — normal, Alt, and italic — with the Alt styles adding initial and terminal swashes to most glyphs to introduce a distinct personality suited to branding and packaging contexts.

name: Mohr Rounded
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with fully rounded stroke terminals across all characters. Shares its skeleton with the original Mohr family but softens every endpoint into a curved form, producing a warmer, more organic texture. Swash variants on most upper and lowercase letters add a calligraphic quality suitable for identity work.
summary: A rounded geometric sans in 27 styles, with swash alternates on upper and lowercase characters that push it beyond the typical soft-terminal workhorse into branding and packaging territory.
description: Mohr Rounded takes the skeleton of Sofia Mohr's original Mohr family and replaces every stroke terminal with a softened, curved end, giving the type a warmer and more approachable feel. The family spans three subfamilies, Normal, Alt and Italic, each across nine weights from Thin to Heavy. Initial and terminal swashes on most upper and lowercase characters extend its range into logotype and packaging work, where a geometric sans with some personality is often useful.
foundry_blurb: Mohr Rounded is a refined version of the original Mohr typeface, with curved, softer terminals that make it feel more organic and friendly. The family comes in three versions (Normal, Alt and Italic), each in nine weights from Thin to Heavy, totalling 27 styles. Initial and terminal swashes on most upper and lowercase characters make it well-suited to branding, packaging and identity design, while its range of weights keeps it usable from small text through to high-impact headlines.

name: Monckeberg
classification_notes: Oldstyle serif construction with Venetian ancestry expressed through a display lens; high contrast between thick and thin strokes with calligraphic diagonal stress; not suited to body text but strong in headlines and branding contexts.
summary: A high-contrast display serif drawing on 15th-century Venetian letterforms, with calligraphic diagonal stress across 36 styles in two subfamilies built for logos, editorial headlines and branding work.
description: Designed by Enrique Hernández and released in 2019, Monckeberg translates classical Venetian type structure into a contemporary display range. Strong stroke modulation and calligraphic diagonal stress give it a refined, expressive quality suited to short text, logos and editorial contexts. The Alt subfamily provides alternate letterforms for compositional variety, while coverage of over 200 Latin-based languages extends its practical reach.
foundry_blurb: Rooted in 15th-century Venetian typefaces, Monckeberg is an expressive display font built on high contrast between thick and thin strokes, calligraphic construction and diagonal stress. It comes in nine weights with matching italics across both the standard and Alt subfamilies, covering 511 characters and more than 200 Latin-based languages, aimed at logos, branding, editorial and web use.

name: Monroe
classification_notes: Serif with a Thin–Bold upright-only range and no stated Didone/transitional classification on the foundry page. Five stylistic sets offering swashes, discretionary ligatures and alternate glyphs point firmly toward display and editorial use rather than extended text setting. No italic or condensed variants exist in the family.
summary: A Latinotype display serif originally from 2010, re-released in 2018 with refined drawing and five stylistic sets of swashes and alternate glyphs across 207 Latin-based languages.
description: Originally released in 2010, Monroe was taken off sale in 2013 before returning in 2018 in a reworked edition with refined drawing and tighter spacing. Five stylistic sets provide swashes, discretionary ligatures and alternate glyphs, lending it well to display headlines and logotype work. The family covers 207 Latin-based languages across five upright weights, with no italic or condensed variants.
foundry_blurb: Monroe was first published in 2010, then quietly discontinued in 2013. It returned in a revised edition featuring improved drawing, better spacing, additional weights and expanded alternate glyph sets.

name: Moranga
classification_notes: Rounded, organic serif with strong 1970s retro character, drawing from faces like Cooper and Souvenir as well as the flowing forms of Café Brasil. Optimised for headlines and high-impact display use; the warmth of its letterforms also suits friendly editorial and branding contexts.
summary: A rounded retro serif by Sofia Mohr that draws from the organic warmth of 1970s faces like Cooper and Souvenir, offered across five weights with matching italics.
description: Moranga was designed by Sofia Mohr and released through Latinotype in January 2020, built for headlines and display work where personality matters. Its letterforms are fluid and rounded, rooted in the friendly retro tradition of the 1970s, drawing from Café Brasil's organic forms and the warmth of typefaces like Cooper and Souvenir. The family covers ten styles across five weights, each with a companion italic, and extends to over 200 Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype position Moranga as a contemporary serif with a strong retro personality, suited to headlines, display use and high-impact or friendly designs. Its design blends Café Brasil's flowing organic shapes with elements drawn from popular 1970s faces like Cooper and Souvenir.

name: Multiple
classification_notes: Low-contrast condensed humanist grotesque with brush-influenced sinuous terminals, rooted in early nineteenth-century grotesque structure and 1960s–70s Chilean mural and poster art. The family pairs five sans subfamilies with four slab subfamilies, all sharing the same condensed proportions. Alternate subfamilies (Alt I–IV) provide character alternates rather than width or optical variants.
summary: A 90-style family pairing condensed humanist sans and slab subfamilies, drawn from Chilean mural and poster arts of the 1960s and 70s, with sinuous brush-influenced terminals across four alternate character sets.
description: Designed by Alfonso García and released in 2018, Multiple pairs five sans subfamilies with four slab subfamilies, all built on low-contrast condensed proportions inherited from early nineteenth-century humanist grotesque. The sinuous, rounded and asymmetric terminals carry a clear brushstroke quality rooted in Chilean muralism, giving the family warmth without sacrificing structure. With five weights plus italics per subfamily and four alternate sets totalling 90 styles, it suits editorial work and branding that calls for cultural character.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype position Multiple as rooted in the murals and poster artwork of 1960s and 70s Chile. Its low-contrast condensed forms recall early nineteenth-century humanist grotesques, while sinuous, rounded and asymmetric terminals bring the energy of the brush. Spanning sans and slab subfamilies, the family is pitched at editorial use and logo design.

name: Muralista
classification_notes: Single-weight condensed display face with low contrast and humanist grotesque bones. Sinuous, rounded, asymmetric terminals read as brush strokes rather than constructed letterforms. Draws on early 19th-century humanist grotesque structure filtered through mid-20th-century Latin American street typography.
summary: A heavy condensed display face drawn from Chilean mural and poster art of the 1960s and 70s, with brush-like terminals and low contrast.
description: Muralista takes its cues from the boldly lettered political murals and propaganda posters of 1960s and 70s Chile. The letterforms are big, heavy and tightly condensed, with sinuous rounded terminals that carry the feel of a brush rather than a pen or punch. With a single regular weight, its use case is narrow but committed: display headlines, editorial accents, logotype work where a specific Latin American vernacular is wanted.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Muralista as a low-contrast condensed typeface inspired by Chilean mural and poster art from the 1960s and 70s. The heavy letterforms echo political propaganda painted on walls, with asymmetric, rounded terminations that evoke an artist's brush. It sits close to early 19th-century humanist grotesque in structure while carrying a distinctly mid-century Latin American character.

name: Namaste
subcategory: Paired calligraphy script and all-caps sans-serif
classification_notes: 21-font collection: a watercolour calligraphy script and a matching all-caps sans-serif, each in five weights (Thin–Black) across Essential and Pro tiers, plus a dedicated ornaments font. The Pro script unlocks a full OpenType feature set including swashes, alternates, ligatures and stylistic sets. The ornaments font draws on Hindu and Buddhist symbols – Mandalas, Yantras and motifs from Indian textiles and monuments.
summary: A watercolour calligraphy script paired with an all-caps sans-serif, built around a wellness and spiritual aesthetic with an ornament set drawn from Hindu and Buddhist symbols.
description: Designed by Guisela "Coto" Mendoza in 2018, Namaste is a 21-font collection comprising a calligraphy-based script and a companion all-caps sans-serif, each in five weights across Essential and Pro tiers. The Pro script includes swashes, alternates, ligatures and contextual alternates; a dedicated ornaments font rounds out the family with Mandalas, Yantras and other Indian motifs. The aesthetic is deliberately narrow – soft curves and watercolour warmth calibrated for essential oil packaging, yoga studios and spiritual publications.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Namaste as a font collection for wellness and spiritual design, comprising a watercolour calligraphy script and an all-caps sans-serif in five weights, each available as Essential or Pro. The Pro script unlocks a wide range of OpenType features including swashes, alternates and stylistic sets, while the accompanying ornaments font gathers Hindu and Buddhist symbols – Mandalas, Yantras and textile patterns – observed by the designer during a trip to India.

name: Neogrotesk
classification_notes: Neo-grotesque sans-serif in the tradition of Swiss grotesques, but designed with a South American sensibility. Five weights with matching italics across four subfamilies: Pro, Ess, Ess Alt and Small Caps. 770 glyphs with extensive OpenType feature support including alternates, ligatures, case-sensitive punctuation and multiple figure styles.
summary: A well-featured neo-grotesque from Chilean foundry Latinotype, spanning 40 styles across four subfamilies with a Latin sensibility its designers describe as "not of the Alps but from Los Andes."
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara and published in 2020, Neogrotesk covers five weights with matching italics across Pro, Ess, Ess Alt and Small Caps subfamilies – 40 styles in total. It sits in familiar neutral grotesque territory but carries a distinctly South American character that separates it from its Swiss predecessors. OpenType features are thorough: alternates, ligatures, small caps, case-sensitive punctuation, arrows and lining, old-style and tabular figures across 770 glyphs.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Neogrotesk as a versatile, functional workhorse with a neutral look and Latin flavour – built for editorial, corporate and advertising work. The foundry's tagline, "not of the Alps but from Los Andes," signals a deliberate departure from Swiss grotesque convention.

name: Nereida
classification_notes: High-contrast upright serif with decorative terminals and ligatures. Three widths (Condensed, Standard, Expanded) across seven weights; 21 styles total with no italic cuts – the maths rule out any italics in the family. Generous x-height gives it paragraph usability despite its display character. Positioned for editorial, beauty and packaging contexts.
summary: A high-contrast Latin serif spanning three widths and seven weights, with decorative terminals and ligatures suited to editorial, beauty and packaging work.
description: Designed by Luis Bandovas and released in late 2023, Nereida is a high-contrast serif with 21 styles across Condensed, Standard and Expanded widths. Its generous x-height supports comfortable paragraph setting while decorative terminals and ligatures give it character for magazine headlines and beauty branding. The family covers a full weight range from Thin to Bold but does not include italics.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Nereida as a delicate, luminous typeface with an expressive and versatile personality. Its high-contrast design pairs a generous x-height for strong paragraph readability with delicately crafted terminals and attractive ligatures – suited to magazines, headlines, logos, packaging and beauty products.

name: Nereida Variable
classification_notes: High-contrast serif with delicate terminals and generous x-height; variable font encodes weight and width axes spanning Condensed, Standard and Expanded at seven weights (Thin–Bold); no italic; designed for editorial and branding contexts
summary: A high-contrast Latin serif from Latinotype spanning three widths and seven weights as a single variable font, with delicate terminals and decorative ligatures suited to editorial and branding work.
description: Nereida Variable covers condensed, standard and expanded widths at seven weights from thin to bold, all in a single variable font. Its high contrast and delicate terminals make it a natural fit for magazine layouts, logos and beauty packaging, while a generous x-height gives it surprising legibility in moderate text settings. Decorative ligatures and initial letters extend its range for more expressive typographic compositions.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Nereida Variable as a delicate, luminous typeface with an expressive and versatile personality, suited to elegant typographic compositions across magazines, headlines, logos, packaging and beauty products.

name: Newslab
classification_notes: A slab serif synthesising characteristics from three Latinotype typefaces: Andes, Sánchez and Roble. Even stroke weight with sturdy serifs, designed to sit comfortably at display sizes while retaining legibility in editorial text settings.
summary: Newslab merges three Latinotype typefaces, Andes, Sánchez and Roble, into a sturdy slab serif built for editorial headlines, logotypes and poster settings.
description: A slab serif that draws on three in-house Latinotype designs to produce a face that balances authority with readability across a wide range of editorial contexts. Eight weights, each paired with an italic, give enough range for headline hierarchies and display applications. The Regular and Italic are available free; the full family of 16 styles requires a licence.
foundry_blurb: A slab serif combining elements from three Latinotype typefaces, Andes, Sánchez and Roble. The harmony across their shared features gives Newslab a neutral yet imposing character suited to editorial projects, logotypes and posters.

name: Nido
classification_notes: Childlike rounded display face with filled (Black) and outline (White) cuts, both available in italic. Companion Dingbats set included. Hand-crafted aesthetic suited to informal, expressive layouts rather than text or branding work.
summary: A childlike display family from Sofia Mohr with filled and outline cuts, a companion Dingbats set, and hand-crafted rounded forms built for party invitations, children's publishing and informal branding.
description: Nido is a five-style display family designed by Sofia Mohr in 2014. The Black and White cuts offer filled and outlined treatments of the same rounded, hand-crafted letterforms, built to be combined freely in a single layout. It suits children's publishing, party invitations and any branding that calls for a warm, informal tone.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Nido as a cute, funny, childish typeface made for logos, book titles, invitations, birthday cards, flyers, posters and advertising.

name: Niemeyer
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif grounded in Brazilian modernist architecture. The design pairs strict straight lines with the fluid organic curves characteristic of Oscar Niemeyer's buildings, landing somewhere between pure geometric construction and humanist warmth. The eight-weight range with matching italics and OpenType features (alternates, oldstyle figures) makes it functional across headline and text settings, not simply a novelty display face.
summary: A geometric sans from Luciano Vergara drawing on Oscar Niemeyer's architecture, pairing straight lines with organic curves across eight weights and their matching italics.
description: Designed after Vergara visited Brazil and observed calligraphic workshops there, Niemeyer balances rigid geometry against the fluid sweep of Niemeyer's buildings. The family runs from Thin to Black with a matching italic for every weight, and OpenType features include alternate characters and oldstyle figures. It covers logotype, advertising, editorial and corporate settings without committing fully to any one of them.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Niemeyer as inspired by the aesthetic of Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer, blending straight lines with abstract curves to produce a characteristic and recognisable style. Designed by Luciano Vergara with support from the Latinotype team, it is positioned for logotypes, advertising, publishing, branding and corporate work.

name: Nizzoli
classification_notes: Modular geometric sans where straight lines meet rounded corners, drawn from the product design vocabulary of Marcello Nizzoli (Olivetti, Necchi). Four subfamilies — standard, rounded, alt and alt rounded — each spanning seven weights with matching italics, totalling 56 styles.
summary: A modular geometric sans in 56 styles across four subfamilies, conceived as a tribute to Italian industrial designer Marcello Nizzoli.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara in 2017, Nizzoli draws on the geometric clarity and curved precision of Marcello Nizzoli's product work for Olivetti and Necchi. Four subfamilies — standard, rounded, alt and alt rounded — each run through seven weights with matching italics, giving the family strong range for headlines, posters and corporate identity.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype position Nizzoli as a modern sans serif tribute to Italian designer Marcello Nizzoli, built on a modular system of geometric shapes where straight lines meet rounded corners. The family of 56 styles is pitched as a workhorse for headlines, posters, corporate identity and advertising campaigns.

name: Nordikka
classification_notes: Condensed grotesque sans-serif with a large x-height and straight terminals. Draws from Scandinavian design principles – clean, unadorned forms – across four weights with matching italics. The condensed proportions push it firmly into the display/headline bracket.
summary: A condensed grotesque with a large x-height and straight terminals, drawing on Scandinavian design principles for clean, unfussy headline setting.
description: Nordikka is a condensed grotesque designed by Luciano Vergara and published through Latinotype in 2015. It spans four weights – ExtraLight to Black – each with a matching italic, giving ten styles in total. Straight terminals, a generous x-height and tight proportions make it well-suited to headlines and space-constrained display work.
foundry_blurb: Nordikka takes its design cues from Scandinavian tradition, with pure, clean and clear forms as its guiding principle. Though completed in Brazil, the typeface stays true to that Nordic simplicity, resulting in a condensed sans-serif built for clarity and visual economy at display sizes.

name: Nowstalgic
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif tempered by humanist details: soft rounded terminals, open apertures, and a mixed-bowl g with teardrop terminal. Dual-subfamily system (standard + Alt) with swappable alternates for g, c, s, f and uppercase variants. Inspired loosely by the Windsor typeface heritage. Consistent typographic colour across all six weights.
designer: Luciano Vergara, Jorge Cisterna, Daniel Hernández, Tania Chacana
summary: A contemporary geometric sans with soft rounded terminals and open apertures, drawing quiet warmth from the Windsor tradition across six weights and a built-in alternates subfamily.
description: Nowstalgic comes in six weights across two subfamilies – the standard cut and an Alt offering swapped-in character variants including alternate g, c, s and f. The design leans on soft geometry rather than strict construction, with consistent typographic colour across the range. It is pitched at branding, packaging and editorial work where a sans needs personality without eccentricity.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Nowstalgic as a contemporary geometric sans that preserves the warmth of the Windsor typeface while building a more considered typographic system – designed, as they put it, for brands that feel like something.

name: Oceanshore
classification_notes: Geometric display sans-serif with stencil-style counter interruptions built on a modular grid; the combination of clean geometry and cut-through strokes produces a retro-futuristic display character. Not suited to body text.
summary: A geometric display sans-serif from Pablo Moreno with stencil-cut counters and a retro-futuristic edge, offered in six weights with 550+ characters per style and coverage of 200+ Latin languages.
description: Oceanshore builds its letterforms on a geometric skeleton then breaks the counters with stencil-style interruptions, landing somewhere between modernist grid work and vintage poster type. Six weights from Thin to Bold give it real display range, though the aesthetic is specific enough to read as a single mood. It covers more than 200 Latin languages and includes alternates and ligatures throughout.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Oceanshore as a modern display sans with stencil characteristics grounded in geometric shapes, a combination they say produces a retro-futuristic look particularly well suited to prominent editorial headlines, posters and short display applications.

name: Olivetta
classification_notes: High-contrast serif loosely descended in spirit from Roger Excoffon's Antique Olive (a sans-serif), reinterpreted with pronounced thick-to-thin stroke variation. Contrast intensifies progressively across the weight range. Humanist proportions beneath the formal contrast; described by Latinotype as having a spontaneous, ironic contemporary character. Suitable for display at heavier weights; intermediate weights can hold body text.
summary: A high-contrast serif from Chilean foundry Latinotype, drawing on the spirit of Excoffon's Antique Olive and stretching it across ten weights with matching italics for editorial and display use.
description: Designed by Alfonso García in 2019, Olivetta takes Antique Olive as a loose conceptual starting point and reinterprets it as a high-contrast serif with marked stroke variation across lowercase letterforms. Contrast deepens progressively at heavier weights, making the family flexible: lighter cuts work in running text, while the bolder weights are built for posters, branding and short editorial headlines. The 400-plus glyphs per style include alternates, giving designers room to play with the face's stated spontaneous, ironic character.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Olivetta as sharing certain design features with Antique Olive while aligning more closely with the spontaneous, ironic sensibility of contemporary typefaces. The high contrast between thick and thin strokes in the lowercase gives words visual weight as images, with stroke contrast increasing as weights get heavier — from hairline cuts suited to refined headlines through to dense black styles built for posters and high-impact branding.

name: Organetto
classification_notes: Art Deco-inspired geometric sans-serif with straight-edge terminals. No italics; instead the family spans a 7×7 grid of weights and widths (49 styles total). OpenType alternates and titling features built in. Upright-only design aimed squarely at display and branding contexts.
summary: An Art Deco-inspired geometric sans spanning 49 upright styles across seven weights and seven widths, built for logos, wordmarks and display work.
description: Organetto draws from the structured lettering of Art Deco posters, translating straight-edge terminals and geometric rigour into a contemporary type system. Across 49 styles – seven weights from Hair to UltraBold by seven widths from Ultra Condensed to Expanded – it covers a wide range of display and branding scenarios. Three sets of OpenType alternates, catchwords and titling characters extend its flexibility without adding italic cuts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Organetto as a typeface inspired by the lettering found on Art Deco posters, designed to take full advantage of digital font technology. Available in 49 styles across seven weights and seven widths, with 397 characters supporting 180 languages, it is positioned as a versatile solution for logos, wordmarks and short display text.

name: Osbourne
classification_notes: Revival and refresh of Salem, originally cut by Keystone Type Foundry. Condensed proportions with an elevated x-height and a sharp, high-contrast character. Released as four subfamilies (Pro, 01, 02, 03), each covering five weights, with stylistic variants introducing wide alternatives for circular characters and varying degrees of sharpness.
summary: A condensed display revival of Salem by Keystone Type Foundry, redrawn with a sharp, contemporary edge and issued across four stylistic subfamilies.
description: Osbourne refreshes the historic Salem typeface from Keystone Type Foundry, tightening the proportions and raising the x-height to suit contemporary display applications. Four subfamilies – Pro, 01, 02 and 03 – each span five weights and introduce distinct stylistic variants, including wide alternatives for circular characters and shifts in sharpness. Cover extends to over 200 Latin-script languages plus basic Cyrillic.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Osbourne as a reworked revival of Salem, updated with condensed, high-x-height proportions suited to titles, branding and short display copy, with three stylistic subfamilies adding glyph-level variation beyond the standard version.

name: Pais
classification_notes: Contemporary grotesque with geometric construction and a wide x-height. Ships in two distinct versions: a neutral standard cut suited to editorial and text work, and Pais Alt with more expressive, characterful letterforms aimed at display and branding use.
summary: A contemporary grotesque with wide x-height and geometric leanings, offered in two personalities — a neutral standard cut for editorial work and an expressive Alt for logos and packaging.
description: Pais is a 36-style grotesque by Enrique Hernández, spanning nine weights with matching italics across both its standard and Alt subfamilies. The standard cut is restrained and versatile, comfortable in editorial, web and broadcast contexts; the Alt carries more distinctive letterforms, pulling it towards display and packaging applications. Character coverage is broad at 682 glyphs, supporting over 200 Latin-based languages and basic Cyrillic.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Pais as a contemporary grotesque drawing on early 20th-century references but with stronger geometric qualities and a wider x-height. The family offers two versions — a neutral standard for editorial and branding, and an expressive Alt with playful characters suited to logos and packaging.

name: Pantano
classification_notes: Single-weight handmade grunge script with alternate characters and ligatures. Rustic, organic aesthetic drawn from Amazonian references. Narrow display application only; not suited to running text.
summary: A single-weight grunge script from Latinotype, drawing on the rustic textures of Amazonia with alternate characters and ligatures for a rough, handmade character.
description: Pantano is a 2011 grunge script with a rough, handmade quality rooted in Amazonian aesthetics. Alternate characters and ligatures vary the letterforms, giving individual settings a more organic, naturalistic feel. With a single weight and a narrow aesthetic remit, it suits short display work where texture is the point.
foundry_blurb: A handmade grunge typeface inspired by the rustic character of Amazonia, using alternate characters and ligatures to bring a sensual, naturalistic quality to the written word.

name: Pantano Pro
classification_notes: Rough, organic display face drawn from handmade lettering traditions. Two distinct styles (Regular and Jaguar) share an Amazonian-rustic aesthetic with visible texture and irregularity. Sits firmly in the display/novelty category with no text-weight application.
summary: A rough, handmade display face by Luciano Vergara inspired by Amazonian rustic aesthetics, offered in two expressive styles with broad Latin language support.
description: Pantano Pro is a grunge display typeface drawing on the visual textures of Amazonia, designed by Luciano Vergara for Latinotype. It comes in two styles – Regular and Jaguar – with ligatures, alternate characters and an extended diacritic set added in the Pro revision. Coverage spans Central European, Baltic, Turkish and Pan African Latin scripts, making it wider-reaching than most novelty faces of its type.
foundry_blurb: A handmade grunge typeface inspired by the rustic character of Amazonia. The Pro update adds more diacritics, alternate characters and ligatures to give a sensual, naturalistic quality to the written word.

name: Pasarela
classification_notes: Thin-stroked display with a neutral, streamlined structure rooted in street fashion aesthetics; includes a Borders ornamental variant for layered graphic compositions; no condensed or mono variants.
summary: A thin-stroked display face drawn from street fashion culture, with two weights, italics and a Borders ornamental set for layered graphic compositions.
description: Pasarela pairs a streamlined silhouette with clean, thin strokes aimed at magazine covers, posters and screen graphics. Two weights with italics and a Borders ornamental variant round out the family, giving designers the means to layer type into decorative compositions. It works confidently within its mid-2010s fashion display register, though that specificity is also its ceiling.
foundry_blurb: Pasarela takes its cue from the new culture of street fashion – a global phenomenon spread through social networks and style bloggers. Designed to answer that eclecticism with a neutral tone and lean construction, it was built for blogs, magazines, posters and television.

name: Patagon
designer: Luciano Vergara, Miguel Hernández, Daniel Hernández
classification_notes: Woodtype-inspired grotesque sans available in three widths (Condensed, Regular, Expanded) at a single weight. Uppercase OpenType ornamental alternates enable textural variation. Designed purely for display and headline use; no text weight.
summary: A woodtype-inspired display sans by Latinotype, spanning three widths — Condensed, Regular and Expanded — designed for high-impact headline setting.
description: Patagon is a contemporary woodtype sans designed by Luciano Vergara, Miguel Hernández and Daniel Hernández for Latinotype in 2011. The family covers three widths rather than multiple weights, with uppercase OpenType alternates that add textural range within a single setting. It is strictly a display face, best used where visual punch matters more than typographic nuance.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Patagon as a contemporary woodtype sans built for fresh, high-impact sentences, featuring a mix of flavoured OpenType features and a three-width system designed to be mixed for striking typographic results.

name: Peckham
classification_notes: Contemporary geometric slab serif. Strong upright serifs sit on a clean geometric skeleton. Carries a slightly playful quality without departing from structural clarity. Stylistic alternates for A, R, Y and a provide modest flexibility. Named after the south London birthplace of Vincent Figgins, who first brought the slab serif to commercial type catalogues.
summary: A geometric slab serif by Daniel Hernández, named after the south London birthplace of type pioneer Vincent Figgins, with eight weights and full italic coverage across 16 styles.
description: Designed in 2018 by Daniel Hernández, Peckham draws its name from the area of south London where Vincent Figgins was born, the designer credited with bringing the slab serif to commercial type catalogues. Its geometric structure carries strong, upright serifs that give it a slightly playful character without sacrificing readability at text sizes. Stylistic alternates for A, R, Y and a offer a small degree of expressive range, and 395 glyphs cover 94% of Latin-script languages.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Peckham as a contemporary and versatile slab serif with strong serifs that lend it a playful quality while preserving its overall geometric structure. The name is a tribute to the London neighbourhood of Peckham, birthplace of Vincent Figgins, the type designer credited with first offering slab serifs in commercial catalogues.

name: Phase Grotesk
classification_notes: Low-contrast grotesque with uniform strokes and closed apertures. Curves are tensioned and slightly compressed, deliberately avoiding geometric regularity in favour of a technical quality. Design draws on early twentieth-century signage tradition, retaining the weight mismatches and optical inconsistencies of vintage sans serifs as intentional features rather than correcting them.
summary: A low-contrast grotesque rooted in early twentieth-century signage, with closed apertures and slightly compressed curves that lend it a quiet, technical character.
description: Phase Grotesk spans 8 weights with matching italics – 16 styles in total – covering editorial, branding and interface work with ease. Its closed apertures and deliberately retained stroke inconsistencies reference vintage sans serifs rather than geometric purity. The design holds its character at display scale while remaining legible and unassuming at text sizes.
foundry_blurb: Phase Grotesk is built on a principle of low contrast, with uniform strokes producing a stable, rhythmic texture on the page. Curves are tensioned and slightly compressed, drawing from early twentieth-century signage and independent type foundries rather than geometric idealism. Closed apertures and retained optical irregularities – weight mismatches and uncorrected adjustments – give the face an authentic, understated quality suited to high-impact compositions and everyday typography alike.

name: Pincoya Black Pro
classification_notes: High-contrast display face drawn from Spanish Civil War poster lettering and Chilean political graphics. Bold, declarative character suited to headlines and logotypes. Two styles with extensive OpenType alternates.
summary: A high-contrast display face drawn from Spanish Civil War poster lettering, with OpenType alternates adding compositional range.
description: Pincoya Black Pro takes its visual reference from the bold lettering of a Spanish Civil War poster, shaped further by graphics associated with La Unidad Popular, the Chilean political coalition of the 1970s. It comes in two styles and carries a set of OpenType alternates, giving it flexibility for headline and logotype use. The historical source material lends it a weight and grit that separates it from generic blackletter revivals.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe it as ideal for high-impact sentences, logotypes, magazine layouts and poster design. The typeface includes numerous alternate characters in OpenType format to support compositional variety across display applications.

name: Princesa
classification_notes: Contemporary high-contrast serif with classical Roman roots; two subfamilies — standard and Alt — the latter offering around 40 alternate characters via four stylistic sets; full Cyrillic support alongside extended Latin; no condensed widths or optical sizes.
summary: A high-contrast serif spanning 36 styles across two subfamilies, developed over two years by Ely and Enrique Hernández with Cyrillic support and around 40 character alternates via four stylistic sets.
description: Princesa draws from classical Roman letterforms and reworks them with high contrast and contemporary proportions, pitched at editorial, headline and branding work. Nine weights from Thin to Heavy each carry an italic, and a parallel Alt subfamily unlocks a substantial set of character alternates. Cyrillic support alongside extended Latin gives it genuine range across multilingual projects.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Princesa as taking inspiration from classic Roman fonts while addressing contemporary typographic challenges. Developed over two years through a collaboration between Enrique and Ely Hernández, the family aims to combine classical elegance with an updated perspective, intended for editorial design, headlines, branding and advertising.

name: Printa
classification_notes: Dual-layer ornamental/pattern typeface. Two complementary sets (Printa A and Printa B) combine via uppercase/lowercase layering to simulate the misregistered look of 1970s silkscreen textile printing. No conventional weight axis; functions primarily as a pattern generation system rather than a text face.
summary: A dual-layer pattern typeface by Guisela Mendoza that mimics the misregistered look of 1970s silkscreen printing, pairing two complementary sets to generate repeat textile patterns.
description: Printa comes in two complementary sets – Printa A and Printa B – designed to be overlaid, with uppercase characters forming one layer and lowercase the other, producing the off-register charm of 70s screen-printed fabric. The underlying concept draws on mandalic symmetry and the deliberate imperfections of serigraphy. It works as a pattern-generation tool rather than a conventional text face, with a very narrow scope of application.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Printa as drawing on the visual language of misregistered silkscreen printing from the 1970s. The front/back layer system – uppercase for one pass, lowercase for the other – lets designers combine characters into a wide variety of repeat print patterns, with results that carry the handmade quality of artisanal textile work.

name: Prêt-à-porter
classification_notes: A three-subfamily script system: Contrast (calligraphic thick-thin modulation), Linear (monolinear stroke), and Slab (a serifed extension of the handwritten aesthetic). Each script subfamily ships with a companion Ornament style featuring connectable initial and terminal forms. The Slab variant is an unusual structural extension for a handwritten system.
summary: A cheerful handwritten script system by Juan Pablo de Gregorio, spanning three subfamilies – Linear, Contrast and Slab – with connectable ornament forms and coverage across 208 languages.
description: Designed in 2016, Prêt-à-porter is built around an expressive, smooth-curved handwriting aesthetic with a deliberately carefree character. The system runs across three distinct families: a contrast script with calligraphic thick-thin modulation, a monolinear linear variant for a more casual feel, and an unexpectedly useful slab extension. Each script subfamily includes companion ornament styles with connectable initial and terminal forms designed to integrate naturally with the letterforms.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype position Prêt-à-porter as carefree, wild and cheerful in character, with smooth curves and a strong typographic identity. The Contrast subfamily is described as the more elegant, formally refined option within the system. The ornament styles are designed as connectable initial and terminal forms, giving typographers a way to add decorative flourishes that read as part of the script itself.

name: Queulat
classification_notes: Hybrid sans-serif combining Grotesk structural rationality with Modern-influenced teardrop terminals. The Alt subfamily makes those terminals more pronounced – particularly on 'k' and 'v' – while the standard cut is the quieter option. A single unicase style completes the family for decorative display use. Overall character is closer to a humanist sans than a pure grotesque, owing to the organic terminal treatment.
summary: A 25-style hybrid sans from Jorge Cisterna that pairs Grotesk structure with Modern teardrop terminals, available in standard, Alt and unicase variants.
description: Queulat blends the rational skeleton of a Grotesk with Modern-style teardrop terminals – most visible in the Alt subfamily on characters like 'k' and 'v'. The standard cut keeps those details quieter, while the single unicase style pushes toward expressive display use. Six weights and italics across two full subfamilies give it enough range for identity and heading work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Queulat as a typeface that combines two distinct stylistic traditions, reflecting charm, freshness and a strong personality. The Regular is the more restrained option; the Alt version brings out Modern styling through pronounced teardrop terminals. The unicase variant introduces a wider range of letterform shapes for a colourful display register.

name: Queulat Condensed
classification_notes: Blends Grotesk geometry with Modern-style teardrop terminals throughout. Two subfamilies: Cnd (cleaner, simpler) and Cnd Alt (more pronounced Modern detailing on letterforms including k and v). All weights are condensed; positioned for headings, subheadings and editorial display rather than body text.
summary: A 24-style condensed hybrid sans by Jorge Cisterna that grafts Modern teardrop terminals onto a Grotesk skeleton, with two subfamilies offering different levels of ornamentation.
description: Queulat Condensed sits at the junction of Grotesk rationality and Modern type detailing, its teardrop terminals lending warmth to an otherwise tightly structured condensed form. The Cnd Alt subfamily pushes the Modern character further, adding ornamental touches to letterforms like k and v for a more expressive result. Six weights with italics across both variants give it enough range for editorial, publishing and display work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Queulat Condensed as a hybrid typeface that brings charm, freshness and a strong personality by drawing from different typographic traditions. The condensed proportions suit publishing and subheading contexts, and the two subfamilies let designers choose between a cleaner Grotesk-led approach and a more ornamented Modern-influenced alternative.

name: Queulat Soft
classification_notes: Hybrid typeface merging Modern and Grotesque traditions. Teardrop terminals are the primary Modern-derived detail; rational proportions and overall structure lean Grotesque. Regular and Alt variants differ in how prominently the Modern characteristics appear – the Alt cut features more visible teardrop detail on characters such as 'k' and 'v'. Comes in standard and condensed widths, each with an Alt counterpart.
summary: A 48-style Modern–Grotesque hybrid with teardrop terminals, available across standard and condensed widths in regular and Alt cuts.
description: Queulat Soft merges Grotesque rationality with Modern-influenced teardrop terminals, giving it enough personality for logotype and display work without sacrificing structural clarity. Four subfamilies span standard and condensed widths, each in a regular and an Alt cut – the Alt leaning further into the Modern with more prominent teardrop detail on characters like 'k' and 'v'. Six weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, make it a practical choice across varied type hierarchies.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Queulat Soft as a hybrid typeface blending Modern and Grotesk traditions to produce something fresh and characterful. Teardrop terminals – most visible in the Alt cut's 'k' and 'v' – are its signature detail, while the Grotesque-derived proportions keep it stable for headings, subheadings and logotype use.

name: Ragazza Script
classification_notes: High-contrast copperplate-inspired script with modern structural elements. Single style. Over 1,000 glyphs with extensive OpenType alternates, swashes and initial capitals. Display only — not suited to body text.
summary: A single-weight display script that crosses ornamental Copperplate with modern high contrast, backed by over 1,000 glyphs and a full suite of OpenType alternates for headline work.
description: Originally developed as a university project at the University of Buenos Aires in 2006, Ragazza Script blends ornamental Copperplate tradition with a high-contrast modern structure. A single weight carries over 1,000 glyphs, including extensive alternates, swashes and initial capitals, which gives designers wide compositional range within the style. Its territory is headlines and short phrases — it is not body text material.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Ragazza Script as a display typeface that sits between ornamental Copperplate and high-contrast modern letterforms, offering an expressive alternative to conventional calligraphy. Designed by Guille Vizzari and published in 2012, it draws on more than 1,000 glyphs and a broad set of OpenType features to give designers near-unlimited compositional flexibility for display use.

name: Rawson
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif drawing explicitly on Johnston and Gill as references. Combines geometric construction with humanist warmth — large x-height, open counterforms, classical proportions. Three subfamilies (Rawson, Rawson Pro, Rawson Alt) each spanning ten weights with matching italics, totalling 60 styles.
summary: A humanist sans-serif drawing on Johnston and Gill, available across 60 styles in three subfamilies with broad language coverage.
description: Rawson pairs geometric structure with humanist warmth, featuring a large x-height, open counterforms and classical proportions. It comes in three subfamilies — Rawson, Rawson Pro and Rawson Alt — each spanning ten weights with matching italics. The 778-character set covers 219 languages and includes small caps, multiple figure styles and discretionary ligatures, making it a capable choice for branding, packaging and signage.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Rawson as a modern interpretation of the English humanist tradition, citing Johnston and Gill as its primary reference points. The family combines the rigour of geometric construction with the warmth of humanist letterforms, aiming for a classical personality that holds up across display and text contexts.

name: Rebrand
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif in 33 styles split across Display (9 weights × 2 + alternates and swashes) and Text (7 weights × 2) optical-size variants, plus a single Dingbats weight. Circular, symmetrical construction is tempered by friendlier details. Both subfamilies include small caps and basic Cyrillic support. Display carries the expressive end of the range; Text restrains itself for body-copy legibility.
summary: A 33-style geometric sans-serif split into Display and Text optical variants, with small caps and basic Cyrillic in both, built for branding systems that need a friendly but structured voice.
description: Rebrand separates its workload cleanly: the Display subfamily (18 styles) carries alternates, swashes and expressive weight contrast for headline use, while the Text cut (14 styles) holds the same geometric personality at a calmer register for body copy. Both share small caps and basic Cyrillic, and a Dingbats weight rounds out the system. It is a competent branding family with good breadth, though it does little to distinguish itself in the crowded geometric sans category.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Rebrand as a geometry-first family that resists the coldness of pure mathematics in favour of a more jovial, approachable personality. The Display subfamily is designed for fluidity and dynamism; the Text subfamily applies the same character at a more measured pace for running text. Between them, the family is intended to cover a full branding system from titles and marks to body copy.

name: Recoleta
classification_notes: 1970s-inflected display serif drawing on Cooper and Windsor; soft rounded letterforms combined with fluid angled strokes; warm and approachable mood across a broad weight range; primary use case is headlines and branding, though lighter weights extend to body text
summary: A 1970s-inspired display serif by Jorge Cisterna that draws on Cooper and Windsor, blending rounded organic warmth with fluid angled strokes into something retro in feel but considered in execution.
description: Designed in 2018, Recoleta pulls its shapes from popular 1970s typefaces, combining the soft rounded forms of Cooper with the quieter refinement of Windsor. Seven weights run from Thin through to Black, with lighter cuts serviceable for body text and heavier ones built for confident headlines. A separate Alt subfamily adds stylistic alternates, and the full family includes Russian Cyrillic support.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype's best-selling typeface, Recoleta combines ingredients from popular 1970s designs to produce soft, gentle shapes alongside fluid angled strokes. It is pitched as familiar yet fresh and suits logos, business cards and editorial work, with two subfamilies, multiple weights and stylistic alternates throughout.

name: Regia Sans Pro
classification_notes: Ultra-condensed, single-weight display sans-serif with modular construction. Thin proportions and tight fitting suit editorial headlines and logo work. OpenType feature set includes ligatures, swash characters and two groups of alternates; character set reaches Pan Africa Latin.
summary: A single-weight ultra-condensed display sans by Chilean designer Luciano Vergara, built for headlines, logos and posters, with over 1,300 characters covering Latin-script languages across Europe and Africa.
description: Regia Sans Pro is an ultra-condensed, thin-weight sans-serif with a modular structure, designed by Luciano Vergara in Concepción, Chile. Originally conceived in 2008 and released by Latinotype in 2011, the Pro version expands on the original with OpenType features including swash characters, multiple ligatures and two sets of alternates. Language coverage spans Western and Central European scripts through to Pan Africa Latin, giving it broad reach for international display use despite its single-weight limitation.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Regia Sans as a very thin, condensed typeface with a modular design, well-suited to short texts, logos, magazines and posters. The Pro edition comprises over 1,300 OpenType characters with multiple ligatures (including diacritical marks and numerals), swash characters and two groups of alternates for typographic variety.

name: Resort
classification_notes: Dual-typeface collection pairing a casual handwritten script (5 weights) with a high-contrast all-caps geometric sans-serif (6 weights) and a set of floral ornaments. Script is the lead face; the sans carries marked thick-thin stroke contrast. Themed around a beach-holiday aesthetic throughout.
summary: A twelve-style paired collection combining a flowing casual script with a high-contrast all-caps sans, built for lifestyle branding and editorial work with a deliberate summery, leisure character.
description: Designed by Guisela Mendoza and Luciano Vergara in 2018, Resort pairs a casual handwritten script in five weights with a geometric all-caps sans in six, plus a set of floral ornaments. The sans carries pronounced contrast between thick and thin strokes, lending the pairing some elegance against the script's warmth. The collection is suited to lifestyle brands, magazine layouts, invitations and social content where a beach-holiday mood is the brief.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Resort as a high-versatility dual-typeface collection designed for magazines, blogs, logos, invitations and social content, evoking a relaxed coastal mood through the pairing of a casual script and a sophisticated all-caps sans.

name: Revista
designer: Paula Nazal Selaive, Daniel Hernández and Marcelo Quiroz
classification_notes: High-contrast Didone serif at its core, extended into a six-subfamily system with script, inline, stencil, dingbat and ornament variants. Hairline-to-black contrast ratio and vertical stress are firmly in the Didone tradition; the decorative subfamilies push it firmly into display territory.
summary: A 26-style Didone editorial system built for fashion magazine work, combining high-contrast serif, script, stencil, inline and ornament variants in a single cohesive family.
description: Designed by Paula Nazal Selaive, Daniel Hernández and Marcelo Quiroz and released in 2015, Revista draws on classic Didone conventions – extreme stroke contrast, delicate hairlines, vertical stress – and extends them across six subfamilies. The script brings contextual alternates and discretionary ligatures; the stencil and inline variants expand the decorative range; dingbat and ornament sets complete a self-contained editorial toolkit. It is most at home in fashion and luxury contexts where the Didone register is already the expected visual language.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype position Revista as a typographic system that brings together everything needed to undertake a fashion magazine project, blending a high-contrast Didone serif with script, stencil and inline treatments, plus dingbats and ornaments, across 26 styles in a single family.

name: Ride my Bike
classification_notes: Casual handwritten script with a street/urban cycling aesthetic. Three-subfamily structure: Pro (ligatures and alternates, 600+ glyphs), Essential (standard OpenType, no extras) and Dingbat (91 cycling-themed ornaments). Regular and Bold weights, each with italic, give it more range than a typical novelty script — but the aesthetic is narrow.
summary: A casual handwritten script from Chilean foundry Latinotype, built around a street cycling aesthetic, with Pro, Essential and Dingbat subfamilies covering headlines and lifestyle branding.
description: Designed by Guisela Mendoza in 2012, Ride my Bike draws on street style and urban cycling culture to produce a lively casual script with Regular and Bold weights, each with italic. The Pro subfamily adds ligatures, alternate characters and a 600+ glyph set; the Dingbat companion contributes 91 cycling-themed ornaments. Best suited to headline work and lifestyle branding where an energetic hand-drawn quality is the brief.
foundry_blurb: A fresh handmade typeface inspired by street style and the culture of cycling around the city. Intended for headlines, brands and fashion photography.

name: Ride my Bike Serif
classification_notes: Structured serif with hand-drawn terminals and rough texture, derived from the brush-lettered Ride My Bike. Headline-only — the handmade construction rules out body text use. Three subfamilies: Pro (full OpenType feature set including alternates and ligatures), Essential (simplified, no OpenType extras), and Ornaments (121 cycling-themed dingbats). Urban/street-culture inspiration throughout.
summary: A hand-drawn display serif spun off from Guisela Mendoza's Ride My Bike, with rough terminals and a street-cycling character suited to headlines and editorial branding.
description: Ride my Bike Serif translates the original brush-lettered Ride My Bike into a structured serif with deliberately rough, handmade terminals and an urban edge. The Pro subfamily adds OpenType alternates and ligatures; the Essential variant strips these back for simpler implementations. A separate Ornaments font provides 121 cycling-themed dingbats, extending the typeface's usefulness for themed branding work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe it as drawn from street style and the urban cycling culture that moves through cities on two wheels, positioning it for headlines, brand work and fashion photography.

name: Rita
classification_notes: Slab serif with a wide weight and width range, from condensed thin to a dedicated Poster weight. The letterforms carry a strong vertical axis and rigid slab construction, giving each weight a distinct display personality. Lacks italics across the family.
summary: A ten-weight display slab ranging from condensed thin to poster-weight heavy, with broad Latin Extended language coverage but no italic companion.
description: Rita began as a single-style project in 2010 and was developed into a full ten-weight family by Daniel Hernández and Rodrigo Fuenzalida, released by Latinotype in 2018. The weight range runs from condensed thin settings through to a dedicated Poster cut, making it well-suited to headline and impact-led work. The absence of italics keeps it firmly in upright display territory.
foundry_blurb: Rita covers a wide range of weights and widths for building varied compositions, from condensed light text to heavyweight poster display. Its 400-character set supports over 200 languages.

name: Roble
classification_notes: Slab serif display family positioned between Latinotype's own geometric sans Andes and their slab Sanchez. Sturdy slab construction with eight weights from Thin to Black, each paired with a matching italic. Designed for headline and display use rather than extended text setting.
summary: A sixteen-style slab serif display family that draws on Latinotype's own Andes and Sanchez to occupy the space between a geometric sans and a traditional slab.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández in 2013, Roble borrows the proportions of Latinotype's geometric sans Andes and the slab construction of their Sanchez, settling into the territory between them. Eight weights from Thin to Black each carry a matching italic, giving the family solid range for headline and display work. The result is direct and confident rather than fussy, with enough weight spread to hold its own in editorial and branding contexts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Roble as a blend of their Andes sans-serif and Sanchez slab, combining both into a single display family with what they call a fresh and dynamic character.

name: Roble Alt
classification_notes: Slab serif display family conceived as an alternate-letterform counterpart to the base Roble, drawing from Latinotype's Andes (geometric sans) and Sanchez (slab serif) lineages. Eight weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic, give a strong weight axis for a display-first family.
summary: A slab serif display family from Latinotype offering alternate letterforms to the base Roble, spanning eight weights with matching italics and bridging the foundry's Andes sans and Sanchez slab traditions.
description: Roble Alt is Daniel Hernández's 2013 display slab, designed as a stylistic counterpart to the base Roble family with alternate character forms throughout. The eight-weight range from Thin to Black, each paired with an italic, gives reasonable versatility across headline and editorial applications. It sits within a coherent design system in Latinotype's catalogue, deliberately positioned between their geometric sans and slab serif lineages.
foundry_blurb: A slab serif family built from a blend of Andes and Sanchez, combining the openness of a sans with the structure of a serif to achieve a fresh, dynamic result across 16 display styles.

name: Romeo
classification_notes: Condensed, unicase display family with extensive decorative apparatus: swashes, alternates, ligatures, ornamental connectors and catchwords. Romantic and theatrical in character. Pro version includes 810 glyphs across Regular and Italic; Essential version covers 247 characters.
summary: A condensed unicase display family from 2012, built around swashes, alternates and ornaments for romantic headline work.
description: Romeo pairs a condensed structure with unicase construction and layers in swashes, ligatures, alternate characters and ornamental connectors. The Pro version reaches 810 glyphs across Regular and Italic cuts; an Essential version covers 247 characters for simpler projects. It is a single-purpose display face suited to wedding stationery, theatrical editorial headers and branding that calls for overt romanticism.
foundry_blurb: Designed as a companion to Latinotype's Julieta, Romeo is a condensed unicase family with a romantic, decorative character. Alternating uppercase and lowercase glyphs alongside alternates, ligatures, swashes and ending forms aim to provide broad compositional scope in display settings.

name: Rosales
classification_notes: Humanist sans with geometric influences and a strong calligraphic underpinning. Two stylistic sets let users toggle between a more humanist and a more geometric interpretation of the same design. Stroke rhythm leans calligraphic in the lighter weights; the heavier cuts are suited to display.
summary: A calligraphically rooted humanist sans from Fernando Perez, offering eight weights with matching italics and two stylistic sets that shift the family between humanist and geometric registers.
description: Rosales was designed by Fernando Perez and released by Latinotype in 2022. The 16-style family runs from Thin to ExtraBold with matching italics throughout, and ships with small caps, oldstyle figures and two stylistic sets – one pulling the letterforms toward humanist warmth, the other toward geometric precision. The lighter weights carry calligraphic trace in the stroke rhythm; the heavier cuts are built for display and logo work, while the middle range holds up in body text.
foundry_blurb: Rosales integrates humanist style with geometry in a typeface deeply inspired by calligraphic tradition. The extreme weights are designed for titles and display use, while the intermediate weights are tuned for body copy, giving the family wide typographic range. Stylistic sets offer humanist and geometric variants, complemented by initial capitals, small caps, and both oldstyle and lining figures.

name: Sana Sans
classification_notes: Functional humanist sans-serif built for legibility across text and display sizes. Eight weights from Thin to Heavy, each with a matching italic, plus small caps throughout. An Alt subfamily swaps in alternate letterforms for a, e, l, q, y, G, L and Q, giving designers a second flavour without a separate licence. No condensed variants.
summary: A clean, functional humanist sans-serif from Latinotype with 32 styles across eight weights and a companion Alt subfamily offering alternate letterforms for a handful of characters.
description: Sana Sans is a humanist sans-serif designed by Felipe Sanzana in 2016, covering eight weights from Thin to Heavy with matching italics and small caps. It holds up well in continuous text while reading neatly at headline sizes, making it a reliable choice for publishing work across print and screen. The Alt subfamily gives designers access to alternate letterforms for select characters without leaving the family.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Sana Sans as a humanist functional typeface with a modern feel, suited to multiple purposes and particularly well matched to publishing. They note it delivers legible, clean text in extended passages and remains neat and simple at display sizes, performing equally well in digital and print contexts.

name: Sanchez
classification_notes: Mechanical Egyptian slab in the Rockwell tradition, distinguished by rounded joins and terminals that soften the otherwise rigidly square bracket structure. The contrast between square serifs and rounded stroke endings gives it a warmer register than pure geometric slabs.
summary: A geometric Egyptian slab that echoes Rockwell's square structure while softening it with rounded joins and terminals for a warmer, more approachable character.
description: Designed by Daniel Hernández and released through Latinotype in 2011, Sanchez spans six weights from ExtraLight to Black, each paired with a matching italic. The square bracket serifs follow a mechanical, Rockwell-adjacent rhythm, but rounded stroke endings and joins pull it away from the coldness of a strict geometric slab – making it better suited to editorial headlines, brand wordmarks and packaging than to pure workhorse display settings. Regular and Italic weights are freely available via Google Fonts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Sanchez as a slab serif that draws on the Rockwell tradition but introduces rounded edges to create contrast and balance against the square skeleton of the letterforms, achieving a more even, considered structure across the family.

name: Sanchez Condensed
classification_notes: Egyptian/slab serif with uniform slab serifs and rounded terminals set at a condensed width. Structurally close to Rockwell but softened by rounded edges throughout; the condensed proportions push it firmly into display and headline territory.
summary: A compressed Egyptian slab from Chilean foundry Latinotype, taking Rockwell's sturdy structure and softening it with rounded edges across six weights.
description: Daniel Hernández released Sanchez Condensed in 2012 as a narrow companion to his Sánchez family, applying the same rounded-terminal treatment to a compressed skeleton suited to headlines and editorial settings. Six weights run from ExtraLight to Black, each paired with an italic, giving it enough range to carry a full typographic system. The softened edges separate it from harder Egyptian models, lending a subtle warmth to what is still a structured, high-contrast slab.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype places Sanchez Condensed in the Egyptian slab tradition, drawing an explicit connection to Rockwell while pointing to the rounded edges as the design element that introduces contrast and balance to its square, geometric base structure.

name: Sanchez Niu
classification_notes: Slab serif with moderate stroke contrast; proportions redrawn from the 2011 Sánchez original for text-setting at screen sizes. Includes small caps, oldstyle figures, tabular figures and stylistic alternates. Six weights from ExtraLight to Black, each with a companion italic.
summary: Latinotype's 2017 revision of their Sánchez slab, redrawn for extended reading with twelve weights, small caps and oldstyle figures across 219 languages.
description: Sanchez Niu is a thorough revision of the original Sánchez released by Latinotype in 2011, with proportions redrawn for extended text and screen use. The family spans six weights from ExtraLight to Black, each paired with an italic, and includes small caps, oldstyle figures, tabular numbers and stylistic alternates. At 720 characters covering 219 languages, it handles multilingual editorial and digital work without strain.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Sanchez Niu as a redesign of the original Sánchez, built to work well with longer text and optimised for web usage. Two styles – Regular and Regular Italic – are available free.

name: Sanchez Slab
classification_notes: Egyptian-style slab serif with geometric construction openly referencing Rockwell. Square structure, straight terminals and low stroke contrast across a six-weight range with full italic companions. All styles share a consistent x-height.
summary: A twelve-style Egyptian slab by Daniel Hernández, built on a square geometric structure with straight edges and a deliberate nod to Rockwell.
description: Sanchez Slab was designed by Daniel Hernández and released through Latinotype in 2013. It sits in the Egyptian slab tradition, drawing openly from Rockwell's geometry while adding more contrast through straight-edged terminals and a consistent x-height across all six weights. The family runs from ExtraLight to Black with matching italics, making it a serviceable pick for editorial headlines and display work.
foundry_blurb: Sanchez Slab is a slab serif in the Egyptian classification with a square construction and straight edges that lend the letterforms character and visual weight. Designed by Daniel Hernández, the family spans twelve styles from ExtraLight to Black, each sharing a consistent x-height. Regular and Italic are available free; the complete family is available for purchase.

name: Santi
classification_notes: Classical grotesque proportions with restrained contemporary detailing. Nine weights with matching italics give it a broad range. No condensed, extended or mono variants. Sits comfortably in the functional workhorse grotesque category rather than the expressive or geometric camps.
summary: A nine-weight grotesque from Latinotype that holds up reliably across headline and body copy without calling attention to itself.
description: Santi is a grotesque sans-serif with nine weights and matching italics — 18 styles in total. Designed by Daniel Hernández and released in 2023, it pairs conventional grotesque structure with understated modern detailing. The result is a dependable workhorse that serves editorial, branding and interface work without drama.
foundry_blurb: Santi blends classical grotesque character with subtle modern touches across nine weights from Thin to Black, each with a matching italic. The family scales from impactful display settings down to comfortable body copy, aiming for a timeless quality that doesn't chase trends.

name: Santis
classification_notes: High-contrast Didone with sharp hairline-to-stem ratio, decorative swash alternates, ornamental glyphs and ligatures; four-style family positioned for display use in fashion and editorial contexts, following the Didot lineage.
summary: A Didone display serif with swash alternates, ligatures and ornamental glyphs, built for fashion editorial and logo work.
description: Santis draws from the Didot tradition, pairing sharp stroke contrast with a 1,017-glyph set that includes swash letters, ligatures and ornamental characters.
