Designed by Enrique Hernández and published in 2013, the four-style family targets display use in fashion publishing, brand identity and magazine layouts. The swash alternates are restrained enough to stay legible in short-form headline settings.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Santis as a multiface typeface for logos, brands, magazines and editorial design, with a particular lean toward fashion. The swash-rich glyph set is designed to display words and phrases harmoniously while preserving legibility, and the family is optimised for OpenType performance.

name: Save the Date
classification_notes: A wedding-focused type system built around a formal calligraphic script, paired with matching sans and serif companions in three weights each, plus a Small decorative variant. The script is the headline style; the sans and serif provide supporting text options within the same stationery system.
summary: A nine-style wedding family from Latinotype pairing a formal calligraphic script with matching sans and serif companions, designed expressly for invitation and stationery work.
description: Save the Date is built around a formal script, supplemented by Light, Regular and Bold weights across dedicated sans and serif companions, plus a Small decorative variant — nine styles in total. The system gives invitation designers enough range to build cohesive stationery without mixing foundries. Its usefulness is narrow: this is occasion typography, suited to wedding collateral and little beyond it.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Save the Date as a font collection conceived for the wedding invitation — a set of tools for couples who want to express something personal on their wedding day through the right typography.

name: Schwager
classification_notes: Slab serif with uniform, heavy stroke weight and squared serifs drawing from industrial and steampunk visual language. The structure is assertive and masculine, built for display and headline use rather than extended text. Alternate glyphs extend typographic options within the same voice.
summary: A steampunk-inflected industrial slab from Latinotype, built across six weights for headlines and branding where a hard, masculine edge is the point.
description: Schwager is a six-weight slab serif designed by Luciano Vergara for Latinotype in 2012. Its heavy squared serifs and assertive stroke structure give it a distinctly industrial character, well-suited to display settings in technology, lifestyle and trend contexts. Each weight ships with a matching italic, and alternate glyphs provide additional flexibility for headline work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Schwager as a slab serif with an industrial accent and a steampunk tone in a contemporary register. Designed for titles and headlines, it suits male-oriented lifestyle, technology and trend categories, with alternate glyphs available for added emphasis.

name: Schwager Sans
classification_notes: Geometric modernist sans-serif with clean construction and no humanist softening. Shares structural DNA with its serif sibling Schwager. Associations lean toward sports and technology rather than editorial warmth.
summary: A geometric modernist sans-serif from Latinotype with six weights and matching italics, pitched at headlines, logos and digital work with a sports-tech character.
description: Schwager Sans is the sans companion to Luciano Vergara's Schwager, preserving its geometric structure and modernist sensibility in a lighter, more contemporary form. Six weights from Thin to Black, each paired with an italic, give it enough range for display and branding work. The design carries associations with sports and technology, making it a serviceable pick for those contexts but not especially distinctive outside them.
foundry_blurb: The sans-serif companion to Schwager, keeping the same geometric structure and modernist principles while taking on a fresher character. Designed for titles, cover design, logos and web applications.

name: Selaive
classification_notes: Geometric display typeface with pronounced thick-thin contrast and ornamental flourishes. Named after its designer. Fashion and luxury retail orientation. Two-weight family (Light and Bold) with no italics or condensed variants.
summary: A geometric display face from Chilean designer Paula Nazal Selaive, built on thick-thin contrast and ornamental flourishes for fashion editorial and luxury branding.
description: Selaive pairs high-contrast strokes with decorative flourishes to produce a glamorous, directional character that sits firmly in fashion territory. The family is compact at just two weights — Light and Bold — which limits its range but keeps its identity focused. Best deployed in logo marks, fashion editorial and retail contexts where the geometry and ornamentation can justify themselves.
foundry_blurb: A geometric typeface with an air of rebelliousness, Selaive plays on contrasting weights and decorative flourishes to create a personal, glamorous aesthetic — suited to fashion publications, logo design and retail branding.

name: Seriguela
classification_notes: Ultra-condensed grotesque sans-serif with unconventional thick-thin contrast deliberately placed against historical convention. Hooked terminals on select curves and a strong vertical rhythm distinguish it from neutral condensed grotesques. Offered in separate text and display cuts, the latter pushing contrast further for headline impact.
summary: A 54-style ultra-condensed grotesque by Sofia Mohr, with hooked terminals, reverse italics and deliberately misplaced contrast across text and display cuts.
description: Seriguela is an ultra-condensed sans-serif by Sofia Mohr, built on a grotesque structure with thick-thin contrast applied in positions that break from historical precedent, growing more pronounced at heavier weights. The family spans 54 styles across text and display versions, each with nine weights from Thin to Poster in upright, italic and reverse italic. Hooked terminals and a strong vertical rhythm give it personality beyond the crowded field of condensed grotesques.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Seriguela as an ultra-condensed sans-serif with a unique personality, built for display use where visual impact matters. The grotesque base gains originality through deliberately unconventional contrast – applied, in their words, "in the wrong places" – and the design becomes more striking as weight increases. The display cut amplifies these qualities through exaggerated thick-thin relationships.

name: Shamgod
classification_notes: Ultra-condensed grotesque sans-serif with sharp diagonal cuts across 9 weights and matching italics (18 styles total). Display-oriented with strong sports and streetwear aesthetic referencing '90s and 2000s urban visual culture.
summary: Shamgod is an ultra-condensed grotesque from Latinotype with nine weights and matching italics, built for high-impact headlines in sports, streetwear and editorial contexts.
description: Designed by Alexis Navarro and released in 2025, Shamgod draws on the visual language of '90s and 2000s sports and urban culture. Sharp diagonal cuts and an extreme condensed form give it strong personality at display sizes. Eighteen styles across nine weights and their italics make it adaptable within its niche.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Shamgod as compact, powerful and full of attitude, designed to exude speed and energy. It references the raw intensity of sports culture and the streetwear aesthetics of the '90s and 2000s, positioning it for headlines, logos, posters and brand work where impact is the priority.

name: Showcase
classification_notes: A five-subfamily display system sharing a pen-drawn, handcrafted character across script, sans, mini sans, slab and ornament styles. Positioned firmly in the decorative/branding end of the display market.
summary: A pen-drawn display family by Paula Nazal Selaive and Daniel Hernández pairing script, sans, slab and ornament styles as one coordinated handmade system.
description: Released in 2014, Showcase unifies five subfamilies – Script, Sans, Sans Mini, Slab and Ornaments – through a shared handcrafted character, making the components feel designed together rather than cobbled from separate sources. The suite is built for decorative display work: café and restaurant branding, editorial headers and signage, where the script carries the expressive lead and the slab or sans handles supporting copy. The ornaments round out a self-contained toolkit for branding projects that want a consistent hand-drawn voice.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by a pen casually writing different typefaces and ornaments, Showcase brings together script, sans, mini sans, slab and ornamental styles into a harmonious handmade family. Latinotype position it as versatile enough for magazines, restaurants, windows and cafés.

name: Singolare
classification_notes: Geometric display sans-serif with angular terminals and a generous x-height. No italics. Three sub-families: standard weights (Ultra Light to Black), matching stencil cuts, and four decorative layer fonts designed to be overlaid for chromatic display compositions. Weights are engineered to become progressively more visually distinct at heavier settings.
summary: A geometric display sans by Sofia Mohr with angular terminals and five weights, extended into stencil and layered sub-families for multi-colour typographic compositions.
description: Singolare (2021) runs from Ultra Light to Black across five weights, becoming progressively more visually distinct at heavier settings. The family branches into a full stencil sub-family with expressive cuts and four layer fonts designed to be overlaid on the black weight, with each layer coloured independently for chromatic display effects. At 15 styles across three sub-families, it is built for display and short-text work where visual impact is the primary requirement.
foundry_blurb: A contemporary geometric sans-serif with angular terminals and a generous x-height. Five weights from Ultra Light to Black are each mirrored in an expressive stencil cut; four decorative layer fonts can work on their own or be stacked over the black weight, with each layer's colour changed independently, extending the family's application possibilities. Intended for display use and short texts requiring visual impact.

name: Snatch
designer: Valentina Vega, Rodrigo Fuenzalida, César Araya (supervised by Dany Berczeller, Daniel Hernández, Luciano Vergara)
classification_notes: Sharp-edged condensed all-caps type system with five weights of uppercase letterforms (small caps and all caps), script catchwords, and two sets each of dingbats and flags. Described by the foundry as the "wild, condensed sister" of their BOWIE family. No lowercase; the design is inherently headline and packaging-facing.
summary: A sharp condensed all-caps display system with five weights and a full set of script catchwords, dingbats and flags – built for branding and packaging work that wants attitude.
description: Released in 2016 by Latinotype's in-house team, Snatch is a condensed all-caps typeface conceived as the rougher counterpart to their BOWIE family. Five weights of sharp uppercase letterforms are accompanied by script catchwords, two sets of dingbats and two sets of flags, giving the system genuine utility for packaging and editorial headlines. Despite its very specific rough-meets-bold aesthetic, the family covers 206 languages across 679 characters – more complete than its personality suggests.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Snatch as a dynamic type system built for creative applications, combining rough and bold aesthetics across publishing, branding and packaging projects.

name: Spirits
classification_notes: Condensed old-style serif derived from Hermann Ihlenburg's Schoeffer Old Style (ATF, 1912). Three stylistic subfamilies – Soft, Neutral and Sharp – each interpret the same historical source at a different level of fidelity and formality. Large x-height throughout; optimised for headline and display settings.
summary: A condensed old-style serif drawn from Ihlenburg's 1912 Schoeffer Old Style, available in three stylistic variants – Soft, Neutral and Sharp – each calibrated for a different editorial register.
description: Designed by Alfonso García in 2020, Spirits offers 12 styles across three subfamilies that each interpret the same historical source differently. Soft stays close to the original printed form; Neutral brings cleaner, more formal serifs suited to newspaper headlines; Sharp takes a contemporary approach suited to branding. All three share condensed proportions, a large x-height and support for over 200 languages.
foundry_blurb: Drawing on Hermann Ihlenburg's Schoeffer Old Style from the 1912 ATF catalogue, Spirits presents three distinct readings of the same design. Soft preserves the warmth of the original; Neutral offers formal serifs for editorial use; Sharp gives the face a contemporary edge for current design applications.

name: Spock
designer: Luciano Vergara, Rodrigo Fuenzalida, César Araya
classification_notes: Neutral, clean-structured sans-serif superfamily in the neo-grotesque tradition; restrained curves and upright strokes keep it workhorse-functional, while extensive OpenType alternates – including a pointed-ear glyph set – add controlled personality without breaking the overall register.
summary: A neutral, clean-structured sans-serif superfamily across 48 styles and four glyph-set variants, suited to advertising, editorial and corporate work.
description: Designed by Luciano Vergara, Rodrigo Fuenzalida and César Araya and released in 2020, Spock is organised into four sub-families – Pro, Essential, Essential Alt 1 and Essential Alt 2 – each offering six weights with matching italics. The Pro family runs to 609 characters and includes a generous range of OpenType alternates, among them glyphs with pointed ears as a quiet typographic in-joke. The system gives designers a reliable neutral workhorse with enough built-in variation to sustain different project tones without switching families.
foundry_blurb: Spock has a neutral, clean structure that opens up into a rich variety of alternates through its OpenType features – pointed-ear glyphs among them. The superfamily spans four sub-families (Spock Pro, Spock Essential, Spock Essential Alt 1 and Spock Essential Alt 2), each with six weights and matching italics for a total of 48 styles; the Pro sub-family alone covers 609 characters. Latinotype positions it as well suited to advertising, editorial and corporate design.

name: Stgotic
classification_notes: Single-weight pixel blackletter engineered for display at 8pt and multiples on low-resolution screens. Letterforms are adapted to a pixel grid rather than drawn from a calligraphic or historical revival tradition. Extremely narrow use case; functionally a display curiosity rather than a workhorse gothic.
summary: Daniel Hernández's debut typeface: a single-weight pixel blackletter built to render cleanly at 8pt and its multiples on low-resolution screens.
description: Designed in 2006 and published through Latinotype in 2012, Stgotic treats blackletter letterforms as a constraint-driven exercise in pixel-grid legibility rather than a calligraphic or historical revival. It won best screen font at the Bienal de Letras Latinas that year. A single Regular weight with no variants, it is a narrow historical artefact with little contemporary utility beyond nostalgic or lo-fi display contexts.
foundry_blurb: Stgotic was Daniel Hernández's first digital font, designed in 2006. A blackletter built specifically for low-resolution screen devices, it was optimised to display at 8 points and multiples of 8. TipoGráfica recognised it as the best screen font at the Bienal de Letras Latinas in 2006.

name: Styling
classification_notes: Geometric-leaning sans-serif with streamlined, aerodynamic letterforms inspired by vintage automotive and aviation design. Clean construction with a slight Art Deco sensibility. Comes as two complementary families – Styling and StylingAlt – the latter providing alternate character forms. Five weights each with a matching italic across both families.
summary: A clean geometric sans-serif drawn from the aerodynamic forms of vintage cars and aircraft, available in five weights with italics across two complementary families.
description: Styling is a geometric sans-serif by Mendoza Vergara, published through Latinotype in 2015 and conceived at 30,000 feet over Latin American cities. The letterforms take their cue from the streamlined shapes of old cars and planes, giving the face a confident, forward-leaning quality. A companion family, StylingAlt, provides alternate character forms across the same five-weight range.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Styling as a simple, light sans-serif inspired by the aerodynamic shapes of old cars and planes, conveying a sense of energy and speed through its streamlined forms.

name: Suiza
classification_notes: Swiss-tradition neo-grotesque referencing Helvetica and 1960s international typography. Clean terminals, sharp cuts and geometric structure are balanced with what Latinotype describes as Latin expressiveness. Rational in construction, with contemporary flexibility.
summary: A 2025 Swiss-tradition neo-grotesque from Latinotype, bringing geometric precision and clean terminals across nine weights with matching italics.
description: Suiza draws on the Swiss typographic tradition of the 1960s, referencing Helvetica and the legibility of New York subway signage. Latinotype pitches it as a meeting point between rational international typography and Latin warmth, with sharp cuts and balanced structure across 18 styles. Solid range for editorial, identity and UI work, though the Swiss-influenced sans category is well crowded.
foundry_blurb: Suiza is a contemporary sans-serif rooted in the Swiss typographic tradition of the 1960s, blending classic precision with a fresh, dynamic sensibility. It harmonises the geometric clarity of international typography with the warmth and expressiveness of Latin design, featuring a balanced structure, clean terminals and sharp, precise cuts.

name: Taberna
classification_notes: Three-subfamily display system (Sans, Serif, Script) with layering variants (inline, shadow) rather than traditional weight/width axes. Heavy capitals throughout. Monolinear script complements the upright subfamilies. Designed for stacking layers to create depth effects.
summary: A 22-style layered display system from 2016 drawing on bar signage and liquor packaging, with sans, serif and script subfamilies built to stack for depth effects in headlines and logotypes.
description: Designed by Jorge Cisterna and Rodrigo Fuenzalida, Taberna organises itself into three subfamilies – Sans, Serif and Script – each with inline and shadow layering variants. The Serif carries a heavier, more sombre character; the Sans reads clean and direct; the monolinear Script bridges them. Twenty-two styles make it a well-considered system for themed display work, though its bar and streetwear aesthetic keeps it firmly in single-context territory.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Taberna as a type system born from exploring design trends in bar signage, liquor packaging and street wear. They position the Sans for clean, simple design and the Serif for a more distinctive, sombre personality, with the monolinear Script rounding out the system. The family is intended as a versatile choice for headlines, posters and logotypes.

name: Texta
classification_notes: Rational humanist sans drawing on Johnston and Frutiger; the Alt subfamily swaps a, g and y for geometric constructions, pushing it slightly toward neo-grotesque territory in that variant. Eight weights from Thin to Heavy with matching italics across both subfamilies.
summary: A rational humanist sans designed by Daniel Hernández, available in 32 styles across two subfamilies – a standard cut and a geometric-alternate variant – with coverage across 200+ languages.
description: Texta was drawn by Daniel Hernández and released in 2014, rooted in the humanist lettering of Edward Johnston and Adrian Frutiger with an additional influence from Gothic sign-painting traditions. The family spans eight weights from Thin to Heavy, each with a matching italic, and comes in two subfamilies: the standard Texta and Texta Alt, which replaces the a, g and y with geometric constructions for more neutral compositions. Broad multilingual coverage across 200+ languages makes it a practical choice for editorial and corporate publishing work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype bills Texta as a contemporary, rational and transparent sans made for composing all kinds of text, with its design stemming from study of humanist models spanning Johnston through to Frutiger, alongside the Gothic lettering of sign painters.

name: Texta Pro
classification_notes: Humanist sans-serif sitting between rational geometry and typographic warmth, conceived in 2014 and substantially expanded in 2022. Draws on Edward Johnston and Adrian Frutiger as reference points. Comes in two subfamilies – Texta Pro and Texta Pro Alt – the latter offering alternate glyph forms via stylistic sets. Comprehensive OpenType feature set including small caps for Latin and Cyrillic, multiple numeral styles, and extended monetary symbols.
summary: A capable humanist sans-serif from Latinotype with thorough OpenType support, Latin and Cyrillic coverage, and 32 styles across two subfamilies – built to disappear into text without being bland.
description: Texta Pro is a rational humanist sans-serif by Daniel Hernández, first conceived in 2014 and significantly expanded in 2022 to 983 glyphs across 32 styles. The design draws on Johnston and Frutiger as touchstones, landing somewhere between warm and neutral. Its alternate subfamily, Texta Pro Alt, provides variant glyph forms, while the OpenType feature set covers small caps, multiple numeral styles and extended monetary symbols.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Texta Pro as a contemporary, rational sans that is "almost invisible, but not quite" – a workhorse built for any type of project. The 2022 update adds nearly 500 glyphs over its predecessor, bringing Cyrillic script support, full small-cap coverage across Latin and Cyrillic, extended monetary signs and two stylistic sets for alternate letterforms.

name: Tita Script
classification_notes: Calligraphic display script rooted in fileteado porteño, the ornate Buenos Aires street lettering tradition. Hand lettering by Sandra Biondi, digitised by Daniel Hernández. Four variants (Pro, Essential, Alt, Icons) rather than traditional weight progression. Strong singular personality suited to theatrical or culturally specific display use.
summary: A theatrical calligraphic script drawn from Argentine fileteado porteño and milonga music, built on Sandra Biondi's hand lettering and released in four decorative variants.
description: Tita Script draws on fileteado porteño – the florid, curlicued lettering tradition of Buenos Aires – and the polyrhythmic curves of milonga calligraphy. Sandra Biondi provided the original hand lettering; Daniel Hernández digitised it into four variants: Pro, Essential, Alt, and an Icons set. It is a narrow-use display face with a strong and specific cultural character.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype presents Tita as a personal dedication to Hernández's grandmother, inspired by milonga music and the fileteado porteño tradition. Their copy envisions it at the Moulin Rouge – sparkling, provocative, loving – grounded in Argentine hand lettering and Biondi's calligraphy.

name: Titular
classification_notes: A condensed grotesque-influenced sans-serif with wood type revival DNA. The narrow proportions and even colour make it well suited to headline and display settings. Two subfamilies – regular and Alt – extend its typographic range across 28 styles.
summary: A condensed sans-serif built for headlines and display work, drawing on historical wood type energy with a contemporary Latin American character across 28 styles.
description: Titular covers seven weights – Thin through Heavy – each with roman and italic, plus a parallel Alt subfamily offering alternate letterforms. Designed by Bruno Jara with the Latinotype team, it suits newspaper mastheads, magazine headlines, poster lettering and brand logotypes with equal ease. Its tight proportions and consistent colour work particularly well at large sizes.
foundry_blurb: Titular revives the spirit of old wood types while adding a contemporary flavour and Latin American character. Designed for headings, subheadings, newspapers, magazines, logotypes, brands and posters, it delivers 28 styles across two subfamilies.

name: Touch Me
classification_notes: Hand-drawn brush script drawing on altered calligraphic contrast and watercolour brush technique. OpenType programming randomises stroke contrast and baseline position to simulate handmade variation. Paired with a neutral grotesque companion (TouchMe Sans) in six weights plus Petite optical variants, and supplemented by ornaments, catchwords and dingbats.
summary: A brush-calligraphic script with OpenType stroke randomisation, paired with a six-weight grotesque and a full set of ornaments and extras across 19 styles.
description: Touch Me pairs a hand-lettered script with a neutral grotesque companion, the two sharing a coherent design language. The script side uses OpenType programming to vary stroke contrast and baseline position, giving running text a convincingly spontaneous, handmade quality. Extras, catchwords and ornaments are included, making the family self-sufficient for most display applications.
foundry_blurb: Touch Me is a hand-drawn script born from polyrhythmic exploration, sign deconstruction and altered calligraphic contrast with a watercolour brush. Designed by Coto Mendoza, with Sans extensions by Luciano Vergara, the family spans 19 styles across two subfamilies and more than 3,000 glyphs, suited to short text in both print and digital contexts.

name: Trend
classification_notes: A self-contained layered display system with two subfamilies — Trend Sans and Trend Slab — each offering five numbered layers (One through Five) with italics, designed to stack over one another for decorative headlines. Layer numbering replaces conventional weight naming. An Ornaments companion set is included.
summary: A 2013 layered display system pairing numbered sans and slab subfamilies designed to stack for decorative headline use, with no external elements required.
description: Designed by Paula Nazal Selaive and Daniel Hernández, Trend pairs Trend Sans and Trend Slab across five numbered layers, each built to sit over the next as a self-contained decorative system. An Ornaments set rounds out the 21-style family. The aesthetic is firmly mid-2010s fashion-editorial, which limits its currency outside nostalgia-aware work.
foundry_blurb: Trend is a layered typeface built on a sans and slab base, developed from research into global design and fashion trends. The family is designed to function as a complete system — every component required for the layered effect is contained within it, with nothing external needed to achieve the full result.

name: Trend Hand Made
classification_notes: A stacking layer system rather than a conventional weight progression. Five numbered layers in both sans and slab variants allow typographic depth through overlay. The ornament subfamily completes the self-contained kit. Fashion and editorial in orientation.
summary: A 21-style layered display system pairing numbered sans and slab variants with an ornament set, built for fashion and editorial work as a self-contained composition kit.
description: Trend Hand Made is a layered typeface system offering five numbered stacking layers in both sans and slab variants, each with an italic, plus a complementary ornament set – 21 styles across three subfamilies. The numbered layers are designed to be overlaid rather than used as a weight progression, creating typographic depth without external embellishment. Paula Nazal Selaive and Daniel Hernández designed it in 2013 with fashion-forward display work in mind.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Trend Hand Made as a font built from layers, combining a sans and a slab typeface to capture the aesthetics of fashion. They present it as a self-sufficient system that contains all the components a design needs, with nothing required from outside the family itself.

name: Trend Rough
classification_notes: A layered display system built on both sans-serif and slab-serif bases. The "Rough" variant applies a distressed texture to each of the five numbered layers. Layers are numbered One through Five rather than named by weight, indicating they are meant to be stacked in design applications. The family also includes ornamental and dingbat extras fonts. Not a text typeface; purely display and decorative.
summary: A 24-style layered display system by Paula Nazal Selaive and Daniel Hernández, offering distressed sans and slab variants in five stackable layers plus ornamental extras.
description: Trend Rough extends Latinotype's Trend family with a distressed texture applied across five numbered layers, available in both sans-serif and slab-serif versions with italics for each. The layering system is the central mechanic: designers stack cuts to build depth and shadow effects without external assets. At 24 styles including ornaments and dingbats, it is a complete kit for a specific genre of retro display work, though the aesthetic is firmly rooted in the design fashions of 2014.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Trend Rough as a font made of layers, built on a sans and slab foundation, and designed to capture contemporary aesthetic trends as a self-contained system requiring no external elements.

name: Trenda
designer: Daniel Hernández and Paula Nazal Selaive
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif that evolved from the uppercase alphabet of Latinotype's earlier Trend (2013). Strong uppercase presence with consistent geometry across a wide weight range. Small caps and alternates included. Targets display and short-text use, corporate identity and logotype work.
summary: A geometric sans-serif developed from the uppercase letters of Latinotype's Trend, with eight weights and matching italics suited to display, identity and publishing work across 206 languages.
description: Trenda is a geometric sans-serif by Daniel Hernández and Paula Nazal Selaive, released in 2017 as a development of the uppercase alphabet from their 2013 typeface Trend. Eight weights from Thin to Heavy, each with a matching italic, give it range from editorial display to short body text. A 634-character set covering 206 languages, alongside small caps and alternates, makes it a practical choice for multilingual publishing and corporate identity.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype position Trenda as a versatile, functional geometric sans with a strong personality. Lighter and heavier weights are intended for display use; middle weights handle short-to-medium text. The family includes small caps and alternates, and is aimed at corporate applications, logotypes and publishing projects.

name: Triump
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif with rounded terminals throughout. A structural idiosyncrasy sets it apart: on A, E, F, H, J and K, horizontal strokes extend past the vertical stems. Six weights from Thin to Black; the heaviest weight also ships in an Inline cut. Fourteen styles in total including italics across all weights.
summary: A rounded geometric sans from Latinotype with six weights and an Inline variant at the heavy end, distinguished by horizontal strokes that overshoot the vertical stems on A, E, F, H, J and K.
description: Triump was released in 2014, designed by Enrique Hernández as a clean rounded geometric sans spanning six weights from Thin through to Black. A deliberate structural quirk gives it character: on A, E, F, H, J and K, the horizontal strokes extend past the vertical stems. An Inline cut at the Black weight adds display versatility, lending itself to poster work and vintage-inflected logomark applications.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Triump as a simple sans-serif with six weights, from Thin for epigraph and small-scale use through to Black for high-impact headlines. Rounded corners give it a smooth, approachable quality throughout the range, and the Black Inline variant is positioned for vintage display work across logos, posters and editorial layouts.

name: Triump Rough
classification_notes: Rough-textured display family split into two subfamilies: Blur (soft, diffused edges with a vintage feel) and Rock (hard, high-contrast forms suited to heavy headlines). The distressing is baked into the letterforms rather than applied as an overlay, giving both variants a consistent weathered character. Supplementary Extras and Ornaments styles add catchwords and decorative glyphs for editorial and packaging use.
summary: A 26-style distressed display family split into two contrasting subfamilies – soft-edged Blur and hard-edged Rock – with ornaments and extras for vintage-inflected headline work.
description: Triump Rough is a Chilean display family by Enrique Hernández built around two textural extremes: Blur, with its hazy, diffused edges and nostalgic warmth, and Rock, a harder-edged variant designed for high-impact headlines. Both come in six weights with italics, giving the family genuine range for a rough-textured release. OpenType ligatures, alternates, catchwords and a dedicated Ornaments set extend its use into packaging and editorial contexts where decorative depth matters.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Blur as a soft, delicate font with a vintage and hipster feel that gives designs a breath of fresh air, while Rock is positioned as a strong, hard font suited to upper- and lower-case high-impact headlines. The family includes OpenType features – ligatures, alternates and catchwords – alongside a series of ornaments and extras.

name: Uffizi
classification_notes: Text serif that draws on classical structure and applies a contemporary hand. Even text colour at small sizes; enough contrast to carry presence at display scale. Nine weights with matching italics across 18 styles. Full OpenType feature set including small caps, ligatures and old-style figures marks it as a properly equipped book or editorial face.
summary: A contemporary text serif from Latinotype spanning nine weights with italics, built for comfortable long reading with a full OpenType feature set including small caps and old-style figures.
description: Uffizi pairs classical structure with a fresh drawing approach, holding even colour across continuous text while retaining presence at display sizes. The 18-style family runs Thin through Black with italic companions at every weight, and the OpenType palette covers small caps, ligatures and proportional old-style numerals. It sits comfortably in books, magazine layouts and screen-based editorial.
foundry_blurb: Designed by Rodrigo López Fuentes with the Latinotype team, Uffizi is conceived as a reading typeface that fuses classical elegance with a contemporary sensibility. The design prioritises uniform text colour and comfortable reading rhythm, while enough contrast in the stroke pattern gives it a distinctive presence when set large.

name: Utily Sans
classification_notes: Geometric sans constructed on Futura-like principles but with humanist warmth introduced through softer stroke terminals and calligraphic rhythm. Designed to sit between pure geometry and text-friendly legibility, making it functional at both display and body sizes.
summary: A geometric sans that softens Futura's rigour with humanist warmth, resulting in a family that holds its own in both display and extended text settings.
description: Utily Sans covers six weights with matching italics, small caps, alternates with geometric origins, uppercase discretionary ligatures, and old-style figures. It supports over 200 Latin-based languages and Cyrillic – a first for Latinotype at the time of its 2019 release. The feature set gives it enough range for editorial and brand work without leaning into novelty.
foundry_blurb: Utily Sans grew from the question of what typeface design might look like had Paul Renner favoured humanism over geometry. Designed by Alfonso García, Rodrigo Fuenzalida and the Latinotype team, it pairs clean geometric structure with a warmth that brings it closer to Garamond in feel. The twelve-style family includes Cyrillic support and a full OpenType feature set with small caps, alternates, lining figures and old-style numbers.
designer: Alfonso García, Rodrigo Fuenzalida, Latinotype Team

name: Vanguardia
classification_notes: Monolinear construction with low contrast throughout, distinguishing it from conventional high-contrast serifs. Exaggerated terminals on a, e, c, C, S, G, E and similar letterforms, paired with diagonal cuts that give the family a contemporary editorial character. Sits comfortably in display and branding use rather than body text.
summary: A low-contrast monolinear serif with exaggerated terminals and diagonal cuts across 16 styles, built for branding, packaging and display work.
description: Vanguardia runs from Thin to Black with matching italics, its monolinear construction keeping stroke weight even where a conventional serif would thin. Exaggerated terminals on letterforms like a, e, c and S give it a contemporary edge well suited to logos, labels and screen titles. Coverage reaches 200+ Latin languages plus a basic Cyrillic set, making it deployable across a broad range of markets.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype position Vanguardia as an expressive modern family, noting that its low contrast and prominent terminals set it apart from traditional serif conventions. Suggested applications include logos, beverage and liquor packaging, labels, and film and television titles.

name: Versina
classification_notes: Display serif with 18th-century Spanish transitional roots. Asymmetric bracketed serifs, organic flowing strokes and calligraphic terminals throughout. Large x-height with shorter ascenders than cap height gives a contemporary proportion. Includes a dedicated ornaments subfamily in Regular and Black.
summary: A calligraphic display serif drawn from 18th-century Spanish transitional models, with asymmetric bracketed serifs, flowing organic strokes and five weights plus a decorative ornaments subfamily.
description: Versina takes Spanish transitional type from the 1700s as its starting point, filtering that historical structure through calligraphic energy – asymmetric bracketed serifs and flowing terminals give it warmth without veering into ornate excess. A large x-height with shortened ascenders modernises the proportions, keeping it functional at display sizes and usable in short text settings. The ornaments subfamily, available in Regular and Black, extends its range for editorial and packaging work.
foundry_blurb: Versina is a display typeface with an expressive yet moderate personality, drawn from the organic elegance of Spanish transitional letterforms of the 18th century. Flowing organic strokes, asymmetric bracketed serifs and calligraphic terminals bring rhythm and movement to the design. A large x-height with shorter ascenders gives it a contemporary quality suited to both headlines and shorter passages of text.

name: Versus
classification_notes: Unicase condensed-to-expanded sans-serif display face. Orthogonal terminals, reduced ascenders and descenders, stylistic alternates and a full ligature set. Nine weights from ExtraLight to Ultra. Designed around Latin American wrestling and boxing poster lettering conventions.
summary: A unicase display sans by Marcelo Moya drawn from Latin American wrestling and boxing poster lettering, spanning nine weights across a condensed-to-expanded range.
description: Versus is a unicase sans-serif display typeface rooted in the bold, compressed lettering of Latin American wrestling and boxing posters. Orthogonal terminals and reduced ascenders and descenders keep it tight in block compositions, while nine weights from ExtraLight to Ultra give it some stretch within that narrow register. Stylistic alternates and a full ligature set add flexibility, though the concept is specific enough to limit where it lands convincingly.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Versus as a type system built around the visual language of Latin American wrestling culture, intended for short text, titles, logos and poster layouts. The range from condensed lightweight to expanded heavy weights is presented as giving designers broad options for building distinct identities.

name: Via Sans
classification_notes: DIN 1451 and Steile Futura references give Via Sans a functional, utilitarian character, but the neo-humanist construction prevents it from reading as coldly geometric. Round corners reduce glare on reflective signage materials. The companion Pict weight is a full pictogram set designed for maps and wayfinding systems.
summary: A DIN and Futura-influenced neo-humanist sans built for distance legibility, with rounded corners for reflective surfaces and a companion pictogram set for wayfinding applications.
description: Via Sans takes its structural cues from DIN 1451 and Steile Futura, producing a clean, space-efficient sans aimed at signage and transport contexts. Ample counters keep letterforms open at small sizes or from a distance, while rounded corners reduce glare on reflective materials. Four weights with italics cover most functional needs, and the Pict subfamily adds a ready-made set of wayfinding pictograms for maps and signage systems.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Via Sans as built for fast reading at distance, with space-efficient composition suited to long phrases in reduced spaces. The round corner treatment addresses glare on reflective surfaces, and the Pict weight extends the family into a complete pictogram set for wayfinding and map design.

name: Weekly
classification_notes: Slab serif built on humanist proportions drawn from 1990s typefaces. Selective serif application: characters like 'a' and 'g' carry no serifs at all, while 'c' and 's' have abbreviated serifs, giving the family a strong sans-like quality. Described by the foundry as an Egyptienne without the retro character.
summary: A humanist slab serif that strips away the genre's retro associations, using selective serif application to produce something that reads almost as a sans.
description: Weekly is built on the premise that a slab serif can function as a sans-serif – characters like 'a' and 'g' carry no serifs at all, while 'c' and 's' have short, abbreviated ones. Three subfamilies (Pro, Basic and Alt) each span 10 weights with italics, giving 60 styles in total. The small x-height to cap-height differential and humanist proportions suit both book and magazine body text and heavier display work.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Weekly as "a slab serif that wants to be a sans" – a fresh design free of the retro character typical of the genre, built instead on humanist proportions drawn from 1990s typefaces, and equally at home in books, magazines and poster headlines.

name: Willy Caslon
classification_notes: Contemporary revival of the William Caslon transitional roman tradition. Moderate modulation with a slightly slanted axis, intensified stroke contrast, and sharp distinctive terminals on the a, c and r. The italic is independently constructed with custom uppercase integration rather than derived from the roman by slanting.
summary: A 2026 Caslon revival from Latinotype with sharpened stroke contrast, distinctive terminals and a purpose-built italic across five weights.
description: Willy Caslon updates the William Caslon transitional roman for contemporary editorial use, keeping the moderate axis modulation and classic spirit while intensifying stroke contrast and sharpening the terminals on key letters. Five weights from Regular to Black, each with a genuinely independent italic that integrates its own uppercase rather than leaning on the roman. Suited to print publications, editorial identities and digital projects where readable personality counts.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype positions Willy Caslon as a meeting point between the historical legacy of transitional roman typefaces and a contemporary editorial vision – fresh in its stroke, classic in its spirit. The design adapts Caslon's proportions and rhythm for contexts where legibility, character and typographic presence all matter.

name: Winden
classification_notes: Geometric slab serif with distinctive trapezoid-shaped serifs, derived from Latinotype's own Isidora. The Alt subfamily substitutes rounded terminals throughout, shifting the family's tone from functional to more approachable. No true condensed variants; italics present across all seven weights in both subfamilies.
summary: A geometric slab from Latinotype with trapezoid serifs and a rounded alternate subfamily, spanning 28 styles and over 200 Latin-based languages.
description: Winden is a geometric slab serif designed by Enrique Hernández and released in 2020, derived from Latinotype's own Isidora. Trapezoid-shaped serifs give the standard subfamily a crisp, contemporary character suited to headlines, branding and editorial work. The Alt variant swaps those serifs for rounded terminals, producing a softer feel without requiring a separate family purchase.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Winden as a geometric slab inspired by the classic slab-serif tradition of the early 20th century, with trapezoid serifs lending a modern edge. The Alt variant introduces rounded terminals for a more playful, contemporary character. Together the two subfamilies cover 28 styles and a 615-character set supporting more than 200 Latin-based languages.

name: Wright
classification_notes: Geometric sans-serif rooted in the lettering found on modernist architectural drawings. Distinctive proportions: small x-height, tall ascenders and wide capitals. Four named subfamilies (Pro, Deco, Funk, Roman) extend its tonal range beyond a single-register geometric. A broad alternates and ligatures set adds typographic flexibility.
summary: A geometric sans-serif by Diego Maldonado drawn from modernist building plan lettering, with tall ascenders, wide capitals and four distinct subfamilies across 48 styles.
description: Wright is a geometric sans-serif released by Latinotype in 2020, rooted in the lettering found on modernist architectural drawings. Its small x-height, tall ascenders and wide capitals give it a clean, structured quality that reads well at display sizes and in short text. Four subfamilies – Pro, Deco, Funk and Roman – each available in six weights with italics, extend its range, supported by a broad alternates set and coverage of over 200 Latin-based languages across 800 characters.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Wright as an elegant geometric sans suited to titles and short paragraphs, with a stylish appearance drawn from its distinctive proportions – small x-height, tall ascenders and wide capitals. The family ships with a wide range of alternates and ligatures, and supports over 200 Latin-based languages.

name: Yankee
classification_notes: Geometric construction with rational proportions, consistent stroke contrast and clean terminals. Nine weights with matching italics give it broad range. The design references American vernacular aesthetics as a mood rather than a strict historical programme – the underlying structure is contemporary geometric sans.
summary: A geometric sans spanning nine weights with matching italics, pitched at the intersection of American vernacular character and clean contemporary structure.
description: Yankee is a 2025 geometric sans-serif from the Latinotype team, available in 18 styles across nine weights from Thin to Black, each paired with an italic. Balanced proportions and consistent construction keep it readable at text sizes, while the heavier cuts carry enough visual weight for display work. The American vernacular references in its brief are largely atmospheric – the typeface itself reads as a capable, well-ranged geometric sans rather than a period revival.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Yankee as a typeface that merges the spirit of American tradition with a contemporary sensibility, drawing on reference points as varied as New York street culture, stadium game nights and winter museum exhibitions. The design aims for geometric precision and clean proportions that allow it to move between institutional and informal contexts.

name: Zennat Pro
classification_notes: Semi-slab serif with a display character; four numbered weight grades (One through Four), each paired with an italic, giving eight styles in total. OpenType feature set includes rotating alternate characters to aid compositional fit. Designed for high-impact setting at large sizes.
summary: A semi-slab display face by Diego Aravena rooted in 1990s Chilean graphic culture, with four numbered weight grades, italics throughout, and an OpenType alternate set that rotates characters for better compositional fit.
description: Zennat Pro draws on the dense, heavy print and poster work that characterised Chilean graphic design in the 1990s. It runs in four numbered grades, each with an italic, suited to editorial headlines, motion graphics and brand identity work where presence at large sizes matters. An OpenType feature rotates alternate characters so individual glyphs can lock into a composition more naturally.
foundry_blurb: Inspired by the compact, high-impact aesthetic of 1990s Chilean graphic design, Zennat Pro is built for eye-catching work at display scale. OpenType features rotate alternate characters to best suit the design, making the family at home in magazine layouts, motion graphics, trademarks, logos and poster work.

name: Águila
classification_notes: Display face that grafts angular semi-serifs and triangular terminals onto a geometric skeleton with Didone-inflected stroke contrast — high-waisted modulation gives it classical tension while the geometry keeps it firmly contemporary.
summary: A semi-serif display typeface from Latinotype that combines triangular terminals and Didone stroke contrast with a clean geometric structure across nine weights.
description: Designed by Sofia Mohr and released in 2020, Águila grafts angled semi-serifs onto a geometric skeleton, drawing on Didone contrast to create tension between classical and contemporary forms. Nine weights from Thin to Heavy give it real range for editorial, packaging and branding work. The character set covers 400-plus glyphs with support for over 200 Latin-based languages.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describe Águila as a clean, modern typeface with a strong character, combining straight lines, curves and triangular shapes with Didone characteristics. It was built for editorial design, packaging, branding and broadcasting, and ships with over 400 characters supporting more than 200 Latin-based languages.

name: Árida
classification_notes: Calligraphic serif with broad-pen construction; flared serifs and strong stroke contrast that builds from soft at Regular to sharp and pointed at Black; relatively low x-height; design concept drawn from the visual character of cacti in Argentina's San Juan province
summary: A calligraphic display serif by Alfonso García for Latinotype, drawn from the pointed geometry of Argentine cacti and spanning five weights with small caps throughout.
description: Árida takes its cue from San Juan's semi-arid landscape: broad-pen construction gives the letterforms flared serifs and strong stroke contrast that shifts from soft and approachable at Regular to sharp and forceful at Black. All five weights carry small caps, multiple figure styles, ligatures and contextual alternates. Best placed at headline and poster sizes; the low x-height warrants sizing up slightly for continuous reading.
foundry_blurb: Latinotype describes Árida as sharp and aggressive at large sizes but friendly at a smaller scale, tracing that duality back to San Juan's cacti – plants that look hostile in silhouette but have always lived alongside the people of the region.
